evidence.quote: 16_evol_instruct

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Nearest catalog entries are star-bootstrapping and rest-em, but both evolve *solutions*: they sample the model's own answers to a fixed instruction set, filter by correctness/reward, and fine-tune on what survived — the instruction distribution never changes. Instruction Evolution changes the *input* distribution and does not require a correctness filter at all. Also distinct from dimensional-synthetic-eval-set, which deliberately rejects free-form LLM rewriting (it enumerates dimension tuples precisely because free-form generation mode-collapses) and targets evaluation inputs rather than training data; and from raft, which is about training a model to ignore retrieval distractors. No catalog entry covers evolving the instruction set itself; grep for 'evol', 'instruct', 'wizardlm', 'self-instruct' across patterns.json returns nothing on point. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: WizardLM: Empowering Large Pre-Trained Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions
evidence.quote: Starting with an initial set of instructions, we use our proposed Evol-Instruct to rewrite them step by step into more complex instructions. Then, we mix all generated instruction data to fine-tune LLaMA. We call the resulting model WizardLM. Human evaluations on a complexity-balanced test bed and Vicuna's testset show that instructions from Evol-Instruct are superior to human-created ones.

candidates.name: Degradation Test Gate
candidates.summary: Before adopting any cost or latency optimization that swaps the inference path — a smaller model, a quantized checkpoint, a distilled student, an aggressive cache — run the incumbent and the candidate over the same corpus and gate on per-example behavioural divergence (answer flips, KL distance, free-form generation quality), not on aggregate benchmark parity. Resolves the force that the cheap configuration is nearly always indistinguishable on a headline accuracy number while being visibly different to the users who hit the affected examples.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the books-and-talks seam: named chapter-level pattern #27 of 32 in the O'Reilly 2026 book 'Generative AI Design Patterns' (Lakshmanan & Hapke), placed in the chapter on addressing constraints immediately after Small Language Model, Prompt Caching and Inference Optimization — i.e. it is positioned as the acceptance gate for exactly those three cost moves. Original Japanese term: 「パターン27：デグレデーションテスト」 (gloss: 'Pattern 27: Degradation Testing'). Corroborated by the companion repository directory and by the compression-metrics literature.

evidence.title: 生成AIデザインパターン ―AIエージェント構築、アプリケーション開発のベストプラクティス (O'Reilly Japan)
evidence.quote: 8.4　パターン27：デグレデーションテスト

evidence.title: lakshmanok/generative-ai-design-patterns — companion code for the O'Reilly book
evidence.quote: 27_degradation_testing

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not shadow-canary: that runs a candidate agent version against live production traffic to cover distributions the offline set missed, and its framing is coverage, not metric choice; a degradation test is an offline acceptance gate for a deliberate cost substitution and its whole point is that the usual metric (accuracy parity) is the wrong instrument. Not eval-harness or eval-as-contract, which detect absolute regression against a held-out set and a pass threshold — accuracy-parity is exactly what those gates report as 'no regression' here. Not scaffold-ablation-on-model-upgrade, which points the other way (removing scaffolding after a model gets stronger). Not multi-model-routing or open-weight-cascade, which are routing topologies and presuppose that the quality delta of the cheap tier is already characterised — this pattern is how you characterise it. Not replay-divergence, an anti-pattern about replaying an event log through a changed model. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Accuracy is Not All You Need
evidence.quote: However, even when the accuracy of baseline and compressed model are similar, we observe the phenomenon of flips, wherein answers change from correct to incorrect and vice versa in some proportion. We conduct a detailed study of metrics across multiple compression techniques, models and datasets, demonstrating that the behavior of compressed models as visible to end-users is often significantly different from the baseline model, even when accuracy is similar.

candidates.name: Confirmation-Bound Action Lease
candidates.summary: Bind a human confirmation to a canonical description of the action it approved and hold that binding as durable, monotonic issuer-side state carrying a remaining execution budget, so that an agent's replanning, retry, sub-agent delegation or crash-recovery cannot silently re-consume the same approval under a freshly minted token. Resolves the force that agents legitimately re-derive the same action many times, and every re-derivation looks like a brand-new request to a stateless authorization check.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the 2026-conference-talk seam. The architectural frame — approval as a first-class, auditable boundary owned by the harness rather than a per-call check — is what QCon AI Boston 2026 put on stage (Vinoth Govindarajan, OpenAI, 2026-06-02), using OpenClaw as the case study. Honest caveat: the talk names the approval boundary and the audit path, it does not name the replay failure; the specific failure mode and its fix come from the CapLease paper, with independent corroboration in Agent libOS's prepare-dispatch-settle protocol. Two 2026 arXiv systems papers converging on durable issuer-side authorization state is what graduates this past 'one framework's gripe'.

evidence.title: The Agent Harness: Control Planes, Invariants, and Approval Boundaries for Production AI Agents — QCon AI Boston 2026
evidence.quote: Using OpenClaw as a concrete case study, this talk explains the systems that keep an agent sane: a control plane that owns sessions and state, the concurrency invariants that prevent overlapping runs from corrupting behavior, and the tool plus approval boundaries that determine when chat becomes action. I'll walk through how events enter the system, how state is rehydrated per session, why single-writer execution and throttling matter, and how auditable approval paths keep powerful tools useful without making them unsafe.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not missing-idempotency: that anti-pattern is about deduplicating *tool calls*, keyed on plan-step id plus arguments, and its own solution concedes that regenerated arguments are the hard case; here each re-request is a genuinely new, legitimately-issued, single-use token, so identifier-level dedup cannot fire at all — the durable state has to sit on the authorization instance, not the call. Not sync-execution-plan-confirmation, which secures the first confirmation before execution but says nothing about what happens when the agent replans afterwards. Not approval-queue (asynchronous review throughput). Not delegated-agent-authorization, which narrows *authority* down a delegation chain via scoped short-lived credentials — the point here is that correctly scoped, correctly short-lived, correctly single-use credentials still permit unbounded re-issuance of the same human consent. Not session-scoped-payment-authorization, which caps a monetary amount inside a session rather than the execution count of one confirmed action. Not deontic-token-delegation, which reifies obligations for accountability tracing, not consumption budgets.

evidence.title: Beyond Single-Use Tokens: Durable Authorization State for Replay-Resistant LLM Agent Actions
evidence.quote: Tool-using large language model agents frequently replan, retry failed operations, delegate tasks, and resume after crashes. These behaviors can cause one user authorization to be requested and executed multiple times under freshly issued token identifiers, even when each individual token is single-use. We call this failure semantic replay: exceeding the execution budget of a token-independent authorization instance rather than merely reusing an old token identifier.

evidence.title: Agent libOS: A Runtime Substrate for Capability-Controlled Self-Evolving LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Provider-backed effects use a prepare-dispatch-settle protocol that exposes ambiguity and prevents blind replay.

candidates.name: Schema Subset Linking
candidates.summary: Before the model writes any query, run a dedicated selection stage that retrieves a small candidate sub-schema (which databases, then which tables and columns) from a catalog far too large to fit in context, and generate only against that subset. The stage is tuned for recall rather than precision, because a wrongly-pruned column makes the question silently unanswerable while a few extra columns only cost tokens.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the data-engineering / cs.DB seam. Original term: 'schema linking' (also 'schema selection', 'schema pruning', 'sub-schema'). This is the single most-published module in the text-to-SQL literature and the catalog has no entry for it — table-augmented-generation covers the pipeline around it but not the selection stage. Corroborated across three independent groups (Stanford/Google CHESS 2024, HUST AutoLink 2025, LinkAlign 2025) plus Amazon Science's RASL and RSL-SQL in the same search; the framing is consistent across all of them (full schema does not fit; pruning must be recall-first).

evidence.title: CHESS: Contextual Harnessing for Efficient SQL Synthesis
evidence.quote: the Information Retriever (IR) extracts relevant data, the Schema Selector (SS) prunes large schemas, the Candidate Generator (CG) generates high-quality candidates and refines queries iteratively, and the Unit Tester (UT) validates queries through LLM-based natural language unit tests.

evidence.title: CHESS: Contextual Harnessing for Efficient SQL Synthesis (results)
evidence.quote: CHESS efficiently narrows down very large database schemas into manageable sub-schemas, boosting system accuracy by approximately 2% and reducing the number of LLM tokens by ×5.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not tool-loadout (that selects a subset of callable TOOLS from a registry; here the objects being selected are schema elements — tables, columns, databases — that are data, not actions). Not hierarchical-retrieval (a cascade over a document corpus scored by relevance; schema linking selects over a typed relational catalog and its correctness criterion is 'does the sub-schema contain everything the target query must reference', an all-or-nothing recall condition, not a ranked relevance list). Not table-augmented-generation, which is the surrounding synthesise-execute-generate pipeline and assumes the schema is already available to the model — this is the missing upstream stage that pipeline needs at enterprise scale. Not context-window-packing (a generic token-budget policy with no notion of a lost join key).

evidence.title: CHESS: Contextual Harnessing for Efficient SQL Synthesis
evidence.quote: Effective text-to-SQL synthesis can become very challenging due to (i) the extensive size of database catalogs (descriptions of tables and their columns) and database values, (ii) reasoning over large database schemas, (iii) ensuring the functional validity of the generated queries, and (iv) navigating the ambiguities of natural language questions.

evidence.title: AutoLink: Autonomous Schema Exploration and Expansion for Scalable Schema Linking in Text-to-SQL at Scale
evidence.quote: For industrial-scale text-to-SQL, supplying the entire database schema to Large Language Models (LLMs) is impractical due to context window limits and irrelevant noise.

evidence.title: LinkAlign: Scalable Schema Linking for Real-World Large-Scale Multi-Database Text-to-SQL
evidence.quote: Schema linking is a critical bottleneck in applying existing Text-to-SQL models to real-world, large-scale, multi-database environments. Through error analysis, we identify two major challenges in schema linking: (1) Database Retrieval: accurately selecting the target database from a large schema pool, while effectively filtering out irrelevant ones; and (2) Schema Item Grounding: precisely identifying the relevant tables and columns within complex and often redundant schemas for SQL generation.

candidates.name: Cumulative Disclosure Accounting
candidates.summary: Keep a running account of what a data agent has already disclosed within a session or task, and evaluate each new query against that accumulated history rather than in isolation, because a sequence of individually-permitted aggregate queries can jointly re-identify the rows the policy was written to protect. The gate is a session-scoped budget or join-composition check, not a per-call allow/deny.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the cs.DB / cs.CR data-agent seam. Original term: the 2026 data-agent security study names this vulnerability class 'Lack of Compositional Leakage Control' (V8, policy layer); the underlying database-privacy literature calls the same mechanism a 'composition attack' (Ganta et al., KDD 2008). Two independent lines converge: the classical DB-privacy result that independently-safe releases compose into a breach, and the 2026 finding that current data agents evaluate policy one tool call at a time. The differential-privacy tradition already answers this with a cumulative privacy budget spent across a query session, which supplies the concrete mechanism.

evidence.title: Data Agents Under Attack: Vulnerabilities in LLM-Driven Analytical Systems (abstract)
evidence.quote: Data agents integrate LLM-driven reasoning with relational data access, executable analytical tools, and multi-step workflow orchestration, making them increasingly central to enterprise analytics. This integration introduces new security vulnerabilities across data resources, database execution, and agent reasoning, recombining concerns from database security and general-purpose LLM-agent security into failure modes that neither line of work captures on its own.

evidence.title: Composition Attacks and Auxiliary Information in Data Privacy
evidence.quote: One of the most significant is the auxiliary information (also called external knowledge, background knowledge, or side information) that an adversary gleans from other channels such as the web, public records, or domain knowledge.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not pii-redaction, which filters identifiers out of a single input or output; here every individual result is already clean and the leak only exists in the join across results. Not rate-limiting (caps request/token volume in a time window; says nothing about what was disclosed). Not lethal-trifecta-threat-model (blocks an exfiltration path built from three capabilities in one execution; this is about legitimate, authorised reads accumulating into an unauthorised inference). Not context-minimization (shrinks untrusted input reaching the model; this constrains authorised output leaving it). Nothing in the catalog carries state across queries for a privacy decision.

evidence.title: Composition Attacks and Auxiliary Information in Data Privacy
evidence.quote: Specifically, we investigate the effectiveness of current anonymization schemes in preserving privacy when multiple organizations independently release anonymized data about overlapping populations. 1. We investigate composition attacks, in which an adversary uses independent anonymized releases to breach privacy.

evidence.title: Data Agents Under Attack: Vulnerabilities in LLM-Driven Analytical Systems
evidence.quote: The policies Π may approve each query in isolation. Yet they check one tool invocation at a time and never track cumulative disclosure across the session.

evidence.title: Agents That Know Too Much: A Data-Centric Survey of Privacy in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Sensitive information can therefore leak not only through its final answer but through the queries it issues, the intermediate results it handles, the memory it writes, and the messages it exchanges with other agents.

candidates.name: Schema-Evolution Query Sentinel
candidates.summary: Bind every saved or cached agent-generated query to a fingerprint of the exact schema objects it reads, re-check that fingerprint against the live catalog before each re-execution, and on a mismatch fail loudly or re-derive the query rather than returning a number computed under changed semantics. The force it resolves: schemas in production change constantly, and a query that still parses after a table split or column rename returns a plausible wrong answer with no error.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the VLDB / cs.DB seam. Original terms: 'schema evolution' (PRISM, VLDB 2008), 'schema evolution robustness' (EvoSchema, PVLDB 18(10)); the industry name for the artefact side is 'data contract'. Two decades apart and independent: PRISM quantifies how fast real schemas move (Wikipedia, 170+ documented schema versions in 4.5 years) and shows legacy queries must be rewritten to survive; EvoSchema shows that in the LLM era the same evolution silently degrades the model's table-selection, with table-level changes hurting far more than column-level ones. The failure is quiet in both eras, which is what makes a re-check sentinel the pattern rather than better prompting.

evidence.title: Graceful Database Schema Evolution: the PRISM Workbench (abstract)
evidence.quote: Wikipedia and its 170+ schema versions provided an invaluable testbed for validating PRISM tools and their ability to support legacy queries.

evidence.title: EvoSchema: Towards Text-to-SQL Robustness against Schema Evolution (findings)
evidence.quote: revealing that table-level perturbations have a significantly greater impact on model performance compared to column-level changes

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not schema-extensibility, which is advice to the schema author on designing for forward compatibility (reserved fields, namespaced extensions); this is a runtime guard on the consumer side, for a schema you do not own and cannot make compatible. Not behavior-pinning-test-before-agent-edit (golden tests pinned before an agent edits code — the change agent is the agent itself and the artefact is source); here the change comes from a separate upstream team and the artefact is a live catalog. Not eval-as-contract (a release gate over an eval suite). Not lineage-tracking, which records which sources produced an output but never re-verifies them at read time.

evidence.title: EvoSchema: Towards Text-to-SQL Robustness against Schema Evolution
evidence.quote: Neural text-to-SQL models, which translate natural language questions (NLQs) into SQL queries given a database schema, have achieved remarkable performance. However, database schemas frequently evolve to meet new requirements. Such schema evolution often leads to performance degradation for models trained on static schemas.

evidence.title: Graceful Database Schema Evolution: the PRISM Workbench
evidence.quote: practitioners and researchers are well aware that schema modifications can: (i) dramatically impact both data and queries [8], endangering the data integrity, (ii) require expensive application maintenance for queries, and (iii) cause unacceptable system downtimes.

candidates.name: Fleet-Level Irreversibility Budget
candidates.summary: Treat a scarce, non-recoverable quantity (residual value-at-risk, spend, irreversible effects) as a first-class cumulative account that a trusted runtime maintains per principal across every agent, workflow and tenant, charging each effect its residual loss and denying the marginal effect once the aggregate would overdraw. Resolves the composition fallacy in which every per-action gate is individually correct while the fleet as a whole overdraws its principal's limit.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (compute/risk as a scarce resource the agent must reason about). Corroborated across two independent 2026 arXiv papers: one theoretical/experimental (48x fleet overdraw under correct per-effect gates), one empirical (63 confirmed production budget-overrun incidents across 21 orchestration frameworks 2023-2026, with a delegation-fanout race documented in 11 of them).

evidence.title: The Irreversibility Budget: Fleet-Level Risk Accounting and Admission Control for Agent Operating Systems
evidence.quote: We perform a controlled study in which per-effect gates admit fleet-level overdraws of up to 48 times the tenant's risk limit while the budget holds every correctly charged run within that limit. Conservative, dependency-aware pricing remains the central open problem for a deployable design.

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents
evidence.quote: the distinguishing value is non-bypassability under operator error in multi-agent delegation: the delegation-fanout race documented in 11 incidents is rejected by the borrow checker at compile time, while the same pattern under asyncio overshoots 30/30 and three disciplined alternatives overshoot 0/30.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not step-budget (caps loop iterations inside one request), not cost-gating (per-action expected-cost threshold requiring acknowledgement), not rate-limiting (per-user request/token quota in a time window), not reversibility-aware-action-filter (per-action reversibility estimate that re-samples the policy), not token-economy-blindness (the anti-pattern of having no per-run budget at all), not cost-observability (dashboards, no admission control). All of those are per-action or per-run. The novel force here is cross-agent aggregation: the cited controlled study shows per-effect gates admitting fleet-level overdraws of up to 48x the tenant limit while every local gate stays correct, so the pattern is the shared priced account plus admission control on the marginal effect, not a tighter local gate.

evidence.title: The Irreversibility Budget: Fleet-Level Risk Accounting and Admission Control for Agent Operating Systems
evidence.quote: Current controls check one effect at a time, so a fleet of individually authorized agents can overdraw its principal's risk under a shared trigger while every local gate stays correct. We propose the irreversibility budget, a cumulative account of residual value-at-risk that a trusted runtime maintains for each principal across agents, workflows, and tenants.

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents, with an Affine-Typed Rust Mitigation as a Case Study
evidence.quote: LLM-agent budget overruns are a documented production failure class: a single retry loop can spend thousands of dollars before an operator notices, and the in-process integrity properties that would prevent it (no aliasing, no double-spend, no use-after-delegation of a cost-bearing value) are enforced, if at all, by ad-hoc wrappers rather than by the type system.

candidates.name: Value-of-Information Gate
candidates.summary: Before paying for any information-acquiring step — executing a proposed tool call, admitting one more tool into context, retrieving, or asking the user a clarifying question — estimate the expected improvement in the downstream decision and compare it against that step's own heterogeneous cost, acting only when the margin is positive. Resolves the force that relevance ranking or an uncertainty score tells you the ordering but never tells you how much is worth buying.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (an agent that must price information before acquiring it — classical value-of-information). Three independent 2026 groups converge on the same shape across three different acquisition surfaces: tool-set admission (CAM-DF), per-call tool execution (ToolGate), and user clarification (Information Gain Reward). The theoretical claim that ranking scores alone are insufficient is proved, not just asserted.

evidence.title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: We prove this objective is Bayes-aligned with the stopping target and that score-only rules are suboptimal under heterogeneous costs.

evidence.title: ToolGate: Token-Efficient Pre-Call Control for Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Agents
evidence.quote: These results show that tool-augmented VLM agents benefit not only from better perceptual tools, but also from explicit control over when tool outputs are worth paying for.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not over-search-and-under-search, which is the anti-pattern naming miscalibrated retrieval frequency without prescribing a decision rule. Not disambiguation (ask a clarifying question when the request is ambiguous) — that has no cost side and no expected-gain arithmetic; here the question is asked only when the Bayesian belief update it induces outweighs the extra interaction step. Not conformal-prediction-help-gate/KnowNo, which triggers on a calibrated set failing to be a singleton (an uncertainty threshold), not on a value-minus-cost comparison. Not cost-gating (cost threshold only, no value term). Not adaptive-compute-allocation (internal thinking budget by input difficulty, not external information acquisition). Not tool-search-lazy-loading (a loading mechanism, not a stopping rule).

evidence.title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: acquiring too few tools leaves the task under-informed, while too many adds cost, context load, and privacy exposure. Routers and retrievers can rank candidate tools by relevance, but a ranking alone does not determine how many are worth selecting. Existing approaches leave acquisition under heterogeneous costs unaddressed.

evidence.title: ToolGate: Token-Efficient Pre-Call Control for Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Agents
evidence.quote: we find that the baseline agent exhibits poor local selectivity: helpful and harmful calls occur at similar rates (11.8% vs. 9.9%), while most calls do not change the immediate forced-answer prediction.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-Aware Clarification in LLM Agents with Information Gain
evidence.quote: Central to our approach is the Information Gain Reward, a metric that quantifies the utility of clarification questions by measuring the Bayesian belief update towards the ground-truth goal induced by the clarification exchange.

candidates.name: Outcome-Contingent Agent Contract
candidates.summary: When a principal delegates work to an agent whose model tier and effort level it cannot observe, pay or reward that agent as a declared share of the verified outcome rather than per token or per call, so the agent's hidden two-dimensional choice of technology and effort is self-selecting. Resolves the moral-hazard force that per-token payment rewards spend while per-task flat payment rewards the cheapest model that still passes.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (outcome-contingent payment shaping what an agent optimises). Grounded in contract theory applied directly to LLM delegation, with the model calibrated on open-weight LLM pairings over MATH and MMLU-Pro; the companion position paper argues that supervisor/sub-agent architectures are structurally principal-agent problems and that scheming vocabulary maps onto known mechanism-design concepts.

evidence.title: Contracting for LLM Delegation: Moral Hazard in Technology and Effort Choice
evidence.quote: This framework is increasingly critical in the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), where Agents choose both a model and an associated effort level (e.g., token budget).

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Systems Should be Treated as Principal-Agent Problems
evidence.quote: This leads to agency loss: a gap between the principal's intended outcome and the realized system behavior.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not vickrey-auction-allocation, which is a one-shot allocation mechanism whose payment is fixed at the second-lowest bid before any work happens and conditions on the bid, never on the realised outcome. Not contract-net-protocol, which awards by bid and is silent about how the contractor is compensated for quality. Not eval-as-contract, which is a release gate on a suite, with no payment or reward term and no hidden-action model. Not progressive-delegation or trust-and-reputation-routing, which change how much autonomy or traffic an agent gets by track record; here the lever is the shape of the reward function itself, and the cited result is that a threshold reward share is exactly what flips the agent between model tiers.

evidence.title: Contracting for LLM Delegation: Moral Hazard in Technology and Effort Choice
evidence.quote: We derive the optimal linear contract for the Principal, demonstrating that the Agent's best response is characterized by a threshold reward share that triggers technology switching.

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Systems Should be Treated as Principal-Agent Problems
evidence.quote: A core property of such systems is information asymmetry: agents observe task-specific information, produce intermediate reasoning traces, and operate with different context windows. In isolation, such asymmetry is not problematic, since agents report truthfully to the principal when incentives are fully aligned. However, this assumption breaks down when incentives diverge.

candidates.name: Reservation-Value Gate for Delegated Negotiation
candidates.summary: Before a delegated agent may commit to any deal, bid, or price it negotiated, require it to clear a deterministic verifier that recomputes the deal against the principal's declared reservation value and discount rate, refusing agreements that fail the individual-rationality check. Resolves the force that an agent under closing pressure will accept money-losing terms, and that a mechanism's incentive-compatibility guarantee does not transfer to an LLM playing it.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (agent-to-agent negotiation and contracting). Two independent 2026 studies: a 9,840-negotiation supply-chain bargaining study benchmarked against a validated Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium, and a mechanism-design framework layered over A2A/MCP. Both conclude the same thing from different angles — the protocol layer carries transport and discovery, not strategic correctness, so the participation constraint has to be verified deterministically outside the model. A second force the first paper isolates: the principal's economic patience and the agent's prompted patience are different variables, and leaving the second implicit hands away most of the surplus.

evidence.title: When LLM Agents Negotiate: Private Information and Dynamic Bargaining in Supply Chains
evidence.quote: Delegation separates the principal's economic patience from the agent's prompted strategic patience, a free deployment choice that is the single strongest driver of surplus division (90% of explained variance).

evidence.title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
evidence.quote: However, these protocols specify transport and discovery rather than strategic correctness and do not guarantee efficient, individually rational, or strategy-proof outcomes.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not cost-gating, which trips on a cost threshold and asks a human to acknowledge — a deal can be cheap and still below reservation, or expensive and excellent. Not velocity-magnitude-governor, which caps financial magnitude per unit time and says nothing about whether any single deal is worth taking. Not session-scoped-payment-authorization or verifiable-purchase-mandate, which bound and attest spending authority rather than economic rationality. It is also the explicit corrective to vickrey-auction-allocation, whose current framing assumes that making truthful reporting a dominant strategy produces truthful reports: the cited evaluation finds one model bidding its exact valuation in only 3.3 percent of trials under a strategy-proof mechanism.

evidence.title: When LLM Agents Negotiate: Private Information and Dynamic Bargaining in Supply Chains
evidence.quote: Capability also governs reliability: baseline models accept individually irrational contracts in 19.2% of cases, versus 0.0-0.6% at mid-tier and flagship, making automated profit verification the binding guardrail below that threshold.

evidence.title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
evidence.quote: In auction experiments (N=30 per model), both models achieve 100 percent efficient allocation but differ sharply in truthful bidding: one bids its exact valuation in every trial, whereas the other does so in only 3.3 percent of trials. Thus, mechanism-level incentive compatibility does not automatically transfer to LLM-agent behavior.

candidates.name: Sanction-Backed Agent Institution
candidates.summary: Govern a population of competing agents with a public, immutable manifest of legal states, transitions, sanctions and restorative paths that a runtime interprets, attaching graded and escalating consequences to detected violations while keeping a per-agent reliability estimate and an append-only log. Resolves the force that a written prohibition inside the prompt does not bind an agent under optimisation pressure, and that a naive one-shot penalty is itself gamed by the agents it governs.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (incentive and mechanism design for LLM agents), following the brief's instruction to go past emergent-agent-collusion. Two independent 2026 results, one measuring collusion tiers in a Cournot market across six model configurations at N=90 runs per condition, one across three simulated environments and varied agent populations. Both isolate the same design ingredients: enforceable graded consequence plus a persistent per-agent reliability estimate, and both find the naive alternative (declarative prohibition, or a simple flat penalty) fails.

evidence.title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
evidence.quote: The prompt-only Constitutional baseline yields no reliable improvement, illustrating that declarative prohibitions do not bind under optimisation pressure.

evidence.title: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
evidence.quote: Our results position norm enforcement mechanisms as scalable levers for shaping agents' behavior, but only when designed to anticipate becoming part of the system they govern.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not constitutional-charter — that is precisely the prompt-only baseline the cited experiment tests and finds ineffective (no reliable improvement over ungoverned). Not policy-as-code-gate, which is a pre-dispatch per-action allow/deny with no graded consequence, no reliability history, and no restorative path; the institution acts ex post on evidence of a multi-agent equilibrium that no single action reveals. Not deontic-token-delegation, which passes obligations along a delegation chain but has no detection-and-penalty loop. Not provenance-ledger, which records without consequence. It is the remedy counterpart to the existing emergent-agent-collusion anti-pattern, and the cited work is explicit that the enforcement mechanism must be designed anticipating that it becomes part of the system it governs.

evidence.title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
evidence.quote: Central to this approach is the governance graph, a public, immutable manifest that declares legal states, transitions, sanctions, and restorative paths; an Oracle/Controller runtime interprets this manifest, attaching enforceable consequences to evidence of coordination while recording a cryptographically keyed, append-only governance log for audit and provenance.

evidence.title: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
evidence.quote: We find that simple enforcement mechanisms are exploited by misaligned agents for competitive advantage, even when they are not explicitly trained or prompted to do so. We thus turn our attention to designing more robust mechanisms, and identify two key ingredients: estimating each agent's reliability over time, and updating this estimate with escalating penalties for repeated misbehavior.

candidates.name: Reactive Repricing Spiral
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: let pricing or bidding agents reprice continuously off each other's freshly observed prices, with no damping, no observation lag, no unit-cost floor and no volatility trip, so responsiveness compounds with feedback until prices oscillate and undercut below cost. Resolves nothing on its own; the force it names is that faster adaptation improves local information processing while simultaneously amplifying endogenous instability.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-economics seam (market-stability safeguards when many agents price against each other). Empirical anchor is the Agent Bazaar multi-agent simulation, which finds that frontier and open-weight models largely fail to self-regulate in the B2C crash scenario and that failure severity tracks the model rather than its size; the theoretical anchor supplies the mechanism (responsiveness x feedback intensity as the joint stability condition), which is what makes the mitigations — damping, observation lag, unit-cost floor, volatility trip — derivable rather than ad hoc.

evidence.title: Agent Bazaar: Enabling Economic Alignment in Multi-Agent Marketplaces
evidence.quote: We evaluate frontier and open-weight models across both scenarios and find that models largely fail to self-regulate, with failure severity varying by model rather than by size. We propose economically aligned harnesses, Stabilizing Firms and Skeptical Guardians, that improve outcomes but remain fragile under harder market conditions.

evidence.title: A theory of algorithmic markets (Frontiers in Complex Systems)
evidence.quote: Faster responsiveness may improve information processing and adjustment while simultaneously amplifying endogenous instability.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not emergent-agent-collusion, which is the opposite direction of failure — independent agents converging on supra-competitive prices upward under repeated interaction. Here the equilibrium is not reached at all: the loop is unstable and terminates in below-cost pricing and market collapse. Not agent-bullwhip-effect, where order-quantity variance is amplified along a serial supply chain by downstream-to-upstream replenishment policies; here the amplification is horizontal, between competitors observing one another's prices, and the amplified variable is price, not order quantity. Not circuit-breaker, which trips on a failing dependency's error rate, not on the agent's own contribution to a market's volatility.

evidence.title: Agent Bazaar: Enabling Economic Alignment in Multi-Agent Marketplaces
evidence.quote: We identify two failure modes: (1) Algorithmic Instability in a B2C market ("The Crash"), where firms amplify price volatility until the market collapses, and (2) Sybil Deception in a C2C market ("The Lemon Market"), where a single deceptive agent controlling multiple coordinated seller identities floods the market with fraudulent listings, eroding trust and consumer welfare.

evidence.title: A theory of algorithmic markets
evidence.quote: The analysis shows that market stability depends jointly on learning responsiveness and feedback intensity. When adaptive updating is sufficiently regular and feedback effects remain weak, the system converges toward stable equilibrium-like behavior, nesting standard equilibrium models as limiting benchmark cases. As learning responsiveness and endogenous feedback increase jointly, however, the adaptive process may generate persistent fluctuations, endogenous volatility, oscillatory dynamics, and local instability.

candidates.name: Search-Sealed Eval Set
candidates.summary: Seal the evaluation set outside the agent's own retrieval reach for the duration of the run — block the dataset-hosting domains at the egress proxy, record the full search trajectory, and void any run whose trace touched a mirror of the benchmark instead of scoring it. Resolves the force between wanting a realistic tool-using agent (which must be allowed to search) and wanting a score that measures reasoning rather than the agent's ability to find its own answer key.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam (English, arXiv cs.CL/cs.LG). Three independent 2025-2026 papers describe the same shape and the same mitigation stack (egress blocking, trajectory recording, run invalidation). Han et al. measure the effect directly: blocking one host moves the contaminated subset by ~15 accuracy points.

evidence.title: Search-Time Data Contamination
evidence.quote: After HuggingFace is blocked, we observe a drop in accuracy on the contaminated subset of approximately 15%.

evidence.title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation
evidence.quote: Holding out a private test set closes the first alone.

evidence.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
evidence.quote: we use LLM-aided log inspection to uncover previously unreported behaviors, such as searching for the benchmark on HuggingFace instead of solving a task, or misusing credit cards in flight booking tasks.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. eval-harness holds a dataset out of *training/tuning* to detect regressions between agent versions, and says nothing about the agent fetching that dataset at inference time through its own tools; the leak here happens at test time, inside the run, and is invisible to a held-out-split discipline. dimensional-synthetic-eval-set is about how eval *inputs are generated* (avoiding mode collapse), not about reachability of the answer key. over-search-and-under-search is a retrieval-frequency miscalibration in the task itself. retrieval-saturation-tool-attack is an adversary flooding the agent's context, not the agent finding the grading key. sampled-prompt-trace-eval samples production traces for judging; it does not gate on what the trace retrieved.

evidence.title: Search-Time Data Contamination
evidence.quote: STC occurs when the retrieval step surfaces a source containing the test question (or a near-duplicate) alongside its answer, enabling agents to copy rather than genuinely infer or reason, undermining benchmark integrity.

evidence.title: Search-Time Contamination in Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation in Public Benchmark Evaluation
evidence.quote: We therefore advocate contamination-aware practices, including isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.

candidates.name: Text-Independent Completion Oracle
candidates.summary: Decide whether a task succeeded by programmatically diffing the environment or system-of-record state against a declarative spec, and treat both the agent's own completion claim and any judge's reading of the transcript as inadmissible evidence of success. Resolves the force between the cheapness of asking the agent (or an LLM judge) whether the job is done and the measured fact that confident closing language is uncorrelated with actual state change.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. Advani (2026) quantifies the base rate of the failure the pattern forbids: 45-48% of tau2-bench failures and 75.8% of self-assessing AppWorld coding trajectories are false successes. Cao et al. (2026) independently show that outcome-only grading passes procedurally corrupt runs at 27-78%.

evidence.title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: LLM agents can fail silently by asserting task completion when the environment state shows otherwise.

evidence.title: Beyond Task Completion: Revealing Corrupt Success in LLM Agents through Procedure-Aware Evaluation
evidence.quote: At the procedural compliance level, 27-78% of benchmark reported successes are corrupt successes concealing violations across interaction and integrity.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. agent-as-judge evaluates the trajectory with another *agent* — which is exactly the configuration Advani (2026) measures and finds capped at AUROC 0.65 for detecting false success, because judges latch onto confident closing language and action-count volume. blind-grader-with-isolated-context still uses an LLM grader, just with a clean context and the artifact; it cannot see state the artifact does not describe. deception-manipulation is the agent falsifying its *action history* to defeat oversight; here the agent is sincere and merely wrong, and the pathology is on the harness side for accepting the claim as the metric. context-anxiety explains one *cause* of premature closing (token-budget misjudgement) but is not a measurement discipline. behavior-pinning-test-before-agent-edit pins pre-existing behaviour before an edit; this pins the post-condition of the task.

evidence.title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Judges rely on surface completion proxies -- confident closing language in tau2-bench and coarse action-sequence volume in AppWorld -- rather than verified state changes.

evidence.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
evidence.quote: For example, SWE-bench Verified uses insufficient test cases, while TAU-bench counts empty responses as successful. Such issues can lead to under- or overestimation of agents' performance by up to 100% in relative terms.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the arxiv-listing scout. Adds a second, cheaper oracle channel to the claimed pattern: besides diffing environment state against a declarative spec, the agent's own dispatch record (which tools were actually invoked) is a text-independent completion signal. Reports no false flags on 207 clean fidelity-passing extractions across three model families while recovering all 50 planted faults, and documents the concrete production trigger — a structured-output constraint that silently disabled tool use while the model answered anyway.

evidence.title: Fidelity Is Not Enough: Dispatch-Level Instrumentation for Agentic Datasheet Extraction
evidence.quote: Fidelity -- whether an extracted value matches the source -- is the standard measure for agentic document extraction, and it scores that run a success. We therefore log every tool call in an agentic benchmark of 25 hand-curated claims over three components, with 12 more on a fourth, 37 in all. From that dispatch record we build two instruments: a rule-based failure-attribution classifier, and a silent-failure detector whose two rules check only which tools were called, never the extracted value.

candidates.name: Accuracy-Cost Pareto Eval
candidates.summary: Report agent quality as a frontier over accuracy and the dollars, tokens or wall-clock spent per task, and select a configuration off that frontier, rather than ranking candidates on accuracy alone. Resolves the force between the accuracy leaderboard's pull toward ever-heavier scaffolds and the deployment reality that an agent's cost per task is a hard constraint, not a footnote.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. Kapoor et al. (2024) is the argumentative anchor; an arXiv sweep for abs:"cost" AND abs:"Pareto" AND abs:"agent" AND abs:"benchmark" returned 13+ distinct 2025-2026 benchmarks and agent systems independently reporting a cost-accuracy Pareto frontier (AgentCARD, GA4GC, syftr, EvoRoute, MedicalAgentsBench, GeoNatureAgent, Surfer-H), which is the cross-product/cross-year recurrence test. Stroebl et al. supply the mechanism for why buying accuracy with compute saturates.

evidence.title: The Limits of Inference Scaling Through Resampling
evidence.quote: However, we show that this approach is fundamentally limited when verifiers are imperfect and have a non-zero probability of producing false positives. Resampling cannot decrease this probability, so it imposes an upper bound to the accuracy of resampling-based inference scaling, regardless of compute budget.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. cost-observability tracks spend telemetry in production; it does not make cost an axis of the pre-deploy score. cost-gating refuses or downgrades work at runtime against a budget. adaptive-compute-allocation and complexity-based-routing are inference-time spend policies. token-economy-blindness is the anti-pattern of ignoring unit economics in operations. None of these changes what the evaluation *reports* — the shape here is that the eval emits a frontier, so a cheaper agent that is statistically indistinguishable on accuracy is a legitimate and visible winner.

evidence.title: AI Agents That Matter
evidence.quote: First, there is a narrow focus on accuracy without attention to other metrics. As a result, SOTA agents are needlessly complex and costly, and the community has reached mistaken conclusions about the sources of accuracy gains. Our focus on cost in addition to accuracy motivates the new goal of jointly optimizing the two metrics.

evidence.title: Specialize Roles, Mix Deployments: Pushing the Cost-Accuracy Frontier of LLM Agent Teams
evidence.quote: In these systems, cost and accuracy are no longer properties of a single model: they depend on which model fills each role and where it is hosted, including API, self-hosted, and hybrid deployment. Existing agentic benchmarks typically evaluate fixed models or fixed agent configurations, and therefore offer limited guidance for cost-accuracy-optimal deployment.

candidates.name: Powered Eval Set
candidates.summary: Size the eval set from a power calculation for the smallest difference worth acting on, report an uncertainty interval with every score, and refuse to act on a gap the set cannot resolve. Resolves the force between the cheapness of a 50-task eval and the fact that agent evals are noisy experiments whose per-task variance routinely exceeds the version-to-version deltas teams ship on.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. Miller (2024) supplies the planning formulas; Bowyer et al. (2025) show the default CLT interval is actively wrong at the set sizes agent teams use; Chandrahas (2026) shows the consequence on a real leaderboard.

evidence.title: evalci: A Python Library for Statistically Rigorous Comparison of Language Model Evaluations
evidence.quote: 3 of the 8 adjacent leaderboard-rank gaps are not statistically significant after correcting for the 36 pairwise comparisons the ranking implies

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. eval-harness runs a held-out set against agent versions to detect regressions, but is silent on how many tasks that takes and on whether an observed delta is distinguishable from sampling noise — which is precisely the failure. bayesian-bandit-experimentation reallocates *live traffic* between variants; this is offline experiment design. shadow-canary is a comparison mechanism, not a statistical one. dual-evaluation-offline-online splits eval into two tracks without addressing the power of either. confident-inconsistency is the anti-pattern of unmeasured run-to-run non-determinism in production output; this is the discipline of quantifying eval-set sampling error.

evidence.title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
evidence.quote: Fundamentally, evaluations are experiments; but the literature on evaluations has largely ignored the literature from other sciences on experiment analysis and planning.

evidence.title: Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints
evidence.quote: In these small-data settings, we demonstrate that CLT-based methods perform very poorly, usually dramatically underestimating uncertainty (i.e. producing error bars that are too small).

candidates.name: Checklist Partial-Credit Scoring
candidates.summary: Decompose each long-horizon task into task-specific graded checkpoints and score progress against that checklist, so improvements and regressions that leave the binary pass/fail unchanged still register. Resolves the force between the auditability of a single official verifier (one bit per task, cheap and unarguable) and the sparse, low-power signal that one bit gives on tasks where most runs fail somewhere in the middle.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. The forces are quantified: on 879 matched pairs whose binary outcome is unchanged, partial credit shows 20.9% improving and 18.7% regressing — signal a pass@1 harness discards entirely. An arXiv sweep for abs:"partial credit" AND abs:"agent" returned independent instances across CTF (DeepRed), terminal (LH-Terminal-Bench, ClawForge), computer-use (PPT-Eval) and finance (BigFinanceBench), i.e. the shape recurs across domains and years, not in one harness.

evidence.title: Grounded Checklist Partial Credit for Agent Skill Trajectories
evidence.quote: Applied to 1,946 matched with/without-skill pairs, GCPC exposes the effects hidden by pass@1: among 879 pairs whose binary outcome does not change, 20.9% improve by more than 0.10 while 18.7% regress by the same margin.

evidence.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench
evidence.quote: This design enables dense intermediate rewards and partial credit, allowing evaluation to capture not only whether an agent reaches the final goal, but also how far it progresses on open-ended workflows.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. process-reward-model trains a step-level verifier to steer inference-time search or RL; the artifact is a learned reward model inside the agent loop, not a scoring rule for an eval report. artifact-evaluation scores intermediate artifacts to *localize* which pipeline node failed; it does not produce a graded task-progress score comparable across agent versions. agent-as-judge is holistic trajectory judgement — Qin et al. measure checklist partial credit against exactly that baseline and beat it (AUC 0.689 vs 0.619). multi-axis-promotion-scoring is a memory-promotion gate, unrelated.

evidence.title: Grounded Checklist Partial Credit for Agent Skill Trajectories
evidence.quote: This binary score hides partial progress and is particularly limited for procedural agent skill evaluations, since a skill can alter execution without changing the final outcome.

evidence.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading
evidence.quote: This setup overlooks intermediate progress and partial solutions, yielding sparse reward signals and an incomplete picture of agent capability.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the arxiv-listing scout. Independent 2026-08-29 controlled study (deterministic support-desk environment, scripted oracle, fault injector, 400 trajectories) that quantifies the exact trade-off the claimed pattern resolves: step-level graded checkpoints buy silent-fault recall at ~3x cost. It also adds a liability the candidate should carry — self-consistency 'triples cost while improving nothing', and an invented promise appended to an otherwise perfect trajectory evades even the step judge 82% of the time, so the checklist must include a claim-versus-trace check.

evidence.title: trajectory-judge: What Outcome-Only LLM Judges Miss on Agent Trajectories
evidence.quote: The outcome-only judge catches 84% of loud faults but 45% of silent ones while flagging 33% of correct trajectories; a step-rubric judge reaches 77% silent recall with zero false alarms at 3x the cost.

candidates.name: Chance-Corrected Judge Validation
candidates.summary: Before an LLM judge's scores are allowed to gate anything, measure the judge against human labels on a held-out meta-eval set using a chance-corrected agreement statistic, publish that number beside every score the judge produces, and re-measure whenever the judge model, its rubric or the task distribution changes. Resolves the force between the scalability of automated judging and the fact that raw exact-match agreement flatters a judge enough to reorder a leaderboard.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. Norman et al. quantify the consequence of skipping the chance correction across 21 judges and ~541,000 judgements; Pisupati et al. build the human-labelled meta-eval artifact the pattern requires for agentic trajectories, with reliable inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha 0.78) and a best judge at only ~65% on reasoning.

evidence.title: Reliability without Validity
evidence.quote: kappa deflation between exact match and Cohen's kappa is universal (33--41 pp on MT-Bench), judge rankings shift by up to 14 positions across benchmarks

evidence.title: Counsel: A Meta-Evaluation Dataset for Agentic Tasks
evidence.quote: Human annotators label critiques on each flagged error as "spot on", "correct location but poor reasoning", or "should not have flagged", achieving reliable inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha of 0.78).

evidence.title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: LLM judges fail reliably: no configuration across 5 judges, 5 prompt strategies, and full task specifications exceeds AUROC 0.65 on tau2-bench, and the same judges reach only 0.54 AUROC on AppWorld API-call traces.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. llm-as-judge introduces the judge but says nothing about whether the judge has been validated. frozen-rubric-reflection fixes the criteria the reviewer may use. blind-grader-with-isolated-context controls what the grader can see. same-model-self-critique and cross-reflection concern generator/critic *independence*, not the judge's measured agreement with humans. scorer-live-monitoring runs scorers in production. The un-catalogued shape is the meta-evaluation loop itself: a labelled human meta-eval set is a first-class, versioned artifact and the judge's chance-corrected agreement on it is the judge's licence to gate.

evidence.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
evidence.quote: LLM-as-a-Judge has become the dominant evaluation paradigm for language models, but judge validation in practice relies on exact-match agreement, a metric that does not correct for chance and systematically overstates discriminative ability.

evidence.title: Counsel: A Meta-Evaluation Dataset for Agentic Tasks
evidence.quote: This has driven widespread reliance on automated approaches such as LLM-as-a-judge (LLMJ) to critique agents at the process and outcome-levels at scale, however, the soundness of LLMJ critiques often goes unmeasured.

candidates.name: Score Validity Envelope
candidates.summary: Record every eval score together with the envelope that makes it interpretable — model snapshot, harness version, elicitation budget, sampled population, contamination status — and treat the score as expired, not merely stale, when any element of that envelope changes. Resolves the force between wanting a stable number to trend and cite and the fact that the number is a joint property of five things, four of which move without notice.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the eval/QA seam. Angulo et al. give the envelope explicitly, plus the expiry semantics for one of its fields ('it is a property of one run, it must be recorded with the reported score rather than with the benchmark release') and the measured disclosure gap: elicitation budgets appear in 13% of documents. Chen et al. show the model-snapshot field moves under a fixed model name; Biderman et al. show the harness field moves and breaks comparability.

evidence.title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation
evidence.quote: Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types.

evidence.title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models
evidence.quote: Researchers and engineers face methodological issues such as the sensitivity of models to evaluation setup, difficulty of proper comparisons across methods, and the lack of reproducibility and transparency.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. lineage-tracking records prompt/model/data provenance for each production *output*; it is provenance for artefacts, not a validity lifetime for measurements, and it carries no expiry rule and no elicitation-budget field. scaffold-ablation-on-model-upgrade re-examines whether harness components are still needed after an upgrade; it does not invalidate the prior score. eval-as-contract gates release on passing the suite but is silent on when a pass stops counting. determinism-tier-replay-gate classifies reproducibility of the agent's own decisions across identical inputs, not comparability of scores across model versions. The load-bearing new element is the invalidation rule: a score outside its envelope is not a weaker score, it is not a score.

evidence.title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation
evidence.quote: A benchmark score is a joint property of the model, the evaluation harness, the elicitation budget, the sampled population, and contamination status. Leaderboards publish the model and the score, so capability and leakage stay observationally equivalent.

evidence.title: How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time?
evidence.quote: Overall, our findings show that the behavior of the "same" LLM service can change substantially in a relatively short amount of time, highlighting the need for continuous monitoring of LLMs.

candidates.name: Cognitive Forcing Function
candidates.summary: Deliberately withhold the agent's recommendation until the reviewing human has committed an independent judgement (or has explicitly asked to see it), inserting a designed friction step at decision time. It resolves the force that a human reviewer under time pressure develops a blanket 'follow the agent' heuristic rather than evaluating each recommendation, and it buys that engagement at a known cost in perceived usability.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the HCI/CSCW seam (ACM CSCW 2021 + CHI 2025). The literature term is 'cognitive forcing function', borrowed from clinical decision-making; the HCI variants are commit-before-reveal, on-demand reveal, and slow-reveal. Peer-reviewed in PACM HCI 5(CSCW1), article 188, DOI 10.1145/3449287; independently corroborated by the 'provocations' study at CHI 2025 and by a follow-up PACM HCI 2025 paper on partial explanations (DOI 10.1145/3710946).

evidence.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
evidence.quote: People supported by AI-powered decision support tools frequently overrely on the AI: they accept an AI's suggestion even when that suggestion is wrong.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not human-in-the-loop: an approval gate shows the agent's proposal first and asks for a yes/no, which is exactly the ordering that produces the follow-the-agent heuristic; the forcing function inverts the order so the human's judgement is formed before the agent's answer is visible. Not hint-ladder: that is a tutoring scaffold that graduates the specificity of help toward a worked answer; here there is no ladder and no pedagogy, only an ordering/friction constraint on a decision-support surface. Not confidence-reporting or confidence-checking-workflow: those annotate an answer that is still presented first. Not productive-struggle-erosion or human-agent-trust-exploitation: those are anti-patterns naming the harm; this is the interaction-level countermeasure, and it carries its own measured liability (users rate it worst).

evidence.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
evidence.quote: Building on prior research on medical decision-making, we designed three cognitive forcing interventions to compel people to engage more thoughtfully with the AI-generated explanations. We conducted an experiment (N=199), in which we compared our three cognitive forcing designs to two simple explainable AI approaches and to a no-AI baseline. The results demonstrate that cognitive forcing significantly reduced overreliance compared to the simple explainable AI approaches. However, there was a trade-off: people assigned the least favorable subjective ratings to the designs that reduced the overreliance the most.

evidence.title: "It makes you think": Provocations Help Restore Critical Thinking to AI-Assisted Knowledge Work
evidence.quote: We study the effect on knowledge work of provocations: brief textual prompts that offer critiques for and propose alternatives to AI suggestions. We conduct a between-subjects study (n=24) in which participants completed AI-assisted shortlisting tasks with and without provocations. We find that provocations can induce critical and metacognitive thinking.

candidates.name: Explanation-Induced Overreliance
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: ship the agent's rationale or reasoning trace to end users as the transparency answer and assume it produces appropriate reliance. Measured against a no-explanation control, the explanation raises the rate at which people accept the agent's recommendation whether or not it is correct, so acceptance rises while joint human-agent accuracy does not.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the HCI/CSCW seam. Two independent CHI/CSCW 2021 studies converge: explanations move acceptance without moving joint accuracy. Directly relevant to shipped agent products that expose 'thinking'/reasoning traces as a trust feature. Bansal et al. is CHI '21, DOI 10.1145/3411764.3445717 (PDF read in full via the UW IDL mirror).

evidence.title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
evidence.quote: explanations increased the chance that humans will accept the AI's recommendation, regardless of its correctness

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not human-agent-trust-exploitation: that anti-pattern is about a deliberately persuasive surface (confident phrasing, polished UX, no friction at the high-stakes action) — here the explanation is well-intentioned and shipped as a safety feature, and still moves acceptance uncontingently on correctness. Not false-confidence-syndrome: that is a model-side calibration failure in which wrong answers carry the same stated confidence as right ones; this is an interface-side effect that holds even when the explanation is accurate. Not black-box-opaqueness: that names the opposite failure (no traces at all) and its remedy is exactly what this anti-pattern warns is insufficient. Not decision-log: that is an operator-facing audit artifact, not a user-facing rationale at decision time.

evidence.title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
evidence.quote: While we observed complementary improvements from AI augmentation, they were not increased by explanations. Rather, explanations increased the chance that humans will accept the AI's recommendation, regardless of its correctness.

evidence.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
evidence.quote: Adding explanations to the AI decisions does not appear to reduce the overreliance and some studies suggest that it might even increase it.

candidates.name: Post-Error Trust Repair
candidates.summary: After the agent takes a visible wrong action, run an explicit repair turn that names the specific violation, expresses regret, gives the causal explanation, and states the concrete change — rather than silently correcting and continuing. It resolves the force that a trust violation does not heal on subsequent correct behaviour alone: without an affective plus informational repair move the human's reliance stays depressed (or, worse, is withdrawn wholesale) even after the underlying defect is fixed.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the HCI/Human-Factors seam. Established literature line ('trust repair', 'trust violation', 'AI apology') spanning Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (Kox et al. 2021, DOI 10.1007/s10458-021-09515-9), ACM THRI / HRI trust-repair work, and a 2024 cross-disciplinary review — a recurring problem across a decade, not a single product's gripe. The catalog currently has mechanical undo but no interaction protocol for the moment after a visible agent error.

evidence.title: Rethinking Trust Repair in Human-Robot Interaction (Esterwood)
evidence.quote: As robots become increasingly prevalent in work-oriented collaborations, trust has emerged as a critical factor in their acceptance and effectiveness. However, trust is dynamic and can erode when mistakes are made.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not compensating-action: that undoes the side effect in the world and says nothing about the human's calibration; a saga can run to completion while the operator still stops trusting the agent. Not conversation-handoff: that escalates the thread to a human operator instead of repairing the relationship in place. Not errors-swept-under-the-rug: that anti-pattern is about scrubbing failures from the agent's own context, an internal-state concern. Tension worth encoding rather than a duplicate: agent-confession-as-forensics warns that the agent's post-hoc self-narrative is not root cause — so the explanation component here must be sourced from the trace, not from the model's recollection.

evidence.title: Trust repair in human-agent teams: the effectiveness of explanations and expressing regret
evidence.quote: Our results indicated that expressing regret was crucial for effective trust repair. After trust declined due to the violation by the agent, trust only significantly recovered when an expression of regret was included in the apology. This effect was stronger when an explanation was added. In this context, the intelligent agent was the most effective in its attempt of rebuilding trust when it provided an apology that was both affective, and informational.

evidence.title: AI Apology: A Critical Review of Apology in AI Systems
evidence.quote: This article provides the first synthesis and critical analysis of the state of AI apology research, focusing on studies published between 2020 and 2023. We derive a framework of attributes to describe five core elements of apology: outcome, interaction, offence, recipient, and offender. With this framework as the basis for our critique, we show how apologies can be used to recover from misalignment in human-AI interactions, and examine trends and inconsistencies within the field.

candidates.name: Shared-Workspace Agent Objects
candidates.summary: Represent the agent's configuration, its invocations and its outputs as first-class shared objects living inside the team's collaborative artifact (named agent profiles, visible task requests, replies anchored in the document's existing comment surface), so every collaborator can see who asked the agent for what and integrate the result in place. It resolves the force that individually-scoped assistants make co-workers leave the shared workspace, consult a private agent, and then re-import and re-explain the result — destroying the awareness that made the shared artifact work.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the CSCW seam. Primary source is a CHI 2026 full paper (DOI 10.1145/3772318.3790648) with a one-week field study of 14 teams. The second source supports the design constraint that the agent's presence should ride on the artifact's existing shared objects rather than on extra conversational chatter, which measurably degrades real-time shared-workspace teamwork. The territory finding (profiles personal, outputs shared) is the load-bearing consequence to encode.

evidence.title: Envisioning Sensemaking in Multi-Human, Multi-Agent Collaborative Knowledge Work (Guan & Rieh, 2026)
evidence.quote: a conceptual framework for a dynamic shared representational workspace in which knowledge workers and specialized AI agents jointly gather evidence, schematize, hypothesize, and pursue collaborative goals

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not blackboard: that is a shared, queryable workspace for multiple *agents* to coordinate with each other; here the parties needing awareness are multiple *humans*, and the object being made visible is the agent's use. Not stigmergic-coordination: same agent-to-agent framing. Not generative-ui: that is one agent rendering interface components for one user's session. Not bidirectional-impulse-channel: that is a single human/single agent duplex channel. Not provenance-ledger: that is a post-hoc audit log for operators, not a co-present awareness surface that collaborators work in.

evidence.title: Collaborative Document Editing with Multiple Users and AI Agents
evidence.quote: Current AI writing support tools are largely designed for individuals, complicating collaboration when co-writers must leave the shared workspace to use AI and then communicate and reintegrate results. We propose integrating AI agents directly into collaborative writing environments. Our prototype makes AI use visible to all users through two new shared objects: user-defined agent profiles and tasks. Agent responses appear in the familiar comment feature. In a user study (N=30), 14 teams worked on writing projects during one week. Interaction logs and interviews show that teams incorporated agents into existing norms of authorship, control, and coordination, rather than treating them as team members. Agent profiles were viewed as personal territory, while created agents and outputs became shared resources.

evidence.title: Mutual Theory of Mind in Human-AI Collaboration: An Empirical Study with LLM-driven AI Agents in a Real-time Shared Workspace Task
evidence.quote: Most participants in our study believe verbal communication increases human burden, and the results show that bidirectional communication leads to lower HAT performance.

candidates.name: Intervention-to-Team Precedent
candidates.summary: When a human in a team workflow intercepts an agent node and overrides or corrects its output, persist the approved decision — with its evidence and its author — into a shared team memory and surface it to teammates as a binding precedent on later runs. It resolves the force that in team-scale agent-mediated work each reviewer's correction dies as a one-off edit, so the same class of mistake is re-fixed independently by every member and the team never accumulates the judgement it is paying for.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the CSCW seam. Honest caveat on evidence tier: the primary source is a peer-reviewed *demo/system* paper (cs.HC/cs.AI), not a controlled study, so it substantiates the recurring problem and the mechanism but not an effect size. The CHI 2026 field study independently establishes the team-scale force (agent outputs become shared resources governed by existing authorship norms). Corroborated in spirit by the CSCW-grounded observation that multi-agent and human-agent teams fail on 'common ground' and 'repair of misalignment' rather than on individual competence.

evidence.title: CollabSim: A CSCW-Grounded Methodology for Investigating Collaborative Competence of LLM Agents through Controlled Multi-Agent Experiments
evidence.quote: Yet recent study suggests that MAS often falter not because agents lack individual task-solving ability, but because they lack collaborative competence: the capacity to establish common ground, maintain shared task understanding, balance individual and collective incentives, and repair misalignment as interaction unfolds.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not agent-to-rule-distillation: that mines the *agent's own* production traces for recurring solutions and promotes them to deterministic rules outside the model; here the source is a *human override*, the scope is a team rather than a system, and the artifact carries author and evidence so it functions as an attributable precedent a teammate can inspect and contest. Not cross-session-memory: that persists one user's facts and preferences and never crosses to another member. Not human-reflection: that collects human critique inside a single reflection loop to improve the current plan, with nothing persisted for others. Not reflexion: the agent writes its own lessons there. Not unstructured-human-capture-layer: that is a raw human note layer the agent may read, with no approval, propagation or precedent semantics.

evidence.title: DeepTrans Studio: Turning Expert Interventions into Shared Team Knowledge in Agentic Translation Workflows
evidence.quote: Professional translation is often a team-based process: translators, reviewers, and project managers must coordinate terminology, legal force, and accountability across documents. Yet many LLM-based translation tools treat human corrections as isolated edits. Expert decisions made in one segment or by one member are rarely captured as reusable knowledge for the rest of the team.

evidence.title: Collaborative Document Editing with Multiple Users and AI Agents
evidence.quote: Interaction logs and interviews show that teams incorporated agents into existing norms of authorship, control, and coordination, rather than treating them as team members.

candidates.name: Pre-Use Expectation Calibration
candidates.summary: Before first use, tell the user the agent's expected accuracy and — critically — which class of error it has been tuned to make (false positives versus false negatives), rather than leaving the mental model to be formed by the first visible failure. It resolves the force that inflated first-run expectations depress acceptance permanently, and that two deployments with identical accuracy but opposite error profiles are perceived as very differently accurate.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the HCI seam. CHI 2019 full paper (DOI 10.1145/3290605.3300641), two studies with N=150 and N=400; PDF read in full via pdftotext, abstract quoted verbatim. Cross-source supports the mechanism rather than the intervention: reliance is governed by a general heuristic the user forms early, which is precisely what a first-run error-profile framing targets. The paper's own keywords include 'AI system on-boarding' and 'Shaping AI expectations', so the source names the shape.

evidence.title: Will You Accept an Imperfect AI? Exploring Designs for Adjusting End-user Expectations of AI Systems (CHI 2019)
evidence.quote: such different focus can lead to vastly different subjective perceptions of accuracy and acceptance

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not confidence-reporting or confidence-checking-workflow: those attach uncertainty to an individual answer at answer time; this is a one-time, pre-interaction framing of the system's error *profile*, and the finding is that the shape of the error, not the accuracy number, drives perceived accuracy. Not enforced-advisory-disclaimer: that is a non-suppressible per-response regulatory notice on high-risk answers.
