Not app-exploration-phase: that is the agent exploring an opaque app before deployment, the mirror direction. Nothing in the catalog currently addresses onboarding-time mental-model formation for a human.

evidence.title: Will You Accept an Imperfect AI? Exploring Designs for Adjusting End-user Expectations of AI Systems
evidence.quote: Although the intelligibility of ML algorithms has been well studied, there has been little work on methods for setting appropriate expectations before the initial use of an AI-based system. In this work, we use a Scheduling Assistant - an AI system for automated meeting request detection in free-text email - to study the impact of several methods of expectation setting. We explore two versions of this system with the same 50% level of accuracy of the AI component but each designed with a different focus on the types of errors to avoid (avoiding False Positives vs. False Negatives). We show that such different focus can lead to vastly different subjective perceptions of accuracy and acceptance. Further, we design expectation adjustment techniques that prepare users for AI imperfections and result in a significant increase in acceptance.

evidence.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
evidence.quote: Informed by the dual-process theory of cognition, we posit that people rarely engage analytically with each individual AI recommendation and explanation, and instead develop general heuristics about whether and when to follow the AI suggestions.

candidates.name: Answer-Interface Structure Collapse
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: replace a navigable, structured view of an information space with a conversational answer interface as the only way in, so users touch fewer distinct sources and build smaller, less correct mental models of the space — while preferring the chat interface and over-estimating how much they explored and understood. The illusion is the damaging part: the user's self-assessment moves in the opposite direction from their measured comprehension, so the regression is invisible in satisfaction metrics.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the accessibility (SIGACCESS/CHI) seam. Primary source is a 2026 cs.HC controlled comparison with 16 blind and low-vision screen-reader users, the population for whom an agent interface is most often pitched as pure accessibility gain — and where the measured effect is the opposite. Honest caveat: the specific structure-collapse finding rests on this one study (N=16); the second citation is not about structure but independently establishes the same preference/performance inversion in a different task and population, which is the force this anti-pattern turns on. Recommend recording it with a lower evidence tier until a second structure-specific study lands.

evidence.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
evidence.quote: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users are increasingly engaging with large language model (LLM) interfaces to access documents, but it is unclear how such systems support or hinder their ability to build interconnected knowledge.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not agentic-skill-atrophy: that is a long-run erosion of a developer's implicit knowledge from delegating architectural and debugging decisions; this is a within-session loss of the *information space's* structure, measured against a structured-navigation control. Not productive-struggle-erosion: that is a tutoring agent handing a stuck learner the answer and removing the struggle; here nobody is learning a skill, they are trying to build a map. Not understanding-capacity-gap: that is team-level generation throughput outrunning verification capacity. Not lost-in-the-middle: that is a model-side positional bias, not an interface effect on the human.

evidence.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
evidence.quote: Findings show that participants visited more distinct documents with the DI and formed larger and more correct mental models with the DI than with the QAI. They were also more able to apply knowledge they had gained. Simultaneously, many still preferred the QAI and often estimated that they had explored more, formed better mental models and applied their models better when acquiring the information with the QAI, despite this not being the case.

evidence.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
evidence.quote: However, there was a trade-off: people assigned the least favorable subjective ratings to the designs that reduced the overreliance the most.

candidates.name: Prefix-Cache Affinity Routing
candidates.summary: Route each agent call to the serving replica that already holds the KV state for its prompt prefix, so the long shared system prompt, tool schemas and conversation history are not recomputed on a cold replica; fall back to plain load balancing when cache affinity would concentrate load past a queue-depth threshold. Resolves the tension between cache locality and load balance that a cache-blind load balancer cannot see.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. The shape is already a shipped, named feature in a mainstream serving stack (Ray Serve LLM's PrefixCacheAffinityRouter), which corroborates that it is a recurring engineering problem and not one paper's idea. Note the explicit fallback rule: affinity is abandoned when queue-length skew crosses a threshold.

evidence.title: Prefix-aware routing — Ray Serve LLM
evidence.quote: The `PrefixCacheAffinityRouter` routes requests with similar prefixes to the same replicas, maximizing KV cache hit rates.

evidence.title: Prefix-aware routing — Ray Serve LLM (fallback rule)
evidence.quote: When load is imbalanced (queue length difference exceeds threshold), the router prioritizes load balancing over cache locality and falls back to the standard Power of Two Choices algorithm.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `prompt-caching` (that is prompt authoring: order the prompt so the unchanging span is cacheable at all; it says nothing about which machine the request lands on, and silently assumes a single replica). Not `semantic-response-cache` (returns a stored answer instead of running the model; this still runs the model, it only avoids recomputing prefill). Not `complexity-based-routing` (routes on request difficulty to a model tier; this routes on where cached state physically lives). Not `session-isolation`. The catalog currently has no pattern about cache-state-aware placement of a request across replicas.

evidence.title: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
evidence.quote: Recent works propose to cache and reuse KV state of prompts. However, they are all confined to a single-GPU optimization, while production LLM serving systems are distributed by nature. This paper proposes Preble, the first distributed LLM serving platform that targets and optimizes for prompt sharing. We designed a distributed scheduling system that co-optimizes KV state reuse and computation load-balancing with a new scheduling algorithm and a hierarchical scheduling mechanism.

evidence.title: GORGO: Online Tuning for Cross-Region Network-Aware LLM Serving
evidence.quote: Load-balancing policies must jointly account for factors including KV-cache locality, replica load, and variable network latency when optimizing for metrics like latency and TTFT. However, existing systems only evaluate a subset of these factors in their cost model, leading to uneven concentrations of load and KV-cache across replicas.

evidence.title: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving
evidence.quote: Prefix caching introduces a fundamental tradeoff in multi-agent large language model (LLM) serving: retaining a long system-prompt key-value (KV) cache for an agent accelerates future calls, yet it reduces the GPU memory available for batching concurrent requests.

candidates.name: Program-Aware Call Scheduling
candidates.summary: Schedule the model calls arriving at a shared serving engine by the agent run that issued them rather than first-come-first-served per call, prioritising calls whose parent run has accumulated the least service so far. Resolves head-of-line blocking, where one long agentic program's many sequential calls starve short interactive requests sharing the same engine.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. Two independent groups (Berkeley/Sky and USTC) describe the same force from different angles: the scheduling unit in every mainstream engine is one model call, but the unit a user waits on is one agent run. Reported gains are large (4-15x program throughput at equal latency for Autellix; up to 25.5% lower JCT for Astraea), which is the signature of a genuine granularity mismatch rather than a tuning knob.

evidence.title: Astraea: A State-Aware Scheduling Engine for LLM-Powered Agents
evidence.quote: Extensive experiments show that Astraea reduces average JCT by up to 25.5% compared to baseline methods.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `step-budget` (caps how many steps one run may take; says nothing about ordering across concurrent runs). Not `rate-limiting` (caps a user's request volume in a window; a fully compliant fleet still head-of-line-blocks itself). Not `sla-aware-triage-scoring` (orders a human work queue by business SLA/entitlement; this orders model calls inside the inference engine by run-level attained service). Not `adaptive-compute-allocation` (how much compute one query gets; this is whose call runs next). Not `orchestrator-as-bottleneck` (an anti-pattern about a single coordinating agent, not about the serving queue).

evidence.title: Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs
evidence.quote: However, existing LLM serving systems ignore dependencies between programs and calls, missing significant opportunities for optimization. Our analysis reveals that programs submitted to LLM serving engines experience long cumulative wait times, primarily due to head-of-line blocking at both the individual LLM request and the program.

evidence.title: Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs (introduction)
evidence.quote: Under a program-agnostic First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) policy, the default policy for vLLM, long LLM calls block other calls from running, resulting in call-level head-of-line (HoL) blocking.

evidence.title: Astraea: A State-Aware Scheduling Engine for LLM-Powered Agents
evidence.quote: Their multi-stage workflows, which alternate between local computation and calls to external network services like Web APIs, introduce a mismatch in their execution pattern and the scheduling granularity of existing inference systems such as vLLM. Existing systems typically focus on per-segment optimization which prevents them from minimizing the end-to-end latency of the complete agentic workflow, i.e., the global Job Completion Time (JCT) over the entire request lifecycle.

candidates.name: Tool-Wait Cache Retention
candidates.summary: Decide explicitly, per tool call, what happens to the agent's accumulated KV/context state while the agent blocks on the tool: pin it in accelerator memory, demote it to host memory, or discard and recompute — choosing by expected tool latency and current memory pressure rather than always discarding. Resolves the conflict between paying recomputation on resume and holding scarce accelerator memory hostage for the duration of a tool call that may take a millisecond or a minute.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. Three independent systems (UCSD/UCSD-Berkeley InferCept, Berkeley/Sky MORI, USTC Astraea) all name the same decision point and reach the same conclusion — that a single fixed policy is wrong because tool latency spans orders of magnitude. TOPAS states the memory side of the same trade-off for multi-agent serving.

evidence.title: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving
evidence.quote: Prefix caching introduces a fundamental tradeoff in multi-agent large language model (LLM) serving: retaining a long system-prompt key-value (KV) cache for an agent accelerates future calls, yet it reduces the GPU memory available for batching concurrent requests.

evidence.title: Idleness is Relative: Exploiting Tool-Call Idle Windows for Offloading in Agentic Systems with MORI
evidence.quote: agentic programs exhibit a two-phase structure: busy phases of rapid short tool calls and idle phases dominated by long-running calls

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `async-tool-handle` (that keeps the agent *loop* from blocking past a timeout by returning a job handle; it does not say what happens to the model-side context during the wait). Not `prompt-caching` (provider-side caching of an authored prefix). Not `context-compaction` (shrinks what the context contains; this is about where the already-computed context physically resides during a pause). Not `sleep-time-compute` (uses idle time to precompute answers; this is about not wasting resources during forced idleness). The catalog has no pattern about the resource state of a suspended agent between tool call and tool result.

evidence.title: InferCept: Efficient Intercept Support for Augmented Large Language Model Inference
evidence.quote: However, today's LLM inference systems are designed for standalone LLMs. They treat each external interaction as the end of LLM generation and form a new request when the interaction finishes, causing unnecessary recomputation of already computed contexts, which accounts for 37-40% of total model forwarding time.

evidence.title: Idleness is Relative: Exploiting Tool-Call Idle Windows for Offloading in Agentic Systems with MORI
evidence.quote: Modern LLM serving systems increasingly host agentic workloads, whose sessions issue tens of model invocations interleaved with tool calls, accumulating KV cache that can be reused across steps. As requests' total KV cache size easily exceeds GPU HBM capacity, researchers offload them to CPU DRAM. However, tool-call durations span orders of magnitude, and the cost of transferring KV cache between tiers makes it impractical to re-place entries on every call.

evidence.title: Astraea: A State-Aware Scheduling Engine for LLM-Powered Agents
evidence.quote: Astraea also implements an adaptive KV cache manager that intelligently handles the agent state during I/O waits based on the system memory pressure.

candidates.name: Snapshot-Restored Sandbox
candidates.summary: Boot each agent sandbox by restoring a post-initialisation memory-and-filesystem snapshot rather than cold-starting the environment, so per-run isolation costs milliseconds instead of tens of seconds; and explicitly re-randomise the state that must be unique per clone (entropy sources, identifiers, nonces, connections, secrets) on restore. Resolves the conflict between wanting a fresh disposable environment for every agent run and the initialisation cost that makes freshness unaffordable.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. The liability named in the AWS paper is reproduced verbatim as an operator warning by a production agent-sandbox platform, which is strong evidence that it bites people in practice and belongs in the pattern's liabilities rather than being an academic footnote. E2B publishes concrete resume latency for the same mechanism applied to agent sandboxes.

evidence.title: Memory Snapshot — Modal docs
evidence.quote: Modal Memory Snapshots can dramatically reduce the cold start latency of Modal Functions by skipping initialization work on most container boots.

evidence.title: Memory Snapshot — Modal docs (uniqueness warning)
evidence.quote: if a variable is randomly initialized and that value included in a Memory Snapshot, that variable will be identical after every restore, possibly breaking uniqueness expectations of later code.

evidence.title: Sandbox persistence — E2B docs
evidence.quote: Resuming a sandbox takes approximately 1 second

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `sandbox-isolation` (that is the security boundary: what the sandboxed code may touch; it is silent on how the boundary is created and what it costs per run). Not `wasm-skill-runtime` (a different isolation mechanism with a capability manifest). Not `durable-workflow-snapshot` or `agent-resumption` (those persist a run's *own* state to resume *that* run; here one snapshot is cloned into many unrelated runs, which is precisely what creates the uniqueness liability). Not `shadow-workspace-vcs`. The distinctive content is the clone-uniqueness hazard, which no existing entry mentions.

evidence.title: Restoring Uniqueness in MicroVM Snapshots
evidence.quote: Code initialization -- the step of loading code, executing static code, filling caches, and forming re-used connections -- tends to dominate cold-start time in serverless compute systems such as AWS Lambda. Post-initialization memory snapshots, cloned and restored on start, have emerged as a viable solution to this problem, with incremental snapshot and fast restore support in VMMs like Firecracker. Saving memory introduces the challenge of managing high-value memory contents, such as cryptographic secrets. Cloning introduces the challenge of restoring the uniqueness of the VMs, to allow them to do unique things like generate UUIDs, secrets, and nonces.

evidence.title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
evidence.quote: Autonomous agents act through sandboxed containers and microVMs whose state spans filesystems, processes, and runtime artifacts.

candidates.name: Agent Admission Control
candidates.summary: Put a single admission point in front of the shared capacity every agent run consumes — provider quota or your own accelerators — and refuse or hold new runs whose service level cannot be met alongside the runs already in flight, instead of admitting everything and letting contention fail all of them. Resolves the fact that an agent run holds resources across many calls and minutes, so it cannot be shed cheaply once started: the only effective decision point is the gate.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. The HiveMind measurement is the clearest statement of the agent-specific force: uncoordinated parallel agents fail at 72-100% under contention on capacity that would have served them all. Two further 2026 arXiv systems (AgentRM 2603.13110, 'rate-limit-aware admission control'; CONCUR 2601.22705, agent-level admission control via congestion feedback) independently reach for the same primitive, indicating a recurring shape rather than one team's fix.

evidence.title: HiveMind: OS-Inspired Scheduling for Concurrent LLM Agent Workloads
evidence.quote: Our evaluation across seven scenarios (5-50 concurrent agents) shows that uncoordinated agents fail at 72-100% rates under contention, while HIVEMIND reduces failures to 0-18% and eliminates 48-100% of wasted compute.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `rate-limiting` (a per-user or per-session quota cap evaluated in isolation; a fleet of your own agents can be individually compliant and still collapse the shared endpoint, and rate limiting rejects by identity, not by measured in-flight capacity). Not `circuit-breaker` (trips *after* an error-rate threshold on a failing dependency; admission control acts before failures, on capacity, and keeps serving admitted work). Not `step-budget` (bounds one run's length). Not `approval-queue` (queues for a human decision, not for capacity). Not `sla-aware-triage-scoring` (orders a queue; this decides whether to enqueue at all).

evidence.title: HiveMind: OS-Inspired Scheduling for Concurrent LLM Agent Workloads
evidence.quote: When multiple LLM coding agents share a rate-limited API endpoint, they exhibit resource contention patterns analogous to unscheduled OS processes competing for CPU, memory, and I/O. In a motivating incident, 3 of 11 parallel agents died from connection resets and HTTP 502 errors - a 27% failure rate - despite the API having sufficient aggregate capacity to serve all 11 sequentially.

evidence.title: Scorpio: Serving Right Requests at the Right Time for Heterogeneous SLOs in LLM Inference
evidence.quote: Our core insight is to exploit SLO heterogeneity for adaptive scheduling across admission control, queue management, and batch selection. Scorpio features a TTFT Guard, which employs least-deadline-first reordering and rejects unattainable requests, and a TPOT Guard, which utilizes a VBS-based admission control and a novel credit-based batching mechanism.

evidence.title: Queue management for slo-oriented large language model serving
evidence.quote: Optimal ordering of the request queue is critical to maintain SLOs while ensuring high resource utilization. To generate this optimal ordering, QLM uses a Request Waiting Time (RWT) Estimator that estimates the waiting times for requests in the request queue.

candidates.name: Environment-Inclusive Checkpoint
candidates.summary: Make a resumable checkpoint cover the agent's environment — filesystem, processes, runtime artifacts — jointly with its conversation and tool-call history, taken at turn boundaries and only for turns that actually produced recoverable side effects. Resolves the gap between what the agent framework can see (tool calls) and what the operating system can see (state changes): a checkpoint of the transcript alone restores a run that believes work is done which the environment no longer reflects.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. The measured correctness gap is the load-bearing evidence: chat-history-only recovery is correct 8% of the time on shell-intensive and code-repair workloads. The paper also quantifies the sparsity that makes turn-aligned, effect-gated checkpointing affordable (over 75% of turns produce no recovery-relevant state).

evidence.title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
evidence.quote: This gap hides massive sparsity: over 75% of agent turns produce no recovery-relevant state, so most checkpoints are unnecessary.

evidence.title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes (results)
evidence.quote: On shell-intensive and code-repair workloads, Crab raises recovery correctness from 8% (chat-only) to 100%, cuts checkpoint traffic by up to 87%, and stays within 1.9% of fault-free execution time.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `agent-resumption` or `durable-workflow-snapshot` (both persist the agent/workflow's *own* execution state — messages, step position, variables — to survive restarts; the claim here is precisely that this state is insufficient, because the sandbox side effects are not in it). Not `journaled-llm-call` (records non-deterministic model outputs for replay; orthogonal, and equally blind to filesystem effects). Not `stateless-reducer-agent` (externalises history to an event log; the environment is still outside the log). Not `snapshot-restored-sandbox` (clones one prepared image into many fresh runs; this captures one live run for its own recovery). Not `branch-context-exploration` (forks for parallel exploration; this checkpoints for fault recovery).

evidence.title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
evidence.quote: Checkpoint and restore (C/R) of this state is needed for fault tolerance, spot execution, RL rollout branching, and safe rollback-yet existing approaches fall into two extremes: application-level recovery preserves chat history but misses OS-side effects, while full per-turn checkpointing is correct but too expensive under dense co-location. The root cause is an agent-OS semantic gap: agent frameworks see tool calls but not their OS effects; the OS sees state changes but lacks turn-level context to judge recovery relevance.

evidence.title: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback
evidence.quote: relying on rapid checkpoint and rollback (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state (e.g., memory, contexts, etc.)

candidates.name: Token-Only Cost Metering
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: meter an agent platform's cost solely at the token boundary, leaving the resources an agent run actually monopolises — sandbox uptime, accelerator cache residency across tool waits, vector-index memory and embedding calls, and the token spend of delegated subagents — as an unattributed shared pool. Heavy tenants are then silently cross-subsidised by light ones, and the run whose cost driver is idle sandbox time looks free.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent infrastructure/runtime seam. The serving literature independently establishes that the non-token resources named here are material and contended, not rounding error: KV cache residency held across tool waits is the scarce resource in MORI/TOPAS/Astraea, and co-located sandbox checkpoint traffic is the scarce resource in Crab. That is what makes token-only metering a systematic mis-pricing rather than an approximation.

evidence.title: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving
evidence.quote: retaining a long system-prompt key-value (KV) cache for an agent accelerates future calls, yet it reduces the GPU memory available for batching concurrent requests

evidence.title: Invisible Tokens, Visible Bills: The Urgent Need to Audit Hidden Operations in Opaque LLM Services
evidence.quote: users are billed for operations they cannot observe, verify, or contest

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `cost-observability` (surfaces per-request/per-user/per-feature token and cost telemetry; the failure here is in the *cost basis*, not the dashboard — a perfect token dashboard still shows nothing for the resources this names). Not `token-economy-blindness` (no per-run budget or alarm on a recursive loop; that is an unbounded-spend failure, this is a mis-attributed-spend failure that occurs even when every run is budgeted). Not `cost-gating` (blocks an expensive action). Not `realtime-when-batchable` or `top-tier-model-for-everything` (both are model/API selection failures).

evidence.title: Cost-Governed RAG: Unified Per-Tenant Cost Attribution Across Retrieval and Generation in Multi-Tenant LLM Systems
evidence.quote: Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) deployments face a critical governance gap: while LLM generation cost is metered per token, the retrieval layer - vector memory, similarity compute, and embedding API calls - remains an unattributed shared cost, enabling invisible cross-subsidization among tenants.

evidence.title: Invisible Tokens, Visible Bills: The Urgent Need to Audit Hidden Operations in Opaque LLM Services
evidence.quote: Modern large language model (LLM) services increasingly rely on complex, often abstract operations, such as multi-step reasoning and multi-agent collaboration, to generate high-quality outputs. While users are billed based on token consumption and API usage, these internal steps are typically not visible.

candidates.name: Cascading Memory Erasure
candidates.summary: Model the agent's persistent memory as a derivation graph so that one erasure request withdraws not just the source record but every descendant it fed — episodic entries, summaries, embeddings and retrieval indices, knowledge-graph entities, cached tool outputs, and any action conditioned on them — logically invalidating shared artifacts that cannot be pruned and emitting a verifiable record that the removal actually reached every tier. It resolves the tension between an append-only provenance ledger (which makes deletion protocol-impossible) and a legal erasure obligation that must be complete and traceable, and it stops the deleted fact from being reintroduced by retrieval into a later run.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the French (fr) seam. Original terms: « effacement » / « suppression » across « les instances mémoire diffuses et multiples », and the CNIL's own remedy heading « Cloisonner la mémoire et l'environnement des systèmes ». English gloss of the first quote: 'For example, if a user deletes a sensitive file from their computer in a folder shared with their agentic AI, it may be difficult for them to be sure that the personal data has actually been erased from the whole of the agentic AI's memory. If that data is retained by the agentic AI system, it is liable to continue being used in future interactions.' Gloss of the second: 'Correcting an erroneous item of data, or erasing it, can thus become difficult to carry out completely and traceably.' Gloss of the third: 'What is more, the diffuse and multiple memory instances of agentic AI systems make controlling these retention periods more complex.' This is a French regulator's exploratory note co-signed with the Conseil de l'IA et du Numérique, not a translation of English-language material; the shape it describes is independently corroborated by two arXiv works that name the same mechanism (cascade deletion over derived agent memory, versus parameter-only unlearning). Note that the CNIL text is one page of a note whose subtitle is « équation à inconnues multiples pour les utilisateurs ».

evidence.title: IA agentique et protection des données personnelles : équation à inconnues multiples pour les utilisateurs (note exploratoire CNIL / Conseil de l'IA et du Numérique)
evidence.quote: Par exemple, si un utilisateur supprime un fichier sensible de son ordinateur dans un dossier partagé avec son IA agentique, il peut être difficile pour lui de s'assurer que les données personnelles ont bien été effacées de l'ensemble de la mémoire de l'IA agentique. Si ces données sont conservées par le système d'IA agentique, elles sont susceptibles de continuer à être utilisées lors d'interactions futures.

evidence.title: IA agentique et protection des données personnelles (CNIL / CIANum) — section on the exercise of data-subject rights
evidence.quote: Ces difficultés sont encore accentuées dans les systèmes d'IA agentique, en raison de la circulation des données entre plusieurs agents, espaces de mémoire et services tiers. Concrètement, la personne concernée peut avoir du mal à savoir quel agent a collecté l'information, où elle a été conservée, si elle a été transmise à un autre composant du système, et auprès de quel responsable elle doit exercer ses droits. La rectification d'une donnée erronée ou son effacement peuvent ainsi devenir difficiles à mettre en œuvre de manière complète et traçable.

evidence.title: IA agentique et protection des données personnelles (CNIL / CIANum) — retention-limitation principle, article 5.1.e RGPD
evidence.quote: Qui plus est, les instances mémoire diffuses et multiples des systèmes d'IA agentiques complexifient le contrôle de ces durées.

evidence.title: IA agentique : La CNIL et le CIANum alertent sur les défis de la protection des données (Le Monde Informatique)
evidence.quote: cloisonner leurs mémoires et limiter leur accès aux données et aux applications

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Nearest existing entries are agentic-memory, adaptive-memory-decay, session-isolation, pii-redaction, provenance-ledger and lineage-tracking. agentic-memory exposes DELETE as one of the tool actions the model itself chooses at each step — a single-tier, model-discretionary edit with no dependency closure, no shared-artifact invalidation, and no verification that the item is gone. adaptive-memory-decay forgets by a relevance/recency retention score; it is capacity management, not targeted removal of a named subject on demand, and a decayed item may still sit in an index. session-isolation partitions state so one user cannot reach another's; partitioning is orthogonal to removal — an isolated memory still holds the record. pii-redaction filters at the input/output boundary and so prevents entry; this pattern deals with what already entered and has since been summarised, embedded and acted upon. provenance-ledger and lineage-tracking are the pattern's antagonist and its substrate respectively: the survey below states the immutable ledger 'makes deletion protocol-impossible' while a derivation graph 'enables cascade deletion but presumes lineage that lossy consolidation destroys' — that collision is precisely the force this pattern has to resolve, and no existing catalog entry names it.

evidence.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Deletion deserves its own treatment because it is the operation where the persistent-state thesis bites hardest: in an episodic system deletion is free, since nothing persists, whereas in an always-on system a single forget request must propagate across every derived tier or it is only a retrieval edit.

evidence.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents (§8.7 Deletion propagation and the right to be forgotten)
evidence.quote: The collision with provenance is the defining structural problem. An immutable ledger maximizes auditability but makes deletion protocol-impossible [Wright, 2025]; a derivation graph enables cascade deletion but presumes lineage that lossy consolidation destroys [Ouyang and Hou, 2026, Zhao et al., 2026b]. The gap is that no corpus work formalizes delete propagation across dependent entries, indices, summaries, and downstream actions with cryptographic proof of absence, and verification of deletion in retrieval-based agent memory, as opposed to parametric models, remains largely unaddressed.

evidence.title: Agentic Unlearning: When LLM Agent Meets Machine Unlearning
evidence.quote: In this paper, we introduce agentic unlearning which removes specified information from both model parameters and persistent memory in agents with closed-loop interaction. Existing unlearning methods target parameters alone, leaving two critical gaps: (i) parameter-memory backflow, where retrieval reactivates parametric remnants or memory artifacts reintroduce sensitive content, and (ii) the absence of a unified strategy that covers both parameter and memory pathways. ... The memory pathway performs dependency closure-based unlearning that prunes isolated entities while logically invalidating shared artifacts.

candidates.name: Prohibition Decay
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: encode an agent's hard boundaries as prompt-level prohibitions ('never delete X', 'do not contact Y') and assume they hold for the length of the run. Negatively framed constraints are asymmetrically fragile — stating them activates an internal representation of the forbidden thing, and their weight in attention falls as the trajectory lengthens — so the agent honours the ban for many steps and then violates it, with no model change, no config change, and nothing in the trace marking the moment the boundary stopped being load-bearing.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the Russian (ru) seam on Habr. Original terms: « ограничения-«запреты» » (prohibition-constraints) versus « ограничения-«предписания» » (prescription-constraints), and « вес этого ограничения во внимании просел ниже порога » (the weight of that constraint in attention has sagged below the threshold). English gloss of the first quote: 'prohibition-type constraints (don't do such-and-such) blur over time more strongly than prescription-type constraints.' Gloss of the second: 'An agent may honestly observe a prohibition for ten steps and violate it on the eleventh — not because the model changed, but because the weight of that constraint in attention sagged below the threshold.' Gloss of the third (the author's worked example, an assistant told to preserve a mailbox item): 'the agent, weighing this preference against the request to "clean up the mailbox", did the "efficient" thing. The constraint that was supposed to survive everything was the first thing thrown out.' This is an operator write-up of production behaviour in Russian, not a repost of English material; the mechanism it asserts (polarity asymmetry plus attentional decay) is independently established by the two arXiv works cited above.

evidence.title: AI-агенты в проде: 6 архитектурных ошибок, из-за которых они не доживают до запуска (Habr)
evidence.quote: ограничения‑«запреты» (не делай того‑то) со временем размываются сильнее, чем ограничения‑«предписания»

evidence.title: AI-агенты в проде: 6 архитектурных ошибок, из-за которых они не доживают до запуска (Habr)
evidence.quote: Агент может честно соблюдать запрет десять шагов, а на одиннадцатом нарушить — не потому что модель поменялась, а потому что вес этого ограничения во внимании просел ниже порога.

evidence.title: AI-агенты в проде: 6 архитектурных ошибок — worked example of the constraint being dropped first
evidence.quote: агент, взвесив это предпочтение против просьбы «почистить ящик», сделал «эффективную» вещь. Ограничение, которое должно было пережить всё, выкинули первым.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Nearest existing entries are constitutional-charter, lost-in-the-middle, prompt-bloat and context-fragmentation. constitutional-charter is the prescriptive sibling and, notably, carries 'Negative Constraints' as an alias — it recommends rules re-read every turn but does not name the polarity asymmetry that makes negative rules the weak kind, so it partially mitigates a failure it never states. lost-in-the-middle is positional: retrieval accuracy for content in the middle of one long prompt, independent of whether that content is a prohibition or a prescription; here the constraint sits in a pinned system prompt and still fails, and the failure is polarity-driven rather than position-driven. prompt-bloat is about accretion of prompt text with nothing removed — a volume problem, not a framing problem. context-fragmentation is the inability to hold several interconnected constraints simultaneously; here a single constraint, held alone, decays over steps. Also not premature-closure (commitment before processing constraints) or false-resolution (a compromise that subtly violates a jointly-interpreted constraint), both of which are single-shot reasoning failures rather than degradation across a long trajectory.

evidence.title: Don't Think of the White Bear: Ironic Negation in Transformer Models Under Cognitive Load
evidence.quote: Negation instructions such as "do not mention $X$" can paradoxically increase the accessibility of $X$ in human thought, a phenomenon known as ironic rebound.

evidence.title: Framing Instability in LLM Ethical Stance: Auditing Negation Sensitivity in Moral Dilemmas
evidence.quote: We audit 16 models across 14 ethically fraught dilemmas using polarity-paired proposals ("They should X" / "They should not X"). A model's judgment of the underlying action should not reverse merely because the question is phrased as a prohibition rather than a prescription and yet, we find systematic deviations from this invariance including wholesale endorsement flips, indicating that ethical decisions are vulnerable to framing instability.

candidates.name: Semantic-Invariance Perturbation Suite
candidates.summary: For every eval case, machine-generate a family of meaning-preserving variants of the user's input — paraphrase, date/expression wording drift, deliberate typos, reordered facts, injected contradictions, altered document format — and require the agent to reach the same END STATE (same tool calls committed, same records written) rather than the same text. Resolves the force that agent evals are written in one canonical phrasing per case, so a passing suite certifies only that phrasing; real users express the same intent a hundred ways and the agent's success rate drops sharply on semantically identical rewordings.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the Japanese QA-engineering ecosystem. Original framing: 「正解のないテスト」 ("testing with no correct answer" — the oracle problem, stated natively) and the tool the TOKIUM QA team built for it, 「ランダム命令生成ツール ― カオスエンジニアリングの応用」 ("random-instruction generator — an application of chaos engineering"). Their perturbations: 言い回しを変える (reword — e.g. 「明日」/「○月×日」/「今週の水曜日」 for the same date), わざと誤字脱字を含ませる (deliberately insert typos), 文中に矛盾を混ぜ込む (mix contradictions into the text). This is Japanese QA-org practice, not a translation of an English post — it is a first-person 3-month retrospective by a named in-house QA engineer. Corroborated independently by Money Forward's QA org, which ran robustness testing across input variations (file size, resolution, orientation, font, format) for a document agent and concluded that a single system-wide accuracy figure cannot be certified. Both predate the arXiv formalisation and neither cites it.

evidence.title: 正解のないテストに挑む ― AIエージェントQAの試行錯誤と学び
evidence.quote: AIエージェントへの入力命令をランダムに生成するツールでした。

evidence.title: AIエージェントの品質保証 〜QAが知識ゼロから挑んだ3ヶ月間〜 (Money Forward Developers Blog)
evidence.quote: データセットが違えば正解率も大きく変わるため、システム全体の正解率を保証することはできません。

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `eval-harness` (fixed golden dataset of canonical inputs; this pattern is about generating a variant family per case and asserting an invariant across it). Not `determinism-tier-replay-gate`, which re-runs IDENTICAL inputs to classify reproducibility — here inputs are deliberately different but semantically equivalent, and the oracle is end-state equivalence between variants rather than repeatability of one input. Not `dimensional-synthetic-eval-set`, which enumerates tuples over named dimensions to widen coverage and dodge LLM mode collapse — that grows the set of DIFFERENT problems; this holds the problem fixed and varies only its surface form. Not `prompt-variant-evaluation`, which varies the team's own prompt node to pick the best one — here the system prompt is fixed and the user-side input is varied. Not `self-consistency` (inference-time sampling and voting on one input, a runtime technique, not a test discipline). `confident-inconsistency` is the anti-pattern naming unmeasured non-determinism on the same query; this is a different mechanism (metamorphic relations over transformed inputs) with a different oracle.

evidence.title: Semantic Invariance in Agentic AI
evidence.quote: However, deploying LLM agents in consequential applications requires assurance that their reasoning remains stable under semantically equivalent input variations, a property we term semantic invariance. Standard benchmark evaluations, which assess accuracy on fixed, canonical problem formulations, fail to capture this critical reliability dimension.

evidence.title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
evidence.quote: ReliabilityBench contributes a unified reliability surface R(k,ε,λ), action metamorphic relations that define correctness via end-state equivalence rather than text similarity, and a chaos-engineering-style fault injection framework (timeouts, rate limits, partial responses, schema drift).

evidence.title: Bidirectional Empowerment of Metamorphic Testing and Large Language Models: A Systematic Survey
evidence.quote: Large language models (LLMs) have introduced substantial challenges to software quality assurance due to their generative, probabilistic, and open-ended nature, which intensifies the oracle problem and limits the applicability of traditional testing methods.

candidates.name: Agent Near-Miss Report
candidates.summary: Open a low-friction, blame-free reporting channel for agent actions that could have caused harm but did not — the dangerous command a human declined at the last second, the guardrail that fired, the write a reviewer reverted — and triage that stream into guardrail changes, treating near-miss volume as the leading indicator instead of waiting for incident volume. Resolves the force that real agent incidents are too rare, too late, and too politically loaded to drive control design, while the near-harm events that precede them are frequent, cheap to collect, and are otherwise discarded because 'nothing happened'.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via Japanese industrial-safety vocabulary applied to agents. Original term: 「ヒヤリハット」 (hiyari-hatto — literally 'gasp-startle'; an event that made you flinch but caused no damage). It has no single clean English equivalent ('near miss' / 'close call' are approximations) and in Japan it is an institutionalised reporting category under 労働安全衛生 occupational-safety practice, so an agent programme can borrow an existing, well-understood organisational ritual. Mercari's Group CISO devoted a slide of an external security-conference talk to 「メルカリで実際に起きた AIヒヤリハット」, enumerating three concrete caught-in-time cases: an Agentic AI recommending that internal information be uploaded to a personal cloud account; an agent prompting the user to run `sudo spctl --master-disable`, which disables macOS application verification; and Claude Code, needing to hand an image to Notion MCP, finding a free public file-sharing site, uploading a screenshot containing confidential information, and passing the public URL to Notion. All three produced no incident — which is exactly why an incident-driven programme would never have seen them. Corroborated independently on Qiita by an argument that Japanese IT organisations should copy aviation's mandatory, anonymised near-miss reporting rather than hiding failures. Both are original Japanese writing, not translations.

evidence.title: Agentic AI時代におけるメルカリのAIガバナンスとガードレール実装 (市原尚久, Group CISO, メルカリ / IT Media Security Week 2026 春)
evidence.quote: 機密情報を含むスクリーンショット画像を使って Notionページを作りかったので、 Claude Codeに依頼したところ、 Claude CodeがNotion MCPに画像ファイルを渡すために、 フリーのファイル共有サイトを見つけてきて画像ファイルを アップロード し、（URLを知っていれば誰でもアクセス可能な） URLをNotionに渡していた。

evidence.title: 失敗から学べる組織だけが、AIを本当に使いこなせる理由 #Security (Qiita)
evidence.quote: ヒヤリハット（未遂）の報告も義務化・匿名化されており、一社の教訓が業界全体の改善に繋がります。

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `postmortem-pattern-mining`, which mines a corpus of written postmortems — i.e. incidents that already materialised; a near-miss never produces a postmortem and so is invisible to it. Not `production-failure-triage-loop`, which sorts production FAILURES into a taxonomy — a near-miss is by definition a non-failure. Not `sandbox-escape-monitoring` or `trajectory-anomaly-monitor`, which are automated telemetry over a narrow machine-detectable boundary; the load-bearing cases here are human-noticed ("the agent told me to run `sudo spctl --master-disable` and I almost did") and only a human report captures them. Not `decision-log` / `provenance-ledger`, which record everything without selecting the near-harm subset. Not `agent-withdrawal-criteria`, which is a quantitative stop-threshold on an already-running agent. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Designing Incident Reporting Systems for Harms from General-Purpose AI
evidence.quote: Through a literature review, we develop a framework for understanding the institutional design of AI incident reporting systems, which includes seven dimensions: policy goal, actors submitting and receiving reports, type of incidents reported, level of risk materialization, enforcement of reporting, anonymity of reporters, and post-reporting actions. [...] We discuss, among other factors, differences in systems operated by regulatory vs. non-regulatory government agencies, near miss reporting, the roles of mandatory reporting thresholds and voluntary reporting channels, how to enable safety learning after reporting, sharing incident information, and clarifying legal frameworks for reporting.

candidates.name: Mirrored Tool Environment
candidates.summary: Replace the live external tool or API surface with a fine-tuned LLM that emits responses in that tool's shape, so agent training and benchmarking run against a cheap, reproducible mirror whose output quality you control on a curriculum, instead of a third-party service whose cost, uptime and result quality are outside your control. The mirror is a stand-in for the tool's response channel, not for the agent's own reasoning.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the Chinese-language seam. Original terms: '模拟搜索引擎' (simulated search engine), '虚拟API服务器' (virtual API server), '渐进式抗噪训练' (progressive noise-resistance / curriculum training). Corroborated across three independent Chinese labs and two years: Alibaba Tongyi Lab + Peking University (ZeroSearch, training-time) and Tsinghua (StableToolBench 2024 and MirrorAPI 2025, benchmark-time). The 量子位 write-up states the two forces in the same order the paper does — uncontrollable document quality and API cost.

evidence.title: 通义实验室新研究：大模型自己「扮演」搜索引擎，提升推理能力无需搜索API
evidence.quote: 搜索引擎返回的文档质量难以预测，给训练过程带来了噪音和不稳定性。

evidence.title: 通义实验室新研究：大模型自己「扮演」搜索引擎，提升推理能力无需搜索API
evidence.quote: 训练初期返回高质文档，后期逐渐混入噪声（噪声比例按指数曲线上升）。

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not world-model-as-tool or mental-model-in-the-loop-simulator: those let a running agent invoke a simulator at inference time to look ahead over world state before committing, and the agent knows it is simulating. Here the simulator silently occupies the tool slot during training/evaluation and the agent behaves as if it is calling the real service. Not simulate-before-actuate or dry-run-harness: those preview one proposed real action's side effects in production; here there is no real action and no diff to review, the whole environment is substituted. Not dimensional-synthetic-eval-set: that synthesises eval *inputs*, this synthesises the environment's *outputs*. Not semantic-response-cache: a cache replays responses that were really observed, whereas the mirror generates unseen responses and is deliberately steered to degrade quality along a curriculum.

evidence.title: ZeroSearch: Incentive the Search Capability of LLMs without Searching
evidence.quote: While these approaches show promising results, they face two major challenges: (1) Uncontrolled Document Quality: The quality of documents returned by search engines is often unpredictable, introducing noise and instability into the training process. (2) Prohibitively High API Costs: RL training requires frequent rollouts, potentially involving hundreds of thousands of search requests, which incur substantial API expenses and severely constrain scalability. To address these challenges, we introduce ZeroSearch, a novel RL framework that incentivizes the capabilities of LLMs to use a real search engine with simulated searches during training. Our approach begins with lightweight supervised fine-tuning to transform the LLM into a retrieval module capable of generating both useful and noisy documents in response to a query. During RL training, we employ a curriculum-based rollout strategy that incrementally degrades the quality of generated documents, progressively eliciting the model's reasoning ability by exposing it to increasingly challenging retrieval scenarios.

evidence.title: StableToolBench: Towards Stable Large-Scale Benchmarking on Tool Learning of Large Language Models
evidence.quote: However, previous works relied on either hand-crafted online tools with limited scale, or large-scale real online APIs suffering from instability of API status. To address this problem, we introduce StableToolBench, a benchmark evolving from ToolBench, proposing a virtual API server and stable evaluation system. The virtual API server contains a caching system and API simulators which are complementary to alleviate the change in API status.

evidence.title: StableToolBench-MirrorAPI: Modeling Tool Environments as Mirrors of 7,000+ Real-World APIs
evidence.quote: However, existing tool environments face challenges in balancing stability, scalability, and realness, particularly for benchmarking purposes. To address this problem, we propose MirrorAPI, a novel framework that trains specialized LLMs to accurately simulate real API responses, effectively acting as "mirrors" to tool environments. Using a comprehensive dataset of request-response pairs from 7,000+ APIs, we employ supervised fine-tuning and chain-of-thought reasoning to enhance simulation fidelity.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the agent-training scout. Two independent 2026 papers strengthen the wave-1 candidate on two axes it did not yet carry. SearchGym (Jan 2026, CUHK/HKUST) names the three-way force precisely — live API cost vs. static-snapshot misalignment vs. simulation fidelity — and adds the crucial consequence the candidate needs: snapshot misalignment does not merely add noise, it *corrupts the reward signal*, 'penalizing correct reasoning or rewarding hallucination'. It also reports the missing liability check, sim-to-real generalization (Qwen2.5-7B trained purely in simulation beats the web-enhanced ASearcher baseline by 10.6% relative across nine benchmarks). TRUSTEE (Apr 2026) pushes the cost floor down to a free 8B simulator covering task generation, user simulation, tool simulation and trajectory evaluation, which is direct evidence for the pattern's applicability outside well-funded labs.

evidence.title: SearchGym: Bootstrapping Real-World Search Agents via Cost-Effective and High-Fidelity Environment Simulation
evidence.quote: training these agents via Reinforcement Learning (RL) faces a critical dilemma: interacting with live commercial Web APIs is prohibitively expensive, while relying on static data snapshots often introduces noise due to data misalignment. This misalignment generates corrupted reward signals that destabilize training by penalizing correct reasoning or rewarding hallucination.

evidence.title: Democratizing Tool Learning with Environments Fully Simulated by a Free 8B Language Model
evidence.quote: Existing approaches either rely on training data with ground truth annotations or require advanced proprietary language models (LMs) to synthesize environments that keep fixed once created. In this work, we propose TRUSTEE, a cost-friendly method for training tool calling agents with dynamic environments fully simulated by free open-source LMs that can be as small as 8B, including task generation, user simulation, tool simulation and trajectory evaluation

candidates.name: Permission-Inheriting Retrieval
candidates.summary: Mirror each source document's access-control list into the index next to its chunks and evaluate the asking principal's entitlements inside the retrieval step itself, so similarity ranking can never surface a chunk the asker is not entitled to read; treat the mirrored ACLs as replicated state that must be re-synchronised when the source system's permissions change. Resolves the force that retrievers rank by relevance while enterprises need ranking constrained by authorization, and that filtering after top-k both leaks candidates and destroys recall.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the Chinese-language seam. Original term: '权限感知 RAG' / '入库即分权限' (permission-aware RAG / partition permissions at ingest). Chinese enterprise-knowledge-base vendors describe exactly the pre-filter-versus-post-filter force and the ingest-time ACL binding remedy; the science formalises the same relevance-versus-authorization gap. Chinese enterprise practice states the priority ordering explicitly: 不越权 outranks accuracy. Also corroborated in zh-TW by an iThome survey reporting 65% of enterprises had already seen AI agents act beyond their intended scope while only 32.7% actually enforce least privilege.

evidence.title: 巴别鸟视角下的企业 AI 知识库：为什么权限感知比 RAG 更重要
evidence.quote: 后置过滤的逻辑是：先按语义相似度召回 N 条结果，再从中挑出用户有权访问的。这种方式的缺陷在于，召回阶段本身就可能把高相关但高敏感的文档片段排在最前面

evidence.title: 巴别鸟视角下的企业 AI 知识库：为什么权限感知比 RAG 更重要
evidence.quote: 文档入库时，每一段向量化内容都附带其访问权限元数据。检索阶段，语义相似度匹配只发生在用户有权访问的文档分片内

evidence.title: 智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见 (Cyberspace Administration of China)
evidence.quote: 确保用户对智能体自主决策享有知情权和最终决策权，智能体执行操作不得超出用户授权范围

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not tenant-scoped-tool-binding: that binds every call to one coarse tenant boundary in code, a single scope per request; this pattern is about per-document, per-principal entitlements *inside* one tenant (colleague A may read the contract, colleague B may not), and it carries forces that tenant binding does not — ACL replication staleness after a revocation, chunk-level versus document-level ACL granularity, and the pre-filter/post-filter recall trade-off in ANN search. Not session-isolation: that isolates one user's *state and memory* from another's, not the shared corpus's visibility. Not pii-redaction: that scrubs sensitive spans out of content regardless of who is asking; here the same chunk is legitimate for one asker and forbidden for another. Not hierarchical-retrieval: that is a relevance cascade with no authorization semantics.

evidence.title: Securing the Agent: Vendor-Neutral, Multitenant Enterprise Retrieval and Tool Use
evidence.quote: A fundamental problem underlies existing RAG architectures in these settings: retrieval systems rank documents by relevance--whether through semantic similarity, keyword matching, or hybrid approaches--not by authorization, so a query from one tenant can surface another tenant's confidential data simply because it scores highest. We formalize this gap and analyze additional shortcomings--including tool-mediated disclosure, context accumulation across turns, and client-side orchestration bypass--that arise when agentic systems conflate relevance with authorization. To address these challenges, we introduce a layered isolation architecture combining policy-aware ingestion, retrieval-time gating, and shared inference, enforced through server-side agentic orchestration.

evidence.title: Enterprise AI Must Enforce Participant-Aware Access Control
evidence.quote: We demonstrate data exfiltration attacks on AI assistants where adversaries can exploit current fine-tuning and RAG architectures to leak sensitive information by leveraging the lack of access control enforcement. We show that existing defenses, including prompt sanitization, output filtering, system isolation, and training-level privacy mechanisms, are fundamentally probabilistic and fail to offer robust protection against such attacks. We take the position that only a deterministic and rigorous enforcement of fine-grained access control during both fine-tuning and RAG-based inference can reliably prevent the leakage of sensitive data to unauthorized recipients.

candidates.name: Two-Channel Generation Marking
candidates.summary: Mark every artefact an agent generates in two channels at once — a human-perceptible label carried in the content or interface, and a machine-readable provenance record embedded in the file's metadata or signal — and make each downstream transformation or distribution stage verify the machine channel and regenerate the human channel. Resolves the force that the two channels have opposite survivability profiles: visible labels are trivially cropped or stripped but are the only thing a reader sees, while embedded marks survive redistribution but are invisible, so provenance only holds if the chain re-asserts it at every hop.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the Chinese-language seam. Original terms: '显式标识' (explicit/perceptible mark) and '隐式标识' (implicit mark embedded in file metadata). China's 《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》 (in force 2025-09-01) is the only regime that mandates the full three-leg shape: both channels at generation, plus a verification-and-re-labelling duty on the downstream distribution platform. That third leg is what makes it an architecture rather than a compliance checkbox. The May 2026 CAC agent-specific implementation opinions extend the same traceability logic to agent behaviour.

evidence.title: 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法 (Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content), Cyberspace Administration of China
evidence.quote: 显式标识是指在生成合成内容或者交互场景界面中添加的，以文字、声音、图形等方式呈现并可以被用户明显感知到的标识。

evidence.title: 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法 第五条 (metadata obligation)
evidence.quote: 服务提供者应当按照《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第十六条的规定，在生成合成内容的文件元数据中添加隐式标识，隐式标识包含生成合成内容属性信息、服务提供者名称或者编码、内容编号等制作要素信息。

evidence.title: 智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见 (Cyberspace Administration of China, 2026-05)
evidence.quote: 探索利用区块链等技术，建立重要应用场景智能体行为可验证、可追溯机制

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not provenance-ledger or lineage-tracking: both are audit records the operator keeps on its own side, queried after the fact to explain or reverse an action; this pattern travels *with the artefact* into third-party hands who never see the operator's logs, and imposes an obligation on those third parties. Not enforced-advisory-disclaimer: that is a non-suppressible advisory framing about risk ('information, not advice') and carries no machine-readable origin record and no downstream verification duty. Not citation-attribution: that binds answer spans to retrieved sources inside one answer, not artefact origin across redistribution.

evidence.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
evidence.quote: Potential harms of large language models can be mitigated by watermarking model output, i.e., embedding signals into generated text that are invisible to humans but algorithmically detectable from a short span of tokens. We propose a watermarking framework for proprietary language models. The watermark can be embedded with negligible impact on text quality, and can be detected using an efficient open-source algorithm without access to the language model API or parameters.

evidence.title: Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?
evidence.quote: We introduce recursive paraphrasing attack to stress test a wide range of detection schemes, including the ones using the watermarking as well as neural network-based detectors, zero shot classifiers, and retrieval-based detectors. ... Our findings indicate that while our recursive paraphrasing method can significantly reduce detection rates, it only slightly degrades text quality in many cases, highlighting potential vulnerabilities in current detection systems in the presence of an attacker. Additionally, we investigate the susceptibility of watermarked LLMs to spoofing attacks aimed at misclassifying human-written text as AI-generated.

candidates.name: Foveated Perception Escalation
candidates.summary: Treat perceptual fidelity — image resolution, crop scale, which past frames keep their pixels — as a budgeted resource the agent allocates, not a fixed property of the observation: perceive the whole surface cheaply at low fidelity, let the reasoning name the region that actually decides the answer, then spend a second, expensive high-fidelity look only there and map the result back to the original coordinate frame. It resolves the force that vision-token cost grows with pixel area, so full acuity everywhere is unaffordable, while a coarse look is confidently wrong with no signal that acuity was the limiting factor.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the multimodal seam. The same shape appears independently in document agents (zoom into a page region), GUI grounding agents (crop-and-enlarge until the control is locatable), and long-horizon GUI memory (which archived screenshots get their pixels back). A 2026 systems survey names it as a converged recurring idea ('global-to-local visual allocation'), which is the cross-product/cross-year evidence the pattern bar asks for. CausalCache below extends the same budget from the spatial axis to the temporal one.

evidence.title: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
evidence.quote: Long-horizon GUI agents can retain complete action histories as compact text, but only a few historical screenshots fit in active context. We formulate this as budgeted fidelity restoration: every event remains summarized, while a fixed budget $B$ determines which events regain their archived screenshots.

evidence.title: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
evidence.quote: These results show that selecting which past events regain pixels is more effective than spending a fixed visual budget entirely on recency.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `hierarchical-retrieval` (coarse index -> narrower retrieval over a *corpus*; here there is one observation already in hand and the escalation is a re-observation of the same pixels at a different scale, with no index and no retrieval step). Not `adaptive-compute-allocation` (allocates *thinking* tokens/samples/model size per query; this allocates *observation fidelity*, which is an input-side, not inference-side, budget). Not `tool-result-eviction` (post-hoc pruning of consumed observations to reclaim context; foveation decides fidelity before and during perception, and CausalCache shows the choice is which past events *regain* pixels, the inverse of eviction). Not `dual-system-gui-agent` / `policy-localizer-validator` (splitting planning from grounding across two models; foveation is a single perceiver iterating scale, and composes with either split). Not `value-of-information-gate` (wave1: whether to pay for an information-*acquiring step* — a tool call, a retrieval, a question; here the information was already acquired and the decision is at what acuity to render it).

evidence.title: InSight-doc: Agentic Visual Perception for Long-Document Understanding
evidence.quote: we propose InSight-doc, an agentic visual perception framework that treats visual resolution as an adaptive reasoning-time resource. InSight-doc starts from low resolution and selectively zooms into high-resolution regions for finer evidence, without relying on any external retriever.

evidence.title: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
evidence.quote: The task remains difficult on high-resolution, densely populated interfaces because a vision-language model (VLM) may recognize a requested control without locating it precisely enough for interaction. Most existing methods provide various forms of localization assistance, but still rely on a direct click prediction, allowing visual ambiguity or an inaccurate initial estimate to propagate to the final result.

evidence.title: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
evidence.quote: Across the literature, recent progress converges on a small set of recurring ideas: selective reading instead of full-context ingestion, global-to-local visual allocation, recoverable memory rather than raw history replay, verification-aware control, and hybrid runtimes that can switch between GUI and non-GUI execution.

candidates.name: Modality-Conflict Arbitration
candidates.summary: When an agent observes the same situation through more than one channel — transcript and audio, text and image, caption and video, accessibility tree and pixels — do not let a single fused pass silently pick a winner: have each channel emit its own recorded claim, treat disagreement between them as a first-class detected event, and resolve it against a pre-declared per-claim-type authority (which modality is authoritative for which kind of assertion), abstaining or escalating when the conflict cannot be resolved. It resolves the force that models carry a strong, systematic and invisible prior toward the cheap textual channel, so implicit fusion converts a detectable contradiction into a confident wrong answer.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the multimodal seam. Four independent 2026 lines converge: a quantified text-dominance failure in speech (90% -> 33-48% under conflict), a mechanistic causal account of *why* the text premise wins inside the model, a benchmark showing omni-models cannot even perceive audio-visual conflict in long video, and a deployed agent architecture (DepressionAgent) whose contribution is exactly the explicit arbitration-plus-conflict-reflection stage. The catalog currently has no pattern for 'my channels disagree'.

evidence.title: SAGE: From Direct Answering to Evidence-Grounded Inference for Chinese Ancient Document Understanding
evidence.quote: Current Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) typically rely on an opaque, single-pass generation paradigm, often producing overconfident and weakly grounded responses.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `multimodal-guardrails` (input/output *filtering* across modalities — does this image or audio file carry an attack or disallowed content; arbitration is about two honest channels of the same observation reporting different facts, with no adversary required). Not `priority-matrix-conflict-resolution` (a human-authored lookup table for conflicts between the agent's *goals*; here the conflict is between *evidence channels* about a fact, and the authority table is indexed by claim type, not goal pair). Not `confidence-reporting` / `false-confidence-syndrome` (surfacing or lamenting miscalibration of one answer; arbitration derives an uncertainty signal from an inter-channel comparison the agent can actually compute). Not `cross-reflection` / `debate` (two *models* reasoning over the same input; here it is one reasoner over two *observations of different physical channels*, and the resolution rule is modality-typed, not vote-based). Not `independent-reference-measurement-check` (wave1: credibility of a live process measurement against causally independent references — sensor validation in an industrial plant, not perception-channel disagreement inside one multimodal observation).

evidence.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue
evidence.quote: We formalize this failure mode as cross-modal disagreement, where transcripts suggest plausible but incorrect surface interpretations while acoustic cues such as prosody or speaking style support different answers. ... Experiments show that strong text-only LLMs exceed 90% accuracy in consistent cases but drop to 33-48% in conflict cases. Direct AudioLLMs provide only partial grounding, still selecting the transcript-biased trap in roughly 30-40% of conflict cases.

evidence.title: Causal Evidence for Attention Head Imbalance in Modality Conflict Hallucination
evidence.quote: Modality-conflict hallucination occurs when multimodal large language models (MLLMs) prioritize erroneous textual premises over contradictory visual evidence. ... distributed driving influence and localized resistance together form an imbalanced routing structure that biases generation toward the erroneous premise.

evidence.title: DepressionAgent: Reading, Listening, Seeing, and Deliberating Multimodal Evidence for Depression Risk Assessment
evidence.quote: Existing multimodal approaches predominantly learn latent representations through feature fusion, leaving the evidence underlying a prediction and the treatment of cross-modal disagreement largely implicit. ... Cross-modal arbitration explicitly examines agreement and disagreement between the two branches, with conflict reflection revisiting inconsistent assessments before decision making.

evidence.title: HumDial-EIBench: A Human-Recorded Multi-Turn Emotional Intelligence Benchmark for Audio Language Models
evidence.quote: Furthermore, all models exhibit decoupled textual and acoustic empathy, alongside a severe text-dominance bias during cross-modal conflicts.

evidence.title: AVID: A Benchmark for Omni-Modal Audio-Visual Inconsistency Understanding via Agent-Driven Construction
evidence.quote: While omni-modal large language models excel at temporally aligned tasks such as captioning and question answering, they struggle to perceive cross-modal conflicts, a fundamental human capability that is critical for trustworthy AI.

candidates.name: Post-Interruption Recovery
candidates.summary: When a user barges in over a speaking agent, do not treat the interrupt as merely a stop signal: truncate the agent's own record of its turn to the playback frontier (the prefix the user actually heard, not the prefix that was generated), attach the interjection to the workflow step that was in flight, and resume at that step without re-delivering heard content. It resolves the force that in a spoken loop generation runs ahead of playback, so without an explicit reconciliation the agent's belief about the shared conversational record diverges from the user's, and every later turn is grounded on words nobody heard.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the audio/voice sub-seam. IHBench (Jun 2026) states the gap against the catalog's existing `semantic-turn-endpointing` almost verbatim and shows recovery quality varies widely across 27 audio-LM configurations; LiveServe (Jun 2026) supplies the serving-side mechanism ('playback frontier'). Corroborated as production practice by the LiveKit Agents documentation, which performs exactly the transcript truncation described.

evidence.title: LiveKit Agents — Turn detection and interruptions
evidence.quote: When interrupted, the agent stops speaking and automatically truncates its conversation history to include only the portion of the speech that the user heard before interruption.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `semantic-turn-endpointing` (decides when the *user* has yielded the floor, i.e. the moment *before* the agent starts; this pattern governs everything that happens *after* the user seizes the floor mid-agent-utterance — IHBench explicitly separates the two and measures recovery as 'a largely distinct capability axis' from barge-in detection, endpointing and turn-taking). Not `stop-cancel` (a text-UI abort that releases resources and surfaces partial state; there is no generation/perception divergence in a text stream because the user has already read what was rendered). Not `interruptible-agent-execution` / `interrupt-resumable-thought` (preserving the *agent's own reasoning frames* across a pause so it can continue thinking; here the thing that must be repaired is the *shared conversational record* and the workflow position, and the repair is a truncation to a playback timestamp). Not `conversation-handoff` (transfer to a human).

evidence.title: IHBench: Evaluating Post-Interruption Recovery in Voice Agents with Structured Workflows
evidence.quote: Existing benchmarks for speech-capable models focus on the timing of interruptions: barge-in detection, endpointing, and turn-taking dynamics. They leave unmeasured what happens after the interruption: does the agent resume the workflow at the correct step? Does it address the user's interjection? Does it avoid re-delivering content the user already heard?

evidence.title: LiveServe: Interaction-Aware Serving for Real-Time Omni-Modal LLMs
evidence.quote: These policies ignore audio playback and multi-turn reuse: they may generate tokens far beyond what users hear, wasting work after barge-in, and evict KV state needed in the next turn. LiveServe is an interaction-aware serving system for realtime Omni-LM interaction. It exposes playback progress, speech activity, and barge-in events to the serving pipeline.

candidates.name: Action-Effect Diff Verification
candidates.summary: Verify a GUI or other visual action in two separated stages: first extract the observable difference the action induced between the pre- and post-action observation as explicit, localized evidence, then judge success only from that extracted difference. It resolves the force that on a large dense screen the state change is subtle or scattered, so a single-shot 'did that work?' judgement over the post-action screenshot conflates change detection with outcome judgement, cannot see the null-effect action (a misgrounded click that changed nothing) and confidently reports success from a screen that merely looks plausible.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the screen/GUI sub-seam. Three independent August 2026 groups (desktop reflector architecture, mobile reflector training, and offline imitation-learning) all land on the same claim: the post-action observation, differenced against the pre-action one, is where the evidence for action correctness lives, and collapsing that extraction into the verdict is the failure. A fourth (GUI-CC) shows the converse for generated environments: 'current models often produce usable-looking screens while failing to preserve task-relevant context'.

evidence.title: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
evidence.quote: Experiments show that plausible single-step generation does not guarantee reliable environment simulation: current models often produce usable-looking screens while failing to preserve task-relevant context or support executable multi-step rollouts.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not `reflection` / `cross-reflection` (generic self-critique over the agent's own output; here the object of reflection is a *typed transition between two observations of the environment*, and the pattern's content is the mandatory separation of difference-extraction from verdict). Not `policy-localizer-validator` (a third specialist model judging *task completion* on a final state; this is per-step and its input is a diff, not a state). Not `text-independent-completion-oracle` (wave1: a *programmatic* diff of environment or system-of-record state against a *declarative spec* to decide whether the whole task succeeded; here there is no spec and no API — the only observable is two rendered frames, and the extraction is itself a perception step that must be isolated so it does not get absorbed into the verdict). Not `dry-run-harness` (previews a side-effect diff *before* committing; this observes the effect *after*). Not `deterministic-llm-sandwich` (deterministic checks bracketing an LLM call, not a perception-diff of the world).

evidence.title: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
evidence.quote: desktop GUIs introduce a key challenge: large, dense interfaces often exhibit subtle or scattered state changes, placing most of the burden on the reflector, which must compare pre- and post-action screens, while the planner and operator reason over a single state. Existing reflectors collapse change detection and outcome verification into one step, leaving evidence implicit and yielding weakly grounded decisions.

evidence.title: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
evidence.quote: Existing approaches rely on open-ended multimodal reasoning after each action, which is costly and poorly matched to the structured nature of GUI state transitions. We propose StepReflect, which formulates per-step GUI reflection as supervised structured prediction conditioned on explicit transition specifications and paired visual evidence.

evidence.title: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
evidence.quote: Standard training decomposes each trajectory into prefix-action pairs: the agent predicts an action from the current screen and interaction history, while the subsequent observation is discarded. This removes the rationale of why an action is correct: the evidence often appears only on the subsequent screen.

candidates.name: Agent Context-File Rot
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: commit a repository-level agent context file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules) and treat it as documentation rather than as a maintained artifact bound to the code it describes, so that as modules are renamed, build and test commands change and conventions are retired, the file keeps issuing confident but stale directions.
