A human reader discounts an out-of-date README; the agent executes it, re-injects the retired convention into new changes, and pays a per-run token tax for guidance nobody has re-validated. The fix is to bind the file to the code with the same consistency checks used for documentation — symbol-reference checks, command-executes checks, convention-still-holds checks — and to gate it in CI.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via an arXiv cs.SE sweep of the repository-context-file literature (arXiv API query abs:"AGENTS.md", 12 distinct papers 2025-2026). The phenomenon is independently named ('context rot'), independently measured (23.0% of a representative repository sample carry stale code-element references), and independently characterised as an artefact class that 'evolves like configuration code'. Four research groups (Adelaide/Bayreuth, NAIST/Queen's, ETH Zurich/LogicStar, Williams College) converge on the same object without citing a shared framework, and a fourth paper records that practitioners actively disagree about whether these files help at all — which is what an unmaintained, untested artefact looks like.

evidence.title: Probe-and-Refine Tuning of Repository Guidance for Coding Agents
evidence.quote: Engineers typically maintain [AGENTS.md] files to supply this context as instructions for coding agents, but whether they help is contested: recent studies disagree on whether LLM-generated guidance improves or harms agent performance.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. context-driven-architecture-drift is the ABSENCE of guidance (the agent sees only the files it can reach and violates unwritten conventions); here guidance is present, authoritative and wrong. own-your-prompts and prompt-versioning govern production prompt artefacts (versioned, owned, rolled back) — neither addresses consistency between a repo file and the evolving codebase it describes, because prompts do not describe a codebase. agentic-context-engineering-playbook is the AGENT's own prompt/memory evolving through delta updates; this file is human-authored, read by humans too, and rots against source code. set-and-forget-system-prompt (wave1) is decay of instructions WITHIN one conversation; this is decay ACROSS releases. guardrail-erosion-through-compaction is a rule paraphrased away by compaction — a context-window mechanism, not staleness. silent-source-rot is an external data source changing shape under a tool wrapper; here the repo's own code moves under its own instruction file. context-window-dumb-zone is long-context degradation (the other, unrelated industry sense of 'context rot').

evidence.title: Context Rot in AI-Assisted Software Development: Repurposing Documentation Consistency for AI Configuration Artifacts
evidence.quote: As preliminary evidence, applying an existing README/wiki consistency checker to a statistically representative sample of 356 repositories identifies stale code element references in 23.0% of repositories, showing that traditional documentation consistency tools can already surface context rot.

evidence.title: Agent READMEs: An Empirical Study of Context Files for Agentic Coding
evidence.quote: We find that these files are not static documentation but complex, difficult-to-read artifacts that evolve like configuration code through frequent, small additions.

evidence.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
evidence.quote: Surprisingly, we find that providing context files does not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average.

candidates.name: Intent-Drift Review
candidates.summary: Review a machine-authored change by recovering, independently of the artifact, the intent it was meant to serve — from the issue, the conversation log and the task metadata — then back-translating the produced diff into a statement of what it actually does, scoring the divergence between the two, and ranking the regions of the change by that divergence so scarce human attention goes only where intent and artifact disagree. The unit of review stops being the line and becomes the intent-to-artifact gap.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via an arXiv cs.SE sweep on code review of agent-authored changes. Two independent groups — an industrial one reporting a deployed system with measured effects (intent prediction 0.86 F1, drift detection QWK = 0.907, spotlight 2.4x over the baseline AI reviewer at 5x fewer tokens, misalignment reduced by 5.76 points p = 0.026 in rollout) and an academic one arguing from explainability that diff-local review structurally cannot see intent divergence — arrive at the same unit-of-review change. A third, larger study independently frames review as the decisive control point, which is why moving its unit matters.

evidence.title: 3100 Opinions on Code Review in an AI World: Building Causal Theory from Practitioner Discourse
evidence.quote: Its organizing claim is that review is the control point through which a coding agent's effect on software is decided, and that AI does not fix the sign of that effect: the team sets it, through the expertise its humans bring and how it structures the review process.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. confidence-checking-workflow has the PRODUCER self-report which parts need checking; the whole point here is that the producer's self-report is what the independently-recovered intent replaces. llm-as-judge and agent-as-judge score an artifact against a rubric and emit a gate decision; this compares an artifact against THIS change's recovered intent and emits an attention ranking, not a score. spec-first-agent fixes the spec before implementation; this recovers intent after the fact for artifacts that never had a spec. approval-view-fidelity-gap (wave1) is an anti-pattern about lossy rendering of an approval surface; this is about what the reviewer should be comparing at all. inner-critic (Self-Modification Diff Gate) has a critic persona gate the agent's edits to its own code/rules. dry-run-harness previews side effects before commit; no intent comparison. rigor-relocation is the general move of putting rigor in scaffolding; this is a specific named mechanism (intent prediction, back-translated drift, spotlight).

evidence.title: From Code Review to Code Critique: Intent, Drift, and Spotlight for AI-Generated Diffs at Scale
evidence.quote: We present ARCTIC, an AI-powered Code Critique system that reframes code review around three capabilities: intent prediction, which infers why a change was made from conversation logs and metadata; drift detection, which measures divergence between the developer's intent and the agent's output via backtranslation; and code spotlight, which ranks the regions of a diff most warranting human scrutiny.

evidence.title: Beyond the 'Diff': Addressing Agentic Entropy in Agentic Software Development
evidence.quote: We term this process agentic entropy: a systemic drift that traditional code diff-based and HCXAI methods fail to capture, as they address local outputs rather than global agentic behaviour.

candidates.name: Machine-Contributor Admission Policy
