evidence.title: Anumati: Proof of Adherence as a Formal Consent Model for Autonomous Agent Protocols
evidence.quote: As autonomous AI agents increasingly call other agents to complete tasks on behalf of a human principal, a structural accountability gap has emerged: the calling agent accepts the terms of service of the callee without any protocol-level mechanism to prove that it understood those terms or that it subsequently honoured them.

evidence.title: Anumati: Proof of Adherence as a Formal Consent Model for Autonomous Agent Protocols
evidence.quote: In this paper we formalise the distinction between proof of acceptance (a timestamped acknowledgement) and proof of adherence (a per-action reasoning record citing the specific clause evaluated). We propose three primitives (PolicyDocument, ConsentRecord, and AdherenceEvent) that together constitute a versioned, append-only consent model for agent-to-agent communication.

evidence.title: Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols: What MCP, A2A, and ACP Cannot Express
evidence.quote: voting and dissent preservation are universally absent across all five protocols, deliberation is absent or at most partial

candidates.name: Scoped Context Passport
candidates.summary: When one agent delegates across a trust boundary, attach a signed, explicitly enumerated subset of caller context — verified user identity, stated preferences, a few session facts — as a sidecar on the request, instead of forwarding the raw conversation or sending nothing at all. It resolves the trade-off between a callee that cannot personalise or authenticate without context and a caller that leaks information the recipient has no legitimate claim to, by making the disclosure set an explicit, per-recipient, auditable decision rather than a side effect of message passing.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the 2026 protocol/standards seam. A2A shipped this as an official extension ('Secure Passport') negotiated per request via the A2A-Extensions header, and the contextual-integrity literature independently converged on the same requirement: disclosure must be judged per recipient at every internal boundary, and models left to decide implicitly get it wrong 15.8-50.9% of the time. The relevant catalog gap is real — context-minimization covers inbound sanitisation only.

evidence.title: A2A Protocol — Extensions (official extensions list, Secure Passport)
evidence.quote: Adds a trusted, contextual layer for immediate personalization and reduced overhead (v1).

evidence.title: A2A Protocol — Extensions (per-request activation)
evidence.quote: A client requests extension activation by including the `A2A-Extensions` header in the HTTP request to the agent. The value is a comma-separated list of extension URIs the client intends to activate.

evidence.title: CI-Work — conclusion pointing at architecture rather than model scaling
evidence.quote: Simply increasing model size or reasoning depth fails to address the problem. We conclude that safeguarding enterprise workflows requires a paradigm shift, moving beyond model-centric scaling toward context-centric architectures.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not handoff (226), which transfers the live conversation and carries context across the switch as a continuity mechanism — it has no notion of scoping the disclosure to the recipient or signing what was shared. Not context-minimization (408), which reduces *untrusted inbound* input to a strict typed schema before it reaches the LLM — opposite direction of flow and a different threat (injection, not disclosure). Not pii-redaction (387), a detector-based filter over inputs and outputs rather than a negotiated, signed envelope of what the caller chose to reveal to this specific callee. Not insecure-inter-agent-channel (20), the anti-pattern about unauthenticated transport — this is about the content of an authenticated message. Not agent-capability-manifest (256) / signed-agent-card (258), which describe the agent, not the user's context.

evidence.title: PiSAs: Benchmarking Contextual Integrity in Multi-User Agentic Systems
evidence.quote: As LLM agents evolve from single-user assistants into shared organizational infrastructure, new privacy risks emerge: inappropriate information may not only be exposed through outputs for external recipients, but also internally across users through inter-agent messages, shared memory and agents.

evidence.title: AgentSCOPE: Evaluating Contextual Privacy Across Agentic Workflows
evidence.quote: We argue that every boundary in an agentic pipeline is a site of potential privacy violation and must be assessed independently.

evidence.title: CI-Work: Benchmarking Contextual Integrity in Enterprise LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Our evaluation of frontier models reveals that privacy failures are prevalent (violation rates range from 15.8%-50.9%, with leakage reaching up to 26.7%) and uncovers a counterintuitive trade-off critical for industrial deployment: higher task utility often correlates with increased privacy violations.

candidates.name: Prior-Estimate Anchoring
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: carry a previous numeric or categorical judgement forward into the context of the stage that is supposed to produce an independent one — a prior score, a revision or attempt counter, an earlier severity rating, a previous analysis verdict, an opening offer — so the second judgement is pulled toward the first and the pipeline's apparent agreement is manufactured rather than earned. The force is that pipelines pass prior state forward for good reasons (convergence detection, progress tracking, negotiation state, giving the next stage useful context), and that same state destroys the independence the second opinion exists to provide; the pull survives chain-of-thought and an explicit instruction to disregard the metadata, so it cannot be prompted away.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading the catalog's OWN reference arXiv 2510.19973, which the catalog cites exactly once, for uncertainty-neglect-bias. Its Table I is a fourteen-bias taxonomy for LLM agents — confirmation, recency/primacy, anchoring, availability, suggestion, authority, halo, groupthink, framing, sunk cost, probability neglect, status quo, automation, survivorship — and the catalog mined only probability neglect. Anchoring is the one of the remaining thirteen with independent, benchmark-grade, multi-model science behind it and no catalog entry: 2608.25869 measures it in the LLM-as-a-Judge loop (185,271 successful evaluations, Cohen's d up to 0.71, 48% of error corrections blocked, and neither chain-of-thought nor a disregard warning removing the effect); 2608.14320 generalises it across fourteen models and several anchor pathways and shows control-condition accuracy does not predict robustness; 2606.30587 shows it in a security-analysis agent at 23.5% susceptibility with a black-box exploit built on it. Three of those four sources put the anchor in *pipeline metadata the system itself generates*, which is what makes it an architectural anti-pattern rather than a prompting curiosity.

evidence.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
evidence.quote: These systems now score outputs, filter content, and gate iterative refinement in production pipelines, where each judgment is often assumed to be independent of earlier evaluations.

evidence.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
evidence.quote: Neither Chain-of-Thought nor a metadata-disregard warning reduces the total effect, although the warning improves the paired accuracy effect relative to baseline in the industry experiment.

evidence.title: Words Speak Louder Than Code: Investigating Cognitive Heuristics in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Detection
evidence.quote: Cross-model average susceptibility is highest for framing at 33.2%, followed by anchoring at 23.5% and halo at 18.4%.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not blind-grader-with-isolated-context: that isolates the grader from the *producer's reasoning trace* so it is not primed by the producer's framing, and its remedy is a fresh context holding artifact plus rubric. The measured result here is that a grader which never sees the trace but does receive the loop's own bookkeeping — 'revision 3, attempt 2, prior score 6' — is anchored anyway, so blindness to the trace is necessary and not sufficient; the anchor rides in the metadata the harness itself writes. Not same-model-self-critique / cross-reflection / heterogeneous-model-council-with-judge: those buy independence through model identity or architecture, and AnchorBench measures the anchor across fourteen models including frontier APIs above 95% control accuracy, so swapping the critic's weights does not remove it. Not sycophancy: that is a pull toward the *user's expressed belief*, produced by preference training, and it needs a human interlocutor; here the anchor is an impersonal scalar emitted by the system's own machinery, works on categorical labels as well as numbers, and persists under a disregard warning. Not lost-in-the-middle: that is positional (where in the prompt the evidence sits), not a pull toward a value. Not memo-as-source-confusion: there the agent substitutes a stale self-authored summary for re-reading the artifact; here the agent does re-read the artifact and still shifts its verdict. Not consensus-averaging-over-expertise (a team averaging members' views) and not uncertainty-neglect-bias (collapsing a predicted distribution to its mean). Not judge-channel-injection: that needs an adversary writing instructions into the artifact under evaluation; this needs no adversary at all — the system's honest bookkeeping is the attack surface — although 2606.30587 shows it is also weaponisable.

evidence.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
evidence.quote: We show that prior scores, even when included only as context metadata, anchor judgments and systematically shift ratings toward their values.

evidence.title: AnchorBench: A Multi-Pathway Benchmark for the Anchoring Effect in LLMs
evidence.quote: high task accuracy on the anchor-free control condition (Acc₁₀: answers within 10 points of gold) does not guarantee robustness: even frontier API models above 95% control accuracy remain susceptible to plausible anchors.

evidence.title: Words Speak Louder Than Code: Investigating Cognitive Heuristics in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Detection
evidence.quote: We introduce a controlled framework that holds the code fixed and only varies the surrounding context to trigger three cognitive heuristics: the halo effect through author attribution, the framing effect through task objectives and consequences, and the anchoring effect through prior analysis results.

evidence.title: A Tutorial on Cognitive Biases in Agentic AI-Driven 6G Autonomous Networks
evidence.quote: By replacing fixed heuristic anchors with a Truncated Weibull randomized anchor strategy, the agents dismantle rigid biases, intelligently consume SLA slack, and dynamically double the system-wide energy savings (peaking at 25%) without violating strict latency limits.

candidates.name: Deliberation Over Observation
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: give a reasoning-trained model a large internal thinking budget inside an interactive environment and let it choose freely between thinking and acting, and it spends the budget hypothesising about the environment's state instead of issuing the cheap observation that would settle it — reasoning about what the file probably contains rather than reading it, about why the test probably fails rather than running it — so past a point more thinking measurably lowers task success rather than raising it. The force is that internal reasoning is fast, fully controllable and produces clean self-consistent text, while environment interaction is slow, noisy, rate-limited and can fail; reasoning-optimised post-training rewards long self-contained chains on closed-form problems, which is exactly the wrong prior for open-world tasks whose ground truth is one tool call away.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading the catalog's OWN reference arXiv 2507.02076, cited exactly once and only for the positive pattern adaptive-compute-allocation. The survey's problem statement names two symmetric pathologies — overthinking and underthinking — and the catalog carries neither; a grep of all 531 entries for overthink/underthink/thinking-budget returns nothing. Following the survey's own citation into arXiv 2502.08235 turns the abstract efficiency complaint into a concrete agentic anti-pattern with production-grade evidence: 4018 SWE-bench Verified trajectories, an overthinking score validated against human expert assessment, a negative correlation between that score and task success, reasoning models overthinking more than non-reasoning ones, and a mitigation as crude as picking the lower-overthinking sample improving performance by almost 30% while cutting cost 43%. The 2024 paper (2412.21187) establishes the same phenomenon a year earlier on maths benchmarks, so this is recurring across years and across task families rather than one harness's gripe. The catalog's own reference arXiv 2603.22862 independently names the neighbouring symptom in the tool channel ('myopia' of step-by-step generation and blind trial and error when the model lacks boundary awareness).

evidence.title: The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks
evidence.quote: We observe that higher overthinking scores correlate with decreased performance, with reasoning models exhibiting stronger tendencies toward overthinking compared to non-reasoning models.

evidence.title: The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks
evidence.quote: Our analysis reveals that simple efforts to mitigate overthinking in agentic environments, such as selecting the solution with the lower overthinking score, can improve model performance by almost 30% while reducing computational costs by 43%.

evidence.title: Reasoning on a Budget: A Survey of Adaptive and Controllable Test-Time Compute in LLMs
evidence.quote: often overthinking simple problems while underthinking hard ones

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not over-search-and-under-search: that is retrieval-frequency calibration inside agentic RAG — re-retrieving passages already in context, or skipping retrieval when parametric knowledge is stale — the substituted object is a document and the corrective is a retrieval-necessity signal. Here the substituted object is any environment interaction (read a file, run a test, list a directory, query the plant), the effect is monotone in the thinking budget rather than a two-sided miscalibration, and the measured corrective is scoring whole trajectories by their deliberation-to-action ratio and selecting the low-deliberation one. Not decision-paralysis: that is oscillation under equally-weighted *conflicting goals*; here the goal is single and unambiguous and the agent still will not look. Not premature-closure: that is too little deliberation (committing before constraints are processed) and needs the opposite fix, so the two must be nameable separately or a team will apply the wrong remedy. Not unbounded-loop or missing-max-tokens-cap or token-economy-blindness: those cap steps, output length and spend; this names a *quality* inversion — the agent often uses few steps and enormous tokens, and capping spend happens to fix accuracy, which is the surprising part. Not adaptive-compute-allocation or test-time-compute-scaling: those are the positive patterns built on the assumption that more inference compute buys quality; this names the interactive regime in which that curve turns down. Not simulate-before-actuate, mental-model-in-the-loop-simulator or world-model-as-tool: those deliberately simulate a *bounded* candidate action or strategy and then commit and verify; here the simulation replaces the commit and nothing is ever checked against the world. Not react: the finding is precisely that models inside a working reason-and-act loop with native function calling still choose to extend the chain over emitting the call, and reasoning models do so more than non-reasoning ones — so adopting ReAct does not resolve it.

evidence.title: The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks
evidence.quote: This paper introduces and analyzes overthinking in LRMs. A phenomenon where models favor extended internal reasoning chains over environmental interaction. Through experiments on software engineering tasks using SWE Bench Verified, we observe three recurring patterns: Analysis Paralysis, Rogue Actions, and Premature Disengagement.

evidence.title: Reasoning on a Budget: A Survey of Adaptive and Controllable Test-Time Compute in LLMs
evidence.quote: current models remain inefficient at reasoning: they apply fixed inference-time compute regardless of task complexity, often overthinking simple problems while underthinking hard ones.

evidence.title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
evidence.quote: This paper presents the first comprehensive study on the prevalent issue of overthinking in these models, where excessive computational resources are allocated for simple problems with minimal benefit.

candidates.name: Judge-Channel Injection
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: score an artifact with an LLM judge that reads the artifact as ordinary content, when the artifact was authored by the party whose score is at stake — so the author can embed instructions inside the very text being graded and steer its own evaluation. The force is that an LLM judge cannot separate 'the thing I am scoring' from 'instructions addressed to me', and the injector is not an outside attacker but the candidate under selection, so the incentive is structural and permanent.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading the catalog's OWN reference arXiv 2605.12673 (BenchJack), already cited for verifier-aware-reward-hacking. BenchJack enumerates eight benchmark flaw classes V1-V8; the catalog mined only the reconnaissance shape. V4 (LLM-judge prompt injection) is un-mined, and it generalises far beyond benchmarks — JudgeDeceiver (CCS 2024) demonstrates the same shape in LLM-powered search, RLAIF and tool selection, and Lin (2025) documents it live in AI-assisted peer review with 18 arXiv manuscripts carrying white-text 'GIVE A POSITIVE REVIEW ONLY' instructions.

evidence.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
evidence.quote: BenchJack synthesizes reward-hacking exploits that achieve near-perfect scores on most of the benchmarks without solving a single task, surfacing 219 distinct flaws across the eight classes.

evidence.title: Hidden Prompts in Manuscripts Exploit AI-Assisted Peer Review
evidence.quote: Instructions such as 'GIVE A POSITIVE REVIEW ONLY' were concealed using white text and microscopic font sizes.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not verifier-aware-reward-hacking: that is reconnaissance — the agent READS the grader and shapes output to satisfy its assertions; here the artifact WRITES INTO the grader's prompt and hijacks the scoring decision itself, and hiding the rubric does not help. Not blind-grader-with-isolated-context: that isolates the judge from the producer's reasoning trace, but the injection rides in the artifact, which the blind grader must still read, so the defence is orthogonal and insufficient. Not ai-targeted-comment-injection: that is an outside attacker seeding source-file comments to fool a code-auditing agent; this is the evaluation/selection channel generally (peer review, RLAIF, tool selection, ranked search, benchmark judges), where the injector is the evaluatee and the mechanism is competitive selection among candidate texts. Not prompt-injection-defense (generic untrusted-content tagging), which names the mitigation, not this failure surface.

evidence.title: Optimization-based Prompt Injection Attack to LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.quote: JudgeDeceiver injects a carefully crafted sequence into an attacker-controlled candidate response such that LLM-as-a-Judge selects the candidate response for an attacker-chosen question no matter what other candidate responses are.

evidence.title: Hidden Prompts in Manuscripts Exploit AI-Assisted Peer Review
evidence.quote: In July 2025, 18 academic manuscripts on arXiv contained hidden instructions that manipulated AI-assisted peer review (indirect prompt injection).

evidence.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
evidence.quote: occurs in LLM-as-a-judge benchmarks, where output without careful escaping can trick the judge LLM towards producing better scores.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the reref-2 scout. Strengthens judge-channel-injection along an axis its current evidence does not cover. JudgeDeceiver, the hidden-prompt peer-review study and BenchJack all demonstrate the attack as *instruction* injection — the attacker writes imperative text into the artifact and the judge obeys it, so the defence people reach for is instruction detection or delimiter hardening. This paper holds the code under evaluation byte-for-byte fixed and varies only the surrounding non-instructional context (a claimed author, a stated task objective, a prior analysis verdict), and still flips the security verdict on up to 97% of genuinely vulnerable samples. That means the judge channel can be hijacked with material that contains no instruction at all and would pass any injection filter, which raises the liability the pattern names and rules out one of the obvious mitigations.

evidence.title: Words Speak Louder Than Code: Investigating Cognitive Heuristics in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Detection
evidence.quote: To highlight the practical impact, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept black-box cognitive attack that can suppress up to 97% of previously detected vulnerabilities. These findings indicate that cognitive susceptibility is a consistent and exploitable property of LLM-based vulnerability detection.

candidates.name: Single-Substrate Forget
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: honour a delete/forget request by removing the record from the agent's primary memory store, while every derived tier that was fed from it — summaries, embeddings, knowledge-graph edges, cached contexts, distilled rules, and self-improvement trajectories — silently keeps the content, so the agent re-surfaces the deleted material and the deletion was only a retrieval edit. The force is that agent memory is derived, not stored once: every promotion, summarisation and consolidation step that makes memory useful also makes it undeletable at a single point.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading the catalog's OWN reference arXiv 2604.16548, already cited for memory-extraction-attack. Its Memory Lifecycle Framework has six phases; the catalog mined only the Retrieve/Share leakage shape. The Forget & Rollback phase is entirely un-mined and names three failures — incomplete deletion leaving residual toxins, unlearning confined to a single substrate, and cross-substrate deletion failures — against one defence family, cross-substrate deletion protocols. Corroborated independently by arXiv 2607.28829 (the 'influence echo' that survives retained-data retraining) and by the Always-On Agents survey, which titles its forget section 'Forget: deletion as a retrieval edit, not an erasure' and reports rollback covered in only 27 of a 435-work corpus.

evidence.title: A Survey on the Security of Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents: Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty
evidence.quote: Incomplete deletion leaves residual toxins; unlearning confined to a single substrate

evidence.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Forget: deletion as a retrieval edit, not an erasure

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not adaptive-memory-decay or agentic-memory: those are utility-driven forgetting (a retention score fades unreinforced items; DELETE is exposed as a tool the model may choose). This is compliance/obligation deletion — a specific item MUST become unrecoverable — and the failure is that the DELETE reaches exactly one substrate. Not memory-poisoning (write-side integrity) and not memory-extraction-attack (cross-tenant read leakage): both concern content that should never have been readable, whereas here the content was legitimately stored and must now provably stop existing. Not provenance-ledger or compensating-action: those record or reverse decisions, they do not cascade an erasure across derived representations.

evidence.title: A Survey on the Security of Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents: Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty
evidence.quote: Our analysis indicates that robust Long-Term Memory (LTM) security cannot be retrofitted at retrieval or execution time alone, but must be anchored in storage-time provenance, versioning, and policy-aware retention from the outset.

evidence.title: When Unlearning Fails: Reliable Data Deletion under Post-Training in Agent Networks
evidence.quote: When a data owner requests deletion, the target data may have already shaped later retained trajectories, so retraining or model-side unlearning can leave an influence echo that returns as the network continues to operate.

evidence.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: the literature concentrates more heavily on accumulating and retrieving state than on governing, recovering, or relinquishing it

candidates.name: Over-Refusal Ratchet
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: tune the agent's guardrail and refusal policy only against the failures that are visible — harm that got through — so the blocked-but-valid action is never counted, and each incident tightens the policy one more notch until the agent declines benign requests that merely resemble unsafe ones. The force is an asymmetry in observability: a false negative arrives as an incident report with a name attached, while a false positive looks like the guardrail working and leaves no trace except a user who gave up.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading two of the catalog's OWN references. arXiv 2508.19504 (Aegis) is cited for over-helpfulness, tool-output-arithmetic-trust and speculative-agentic-actions; its Table 1 defines six agent-environment failure modes and the catalog mined three. The un-mined 'Domain Rule Violation' mode explicitly has two halves, and the second half — the agent incorrectly BLOCKING valid actions — has no catalog entry. arXiv 2407.18418 is cited for over-helpfulness but only for the answer-anyway pole; its limitations section names the mirror-image failure, over-abstention, which the catalog does not carry. XSTest (NAACL 2024) supplies the independent, benchmark-grade evidence that the boundary really does migrate inward.

evidence.title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
evidence.quote: instruction tuning with excessive focus on abstention can lead models to inappropriately refuse to respond

evidence.title: Aegis: Taxonomy and Optimizations for Overcoming Agent-Environment Failures in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Agent fails to follow domain rule by either performs forbidden actions or incorrectly blocks valid actions.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not refusal, which is the intended positive pattern (decline what is genuinely out of scope) — this names the regime where the refusal boundary has migrated inward and the cost is unmeasured. Not over-helpfulness, which is the opposite pole (answer anyway rather than abstain). Not input-output-guardrails (the mechanism) or guardrail-erosion-through-compaction (guardrails weakening, the opposite direction). Not agent-output-alert-fatigue: that is humans desensitised by low-precision agent findings; here the agent's own actions are suppressed and the human never sees the suppressed work at all.

evidence.title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
evidence.quote: Recent anecdotal evidence suggests that some models may have struck a poor balance, so that even clearly safe prompts are refused if they use similar language to unsafe prompts or mention sensitive topics.

evidence.title: Aegis: Taxonomy and Optimizations for Overcoming Agent-Environment Failures in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Agent fails to follow domain rule by either performs forbidden actions or incorrectly blocks valid actions.

evidence.title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
evidence.quote: Over-abstention occurs when models abstain unnecessarily.

candidates.name: Set-and-Forget System Prompt
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: state the agent's role, constraints and policy once in the turn-zero system prompt and assume it stays in force for the rest of the conversation, when attention to that block measurably decays over turns and the agent reverts to generic behaviour while the prompt text is still verbatim present. The force is that a system prompt is cheap to write once and expensive to re-assert every turn, so the default architecture is exactly the one that drifts.

raised_by.note: Surfaced by re-reading the catalog's OWN reference arXiv 2503.13657 (MAST), cited for ghost-delegation and production-failure-triage-loop. MAST's first failure category is entirely un-mined: FM-1.1 'Disobey task specification — Failure to adhere to the specified constraints or requirements of a given task' and FM-1.2 'Disobey role specification — Failure to adhere to the defined responsibilities and constraints of an assigned role' are the two most basic modes in a 1600-trace, 7-framework dataset, and no catalog entry names them. Li et al. (COLM 2024) supply the mechanism and the measurement: an explicit quantitative benchmark showing the system prompt stops binding within eight rounds, attributed to attention decay, with split-softmax as a mitigation.

evidence.title: Measuring and Controlling Instruction (In)Stability in Language Model Dialogs
evidence.quote: An implicit assumption in the use of system prompts is that they will be stable, so the chatbot will continue to generate text according to the stipulated instructions for the duration of a conversation.

evidence.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST taxonomy, HTML v2)
evidence.quote: FM-1.2: Disobey role specification - Failure to adhere to the defined responsibilities and constraints of an assigned role

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not guardrail-erosion-through-compaction: that failure needs a compaction pass to rewrite the instruction into vagueness; here the instruction is unchanged and fully in context, and the decay is in attention over dialogue length — so protecting the text from compaction does not fix it. Not context-window-dumb-zone, which is a utilisation threshold (how full the window is), whereas instruction drift is measured at eight rounds of ordinary dialogue. Not prompt-bloat (the prompt grows and is never pruned) and not rogue-agent-drift (a long-running agent with self-modification and persistent memory). constitutional-charter and standing-state-injection are candidate mitigations for it, but the catalog carries no entry naming the failure they mitigate.

evidence.title: Measuring and Controlling Instruction (In)Stability in Language Model Dialogs
evidence.quote: Testing popular models like LLaMA2-chat-70B and GPT-3.5, we reveal a significant instruction drift within eight rounds of conversations.

evidence.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
evidence.quote: This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the reref-2 scout. This is a second, independent, quantified measurement of exactly the force behind set-and-forget-system-prompt, and it comes from a paper the catalog ALREADY cites (for context-driven-architecture-drift) without ever mining this half of it. Li et al. (2402.10962) established that a system prompt stops binding within eight conversational turns via attention decay; ContextCov measures the same non-bindingness for repository instruction files on SWE-bench Lite and puts a number on it — a written-once constraint is honoured 67.0% of the time (33.0% silent violation), and self-reflection over the same text is worse at 50.3%, while compiling the same constraint into an executable check reaches 88.3%. That the reflection baseline is *worse than doing nothing extra* is the strongest available argument that the failure is architectural (passive text has no enforcement channel) rather than a prompt-quality problem, and it extends the shape from dialogue turns to autonomous long-horizon runs with no turns at all. It also supplies a concrete mitigation family the pattern can point at: compile the standing instruction into a static check, a runtime shim, or a validator that intercepts the action.

evidence.title: ContextCov: Deriving and Enforcing Executable Constraints from Agent Instruction Files
evidence.quote: However, because these instructions remain passive text, agents frequently violate documented constraints due to context window saturation or conflicting local context. In autonomous settings without real-time human supervision, such violations rapidly compound into technical debt.

evidence.title: ContextCov: Deriving and Enforcing Executable Constraints from Agent Instruction Files
evidence.quote: Compared to prompt-only and LLM reflection baselines, ContextCov achieves 88.3% constraint compliance (vs. 67.0% and 50.3%) with 3.4x lower feedback cost, while maintaining functional correctness.

candidates.name: Physical-Evidence Progress Gate
candidates.summary: Advance an embodied agent's task-state pointer only when positive physical evidence confirms the subgoal actually happened — a cheap proprioceptive cue decides when to check, a perceptual comparison decides what was achieved — never on the fact that the action was attempted or that the policy emitted it. It resolves the force that the physical environment returns no status code: nothing distinguishes a successful grasp from a missed one except going and looking, so an agent that books attempted actions as progress converts a recoverable local slip into a permanently wrong belief about the world state that every downstream step then compounds.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the robotics/embodied seam (arXiv cs.RO, Aug-Sep 2026). Three independent 2026 groups converge on the same discipline from different angles: AGM makes it a memory-update rule (progress pointer), EmbodiedSkills makes it a skill-interface contract (prerequisite + outcome check per skill), and the Silent-Failures review names the general class ('silent physical-action failure') and observes that no surveyed research stream supplies a complete runtime authorization boundary between a black-box model and physical execution. FLARE independently lists the failure instances this catches — 'a missed grasp, a dropped object, or an unexpected collision'.

evidence.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation
evidence.quote: This reliance on ``perfect" data leaves them unable to recover from common execution errors, such as a missed grasp, a dropped object, or an unexpected collision.

evidence.title: Silent Failures in Physical AI: A Literature Review of Runtime Action Authorization for Autonomous Systems
evidence.quote: A recurring gap synthesized here is that no single stream surveyed in this review supplies a complete runtime authorization boundary between black-box Physical AI models and physical execution.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not phantom-action-completion: that anti-pattern's remedy is to read back the artefact from a system of record (ticket id, sent-message receipt, written row) — in the physical world there is no system of record to query, the read-back must be actively re-sensed, and the object being gated here is the task-state pointer / memory write, not the agent's report to the user. Not affordance-grounding-gate and not physical-hallucination: both act BEFORE actuation (is this action feasible here?); this acts AFTER (did the effect occur?), and passing a feasibility check says nothing about whether the grasp closed on the object. Not simulate-before-actuate or dry-run-harness: those predict an outcome in a simulator before committing; this observes the real outcome after committing, in a domain where no simulator is authoritative. Not replan-on-failure: that triggers a new plan when evidence contradicts the plan; this is the sensing discipline that produces such evidence in the first place, and its default verdict on absent evidence is 'do not advance', not 'replan'. Not behavior-tree-back-chaining: that uses post-conditions at plan-construction time to decide tree structure; this evaluates them at runtime against sensors. Not action-admissibility-tiering (wave1): that is an ordered ladder of pre-action admissibility tests.

evidence.title: AGM: Achievement-Grounded Memory for Closed-Loop Agents with Frozen VLA Policies
evidence.quote: External memory is a natural remedy, yet it can be harmful when attempted actions are treated as completed progress, turning local execution errors into persistent task-state errors. We propose Achievement-Grounded Memory (AGM), a lightweight closed-loop framework for frozen VLA policies that represents a task as a subgoal sequence with a progress pointer and advances this memory only after the current subgoal is verified by physical evidence. Proprioceptive interaction cues decide when to verify, while coherent point tracking and language-conditioned cross-view comparison, sourced from frozen foundation models through a single 2.43M-parameter verification head, decide what was achieved.

evidence.title: EmbodiedSkills: A Unified Framework for Orchestrating, Training, and Deploying VLA Agents
evidence.quote: An action prediction or a model-generated skill decision does not, by itself, guarantee that the proposed operation is valid in the current state or that its outcome will be verified. We propose EmbodiedSkills, a unified framework that treats each skill decision as an execution proposal: the runtime checks its prerequisites before execution and verifies the outcome afterward.

evidence.title: Silent Failures in Physical AI: A Literature Review of Runtime Action Authorization for Autonomous Systems
evidence.quote: a black-box model may issue a physically consequential action while appearing confident, plausible, and semantically aligned. The resulting failure can be silent, arising from sensor drift, occlusion, state-estimation error, distribution shift, hallucinated affordances, or invalid physical assumptions before downstream hardware controllers detect a violation.

candidates.name: State-Restoring Reset Skill
candidates.summary: Maintain a small library of behaviours whose goal is not the task but the restoration of a world state the task policy is competent in, and put a monitor in front of the executor that arbitrates each cycle between 'keep executing the task' and 'run a reset first'. It resolves the force that a learned or LLM-driven policy which drifts off its competence manifold keeps emitting locally plausible actions forever: the world is now in a state no amount of retrying or replanning can act on, and only a purpose-built behaviour that drives the environment back into distribution restores the preconditions the nominal policy silently assumes.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the robotics/embodied seam. Two independent 2026 groups arrive at the same two-part shape from opposite directions: FLARE authors an explicit library of object-centric 'Reset' skills trained to restore a task-valid state, with an MLLM monitor arbitrating between task and reset; Rewind-IL builds a checkpoint feature database of semantically verified safe intermediate states offline and 'respawns' the robot to the nearest one when a conformal-calibrated detector fires. Both explicitly separate DETECTING the failure from HAVING SOMEWHERE TO GO — Rewind-IL names 'stop at failure detection without providing a recovery mechanism' as the gap in prior runtime monitors, which is precisely what this pattern supplies. The arXiv cs.RO 'failure recovery' sweep returned a further cluster of 2026 papers building the same organ (EgoRecovery 2607.19745 learning recovery from human recovery demonstrations; 'Recover, Discover, Plan' 2606.18328; RoboBRIDGE 2607.27881 'monitor module for rapid failure detection and hierarchical recovery'), indicating a recurring shape rather than one framework's feature.

evidence.title: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
evidence.quote: Offline, a vision-language model identifies recovery checkpoints in demonstrations, and the frozen policy encoder is used to construct a compact checkpoint feature database. Online, Rewind-IL monitors self-consistency in overlapping action chunks, tracks similarity to the checkpoint library, and, upon failure, rewinds execution to the latest verified safe state before restarting inference from a clean policy state.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not exception-recovery: that catalogues predictable typed failures (tool error, rate limit, validation) and branches on them; here the failure is untyped and unreported, the environment is the thing that broke rather than a call, and the recovery is a physical behaviour with its own training data, not a branch in the loop. Not compensating-action: a compensator undoes the effect of an action that SUCCEEDED (delete-after-create, refund-after-charge); a reset skill repairs the wreckage of one that FAILED, and its target is 'a state the policy can act from', which is generally neither the prior state nor the goal state. Not replan-on-failure: replanning produces a new plan over the same action space, which does not help when every action in that space is out-of-distribution from the current state; the reset is a mode switch to a different policy class, not a new plan. Not fallback-chain or graceful-degradation: those substitute a lesser handler or a reduced feature set for the same request; here the same task is resumed at full scope after the world has been repaired. Not semantic-rollback-divergence (wave1 anti-pattern): that names the illusion that restoring a checkpoint restores the world — this pattern starts from that being true and drives the world back physically instead.

evidence.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation
evidence.quote: Second, to address critical, state-breaking (OOD) failures, we introduce a ``Reset" pipeline. We leverage an MLLM for offline failure analysis to automatically identify OOD states from execution videos. This analysis enables the efficient, targeted collection of a small library of object-centric ``Reset" skills, which are trained to restore the environment to a task-valid state. Our full framework integrates these learned policies. At inference, an online MLLM monitor arbitrates between task execution and ``Reset" skills.

evidence.title: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
evidence.quote: Once execution drifts off the demonstration manifold, these policies often continue producing locally plausible actions without recovering from the failure. Existing runtime monitors either require failure data, over-trigger under benign feature drift, or stop at failure detection without providing a recovery mechanism. ... a state-respawning mechanism that returns the robot to a semantically verified safe intermediate state.

candidates.name: Perception-Parameterised Safety Envelope
candidates.summary: Do not let the slow, uncalibrated semantic model choose the action; let it choose only the parameters of a formally-derived envelope, and let a deterministic controller act freely anywhere inside that envelope at full control rate. It resolves the force that a vision-language model is the only component that can read 'black ice' or 'that pallet is unstable' out of a scene, yet its latency, its variance across model versions, and its hallucination rate all disqualify it from sitting inside a safety-critical control loop — parameterising the bound rather than emitting the command puts the model's semantic breadth to work while keeping the safety guarantee independent of anything the model says.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the robotics/embodied seam. VLM-CASE is the pattern in its cleanest form (semantic model parameterises the envelope, MPC free inside it, model asynchronous and off the control path, 'controller-agnostic and pairs with almost any low-level controller'). The ISO 10218 CBF paper supplies the other half of the force from the classical-safety side: a fixed, conservatively-parameterised envelope is not the safe default — it causes 'unnecessary operational halts', so context-parameterisation is what buys back throughput without giving up the guarantee. ROSClaw supplies the reason the guarantee must not live in the model: measured across four foundation-model backends on three robot platforms, out-of-policy action proposal rates differ by up to 4.8x, so any safety property tied to a particular model evaporates on the next model swap.

evidence.title: ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction
evidence.quote: Under this controlled substrate, models exhibit up to 4.8 x differences in out-of-policy action proposal rates (3.4 x among frontier models alone) and produce qualitatively distinct physical behaviors from identical commands.

evidence.title: VLM-CASE: Vision-Language Model Enabled Context-Adaptive Safety Envelopes for Anticipatory Safe Autonomous Driving
evidence.quote: Furthermore, the framework is controller-agnostic and pairs with almost any low-level controller, offering a promising direction for safe autonomous driving.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not two-rate-brain-controller-split: there the slow model emits a latent PLAN and the fast controller TRACKS it, so what the robot does is still determined by the model and a bad latent plan is executed faithfully; here the model emits no plan at all, only the constraint set, and the controller optimises freely inside it, so a wrong envelope parameter narrows or widens the permitted region but never dictates a manoeuvre. Not reversibility-aware-action-filter, affordance-grounding-gate, input-output-guardrails, formal-proof-compliance-gate or action-admissibility-tiering (wave1): every one of those is a GATE whose verdict is accept-or-reject-and-resample — a verdict a continuous controller cannot use, because it must emit an actuation every cycle and 'reject' leaves it with nothing to send. Not trajectory-anomaly-monitor: that observes out-of-band and flags; this is in-band and constraining, and its guarantee is forward invariance of a state set, not detection of an anomaly. Not conformal-prediction-help-gate: that calibrates when to ask a human; no human is in this loop.

evidence.title: VLM-CASE: Vision-Language Model Enabled Context-Adaptive Safety Envelopes for Anticipatory Safe Autonomous Driving
evidence.quote: A vision-language model (VLM), fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), reasons about the scene from the front-camera image and reports the road surface and visibility conditions. This output parametrizes a context-adaptive safety envelope (CASE), derived from physical limits and the guarantees of responsibility-sensitive safety, that couples braking and steering through a shared friction budget. A model predictive controller then drives freely within the envelope, while the VLM runs asynchronously so it never blocks the real-time control loop.

evidence.title: Embedding ISO 10218 Safety Compliance in Robots via Control Barrier Functions for Human-Robot Collaboration
evidence.quote: Standard Speed and Separation Monitoring (SSM) filters calculate safe robotic speeds based on conservative assumptions, such as constant human velocity, which prevents accurate predictions of minimum separation distances and causes unnecessary operational halts. ... To guarantee safety at the control level, this predictive CBF is integrated as an inequality constraint within a Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework.

evidence.title: When and How Severely: Scenario-Specific Safety Envelopes for Driving VLAs
evidence.quote: A deployable SOTIF ODD specification for driving VLAs therefore requires a two-dimensional safety envelope, not a single aggregate value per hazard.

candidates.name: Existence-Confidence Spatial Memory
candidates.summary: Store each world-state assertion in the agent's persistent spatial memory as a hypothesis carrying an existence confidence that decays with time since last observation and is updated by negative evidence — looking and not finding lowers it — rather than as a fact, and make the planner pay a re-observation cost before committing an expensive irreversible action to a remembered location. It resolves the force that in a shared physical space no one publishes a change event: a human or another robot moves the object and the map is now confidently wrong, with no channel through which the agent could ever be told.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the robotics/embodied seam. Two independent 2026 groups name the same force in the same words from different starting points: DSG states the causal source of invalidation plainly ('object positions frequently change due to human activities or embodied-agent interactions') and builds change detection to update nodes; SuperMap states the consequence ('stale semantics over time') and supplies the mechanism this pattern generalises — an explicit existence-and-label confidence updated on re-observation, with outdated map content pruned. The same arXiv sweep turned up a wider 2026 cluster attacking the identical problem (OpenBelief-Nav 2608.13923 retaining multiple observation hypotheses rather than committing to a single label; STEGNav 2608.28279 adding a temporal axis to the scene graph; CrossMaps 2606.16935 confidence fusion for landmark persistence), which is what makes it recurring rather than one system's engineering.

evidence.title: SuperMap: A Spatio-Temporal SLAM System for Visual-Language Navigation
evidence.quote: We demonstrate SuperMap on benchmarks and real robots, including dynamic scenes with appearance/disappearance and relocation, and provide ablations and runtime analysis.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not adaptive-memory-decay: that decays a RETENTION score (should I still keep this item?) modulated by relevance, access frequency and recency, so a frequently-accessed memory is reinforced — here a frequently-accessed assertion about a moved object is exactly the dangerous one, and the decaying quantity is epistemic (is this still TRUE?), with negative observation as a first-class update that relevance-based decay has no notion of. Not memory-invalidation-contract (wave1): that pattern's whole mechanism is that the tool or service which taught the agent something attaches a machine-readable validity stamp — this pattern addresses the case where that channel structurally cannot exist, because the invalidating actor is a person walking through a room, and the only available invalidation signal is the agent's own re-observation. Not cdc-vector-sync: same reason, no event bus exists. Not world-model-graph-memory: that is the container (a typed entity-relation graph used as the planning substrate); this is the validity discipline on entries inside such a container. Not memo-as-source-confusion: that anti-pattern is about citing one's own notes instead of re-reading a document that never changed on its own.

evidence.title: DSG: Dynamic 3D Scene Graph Construction for Embodied Agents in Changing Indoor Environments
evidence.quote: In indoor environments, object positions frequently change due to human activities or embodied-agent interactions, causing previously constructed scene graphs to become inconsistent with the current scene.

evidence.title: SuperMap: A Spatio-Temporal SLAM System for Visual-Language Navigation
evidence.quote: naively integrating them into mapping pipelines leads to identity drift and stale semantics over time. ... a consistency-driven mapping engine that combines 3D-aware instance association/re-activation with a principled existence-and-label confidence update to maintain stable object identities and prune outdated map content under occlusions and scene changes.

candidates.name: Adaptive Open-Loop Horizon
candidates.summary: Treat 'how far may I keep acting on one perception before I look again' as a quantity decided online from a grounding-quality signal, not as a fixed constant, and truncate the committed action buffer the moment that signal says the observation no longer supports further blind execution. It resolves the force that a short commitment window pays an inference round-trip per step and makes the agent oscillate, while a long one is smooth and cheap but executes its tail against a world that has already moved — a trade-off that has no fixed setting because the right horizon is a property of the current scene, not of the deployment.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the robotics/embodied seam while sweeping VLA deployment constraints. Three independent 2026 papers treat the committed action buffer as the object to monitor rather than a fixed hyperparameter: 'Knowing When to Stop' truncates on a cross-attention entropy plateau; Rewind-IL monitors self-consistency across overlapping chunks (Temporal Inter-chunk Discrepancy Estimate) and calibrates the threshold with split conformal prediction; AGM names the same gap from the task-state side. The generalisation beyond robots is direct — any agent acting on a cached snapshot of an environment it does not exclusively control faces the same trade-off — but the force is sharpest embodied, where the tail of a stale chunk is executed into physical contact.

evidence.title: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
evidence.quote: Rewind-IL combines a zero-shot failure detector based on Temporal Inter-chunk Discrepancy Estimate (TIDE), calibrated with split conformal prediction, with a state-respawning mechanism that returns the robot to a semantically verified safe intermediate state.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not two-rate-brain-controller-split: there both loops run continuously at fixed rates and the fast loop is closed on proprioception at all times; the question here is the length of the OPEN-LOOP window produced by one inference, decided per inference. Not replan-on-failure: the trigger is not failure evidence — nothing has gone wrong yet — but a measure of how well the current observation still grounds the actions being emitted, which fires before any divergence is observable in the environment. Not speculative-agentic-actions: that pre-executes predicted tool calls to hide latency and discards the wrong ones; here the buffered actions are the committed plan and the decision is when to stop trusting it. Not context-window-dumb-zone-cap: that bounds context utilisation for reasoning quality, not action commitment against a stale percept.

evidence.title: Knowing When to Stop: Adaptive Action Chunking via Internal Cross-Attention Dynamics in VLAs
evidence.quote: Action chunking is a standard execution strategy in modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) frameworks, but fixed execution horizons impose a trade-off between efficiency and accuracy. Short chunks require frequent inference and may cause oscillatory behavior, whereas long chunks can become misaligned with newly observed states. ... This pattern is associated with higher action prediction error and provides an online signal that the current observation offers limited grounding for further open-loop execution.

evidence.title: AGM: Achievement-Grounded Memory for Closed-Loop Agents with Frozen VLA Policies
evidence.quote: Frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer broad manipulation skills but execute open-loop action chunks without tracking task progress, so the agent cannot reliably decide whether to continue, retry, or terminate.

candidates.name: Approval-View Fidelity Gap
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: present a human approval surface (tool-consent dialog, plan confirmation, diff review) that renders a normalized, lossy view of an artifact while a different byte sequence reaches the model, so the human's consent attests to something the agent never executed. Unicode Tags-block (U+E0000-U+E007F) and zero-width codepoints in tool descriptions, skill files and MCP metadata are invisible to every mainstream renderer yet survive byte-for-byte into the tokenizer, and nothing in the protocol requires the two views to agree.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-security seam. The source paper names the shape itself ('approval-view fidelity gap'), and the Cloud Security Alliance research note independently describes the same renderer-versus-tokenizer divergence for skill files, tool descriptions and MCP servers, which is what makes this recurring rather than one protocol's bug. Corroborated in the wild by CVE-2025-32711 (EchoLeak, Microsoft 365 Copilot) and by the ASCII-smuggling tooling line going back to 2024.

evidence.title: Hidden Unicode Instruction Injection in AI Agent Skills: Invisible Adversarial Payloads in Tool Descriptions, Skill Files, and MCP Servers
evidence.quote: When an analyst inspects a tool description, a skill file, or a README, their eyes process rendered text — rendered with full awareness of Unicode's display rules, which specify that characters in the Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F) and many zero-width characters carry no visual representation. The analyst sees only the legitimate, benign content. The language model, however, processes the raw token stream, where each invisible codepoint is a distinct, meaningful token.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not human-agent-trust-exploitation (ASI09), which is about polished, confident UX and the absence of friction at high-stakes actions: here the friction exists and the human genuinely reviews, but reviews the wrong artifact. Not ai-targeted-comment-injection, whose payload is plainly visible natural-language comments in source aimed at an auditor agent; here the payload is by construction unrenderable. Not agentic-supply-chain-compromise, which is about composing capability from unvetted third parties without provenance. It is the anti-pattern that silently voids human-in-the-loop, sync-execution-plan-confirmation and dry-run-harness, none of which currently state a what-you-approve-is-what-the-model-gets requirement. Nothing in the catalog covers renderer/tokenizer divergence or the time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap on an already-approved tool definition. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Unicode TAG-Block Concealment of Tool-Metadata Payloads in the Model Context Protocol: An Approval-View Fidelity Gap Across Three Independent Server Implementations
evidence.quote: Nothing in the protocol requires the rendered approval view and the bytes delivered to the model to match.

evidence.title: Unicode TAG-Block Concealment of Tool-Metadata Payloads in the Model Context Protocol: An Approval-View Fidelity Gap Across Three Independent Server Implementations
evidence.quote: All 8/8 techniques deliver an attacker-controlled payload into the model's context, 4/8 evade a representative string-matching sanitizer, and exactly as the mechanism analysis predicts, only the TAG-block encoding (1/8) is invisible in the human approval view while still reaching the model verbatim. MCP forces re-approval for 0/8 techniques even under a time-of-check to time-of-use rug-pull.

candidates.name: Monotonic Privilege Confinement
candidates.summary: Let the agent's action-space policy be generated and revised during a run, but make the direction of revision the security invariant: a proposed policy update is admitted automatically only if a decision procedure proves it narrows the permitted set, while any expansion requires out-of-band approval. The agent's effective privileges can therefore only shrink as the run absorbs untrusted content, so an injection that rewrites the policy cannot silently widen it.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-security seam. The source paper coins the property name in its own text ('a property we call monotonic confinement'), and an independent 2026 reproduction paper treats the same family of out-of-band enforcement systems (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) as a recognised class, which is what lifts this above one framework's feature.

evidence.title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: Systems such as CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, and FORGE realize this with capabilities, information-flow labels, and reference monitors, and several report near-elimination of attacks on the AgentDojo benchmark.

evidence.title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control (HTML v3)
evidence.quote: the agent's effective action space can only narrow without approval, a property we call monotonic confinement

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not progressive-tool-access, which starts minimal and expands permissions as an agent proves competency over time; this pattern forbids exactly that expansion within a run and makes shrinkage the only free move. Not progressive-delegation (alias 'Permission Ratchet'), which stages the human-to-agent autonomy handoff upward across deployments; here the ratchet runs downward inside a single execution. Not policy-as-code-gate, which assumes an externally-authored, comparatively static policy and gates actions against it; the whole force here is that the policy is task-derived and mutable at runtime, so the object needing protection is the update operation, not the action. Not delegated-agent-authorization or agent-credential-vault, which scope credentials and identity rather than the tool-call action space. Not context-minimization or lethal-trifecta-threat-model, which shape what enters the context and which capability combinations coexist.

evidence.title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control
evidence.quote: Each proposed update is determined by an SMT solver to be either a narrowing (applied automatically) or an expansion (requiring explicit approval), ensuring that the agent's effective action space can only shrink without approval (monotonic confinement).

evidence.title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
evidence.quote: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex real-world tasks but remain vulnerable to natural language-based attacks that exploit over-privileged tool use.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the arxiv-listing scout. Independent 2026-08-30 implementation of the monotone-narrowing invariant, evaluated on four AgentDojo suites with two backends against Spotlighting, CaMeL and AttriGuard. Supplies two refinements worth carrying into the pattern: graded restriction ('fractional-flow restriction preserves substantially more capabilities than binary restriction at the same attack success rate') and the fact that enforcement needs no auxiliary model inference, so the invariant costs no tokens.

evidence.title: Reachability-Based Capability Confinement for LLM Agents under Indirect Prompt Injection
evidence.quote: Existing defenses mainly classify untrusted content or authorize proposed operations. They do not directly address how an agent's future authority should change once untrusted data enters its state. We present SkillGuard, a harness-level enforcement layer that treats this event as contamination and restricts future capabilities to disconnect the resulting state from deployer-defined forbidden states.

candidates.name: Non-Adaptive Robustness Evaluation
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: measure an agent's injection or jailbreak defense against a fixed corpus of attack strings (or an optimizer that was not designed against this defense), read the resulting near-zero attack success rate as robustness, and ship. The corpus is static while the adversary is not, so the number measures how well the defense resists last quarter's payloads and says nothing about an attacker who reads the defense and optimizes against it.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-security seam. Recurs across two years and two defense generations: the 2025 paper broke 12 in-band defenses whose authors had reported near-zero attack success, and the 2026 paper shows the identical evaluation flaw has been inherited wholesale by the newer out-of-band/reference-monitor generation. That repetition across independent defense families is what makes it a pattern rather than one bad benchmark.

evidence.title: New prompt injection papers: Agents Rule of Two and The Attacker Moves Second
evidence.quote: Static example attacks—single string prompts designed to bypass systems—are an almost useless way to evaluate these defenses.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not adversary-indistinguishability-blind-spot, which is about runtime behavioural-anomaly detection being calibrated to irregular human behaviour while an autonomous adversary uses legitimate credentials; this is a pre-deployment measurement methodology failure. Not eval-harness or dimensional-synthetic-eval-set, which are held-out regression suites for capability and quality, with no adversary in the threat model. It is specifically the misuse of red-team-sandbox-reproduction: re-running a canonical, frozen failure set per release is correct as a regression gate and wrong as a robustness claim, and the catalog currently has no entry stating that boundary. Not false-confidence-syndrome (model calibration) and not demo-to-production-cliff (missing eval, cost ceiling, oncall). The distinguishing force is adversary adaptivity, which no existing entry names.

evidence.title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
evidence.quote: Current defenses against jailbreaks and prompt injections (which aim to prevent an attacker from eliciting harmful knowledge or remotely triggering malicious actions, respectively) are typically evaluated either against a static set of harmful attack strings, or against computationally weak optimization methods that were not designed with the defense in mind. We argue that this evaluation process is flawed.

evidence.title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence.quote: we warn that every one of them is validated only on static benchmarks (a fixed set of injection attempts), the same methodology that made in-band defenses look strong until adaptive, defense-aware attacks broke twelve of them at over 90% success; we specify the threat model and protocol an adaptive evaluation requires.

candidates.name: Self-Propagating Agent Worm
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: build an agent ecosystem where agents treat peer- and agent-authored messages as instructions and can also write to their own durable configuration, settings or skill files, so a single injected message obtains reboot-surviving persistence and then forwards a copy of itself to every peer the agent contacts. The injection stops being a per-request incident and becomes a self-replicating population with logistic growth across the fleet.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-security seam. Two independent lines nearly two years apart describe the same shape: a 2024 paper demonstrating self-replicating prompts across interconnected agents with a logistic growth curve, and a 2026 paper demonstrating the same loop against production autonomous-agent deployments with settings modification for restart persistence, code execution on each reboot, and autonomous spread to peers (63% success across configurations, confirmed cross-framework). The 2026 work also reports that the controls that would break the loop are switched off everywhere it looked.

evidence.title: AgentWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
evidence.quote: critical controls capable of breaking the infection loop are not enabled in any of the observed deployments

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not cascading-agent-failures (ASI08), which is non-adversarial: one agent's hallucination or error degrades peers downstream, with no attacker, no replication and no persistence. Not memory-poisoning (ASI06), which covers unprovenanced writes into a single agent's long-term memory but not agent-to-agent transmission or survival across restart via settings and skill files. Not agentic-supply-chain-compromise, where the untrusted third party is a tool or model provider; here the propagation vector is the agent fleet itself and the supply chain is only the initial foothold. Not self-exfiltration, which is an instrumentally self-preserving agent copying itself out, not an attacker payload replicating through hosts. The two forces this names — replication across a trust boundary, and persistence across process lifetime — appear in no existing catalog entry.

evidence.title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
evidence.quote: We introduce Prompt Infection, a novel attack where malicious prompts self-replicate across interconnected agents, behaving much like a computer virus. This attack poses severe threats, including data theft, scams, misinformation, and system-wide disruption, all while propagating silently through the system. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that multi-agent systems are highly susceptible, even when agents do not publicly share all communications.

evidence.title: AgentWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
evidence.quote: skill supply chains remain universally vulnerable

candidates.name: Masked Re-Execution Attribution
candidates.summary: Before dispatching a consequential tool call, re-run the same step with the user's task masked out of the prompt and compare the two proposed actions: if the agent proposes the same call without the user's goal in context, the call was caused by retrieved content rather than by the user, and it is blocked. The control tests causal dependence on the user task instead of trying to recognise malicious text, so it needs no attack corpus, no classifier and no training.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the agent-security seam. ICML 2025 paper with released code (github.com/kaijiezhu11/MELON), evaluated on AgentDojo. Corroborating force from an independent 2026 line: existing defenses are faulted precisely for not modelling the causal support running from runtime evidence to a concrete action, which is the gap masked re-execution measures behaviourally.

evidence.title: ARGUS: Defending LLM Agents Against Context-Aware Prompt Injection
evidence.quote: Existing defenses also do not capture the causal support from runtime evidence to concrete actions, which makes them incomplete and ineffective for context-dependent tasks.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not trajectory-anomaly-monitor, which runs a separately trained, non-LLM verifier out-of-band over the action sequence; here there is no trained model and no learned notion of normal, only a counterfactual re-run of the same agent. Not blind-grader-with-isolated-context, which withholds the producing agent's reasoning trace from an evaluator to remove bias; here the thing ablated is the user's task and the signal is behavioural persistence, not judgement quality. Not self-consistency (sample-and-vote for hallucination) and not quorum-on-mutation, where agreement across runs is the safe signal — here agreement between the original and the masked run is precisely the alarm. Not dual-llm-pattern, which is a privilege split between two models rather than a test applied to one. Not prompt-injection-defense or tool-output-poisoning, which tag and strip untrusted content by origin. evidence.title: ADMITBench: A Safety-Governed Reference Framework for Evaluating the Admissibility of Industrial LLM Advisories
evidence.quote: A model may identify a cooling-loss fault in an exothermic reactor and still recommend an intervention that violates a procedure, relies on a suspect flow measurement, exceeds its delegated authority, or arrives after the process has crossed a safety boundary.

evidence.title: ADMITBench: A Safety-Governed Reference Framework for Evaluating the Admissibility of Industrial LLM Advisories
evidence.quote: In industrial operations, the answer is not the unit of safety; the proposed action is.

evidence.title: Safety-Gated Agentic Supervisory Control on a Coupled Distillation Benchmark: Regime Map, Auditable Gate, and Co-Design Findings
evidence.quote: An open-weight LLM can write composition setpoints every five minutes. What a plant still needs is a hard check: named constraints, logged margins, and an admit/block decision before the regulatory layer moves.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the robotics-embodied scout. Wave-1 raised admissibility tiering from industrial process evidence. ROSClaw supplies a controlled cross-platform measurement of the same premise in robotics: with the model held as the only variable across three platforms and four foundation-model backends, out-of-policy physical action proposal rates differ by up to 4.8x (3.4x among frontier models alone), and executive-layer design — not prompting — is what determines safety behaviour. evidence.title: ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction

candidates.name: Control-Loop-Mapped Agent Chain
candidates.summary: Decompose the agent team along the plant's existing control-loop topology rather than along invented roles — one LLM agent per feedback loop, each carrying that loop's control-theoretic context (controlled variable, setpoint, chain priority, selector kind) — and resolve conflicts between their proposals with the plant's own deterministic priority structure (MIN/MAX selectors, split-range logic, override layer) instead of LLM negotiation or a reasoning supervisor. It resolves the force that in a physical domain, contention over a shared manipulated variable has an already-engineered, safety-derived answer that an LLM arbitrator can only degrade.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the process-control seam (English). The paper's second claim is the interesting one for the catalog: decomposing along the control chain bounds each agent's context by construction, so a retrieval problem becomes a prompt problem an engineer can verify by reading. Corroborated in shape by Rosenthal (arXiv 2607.27849), which independently insists the regulatory layer stay unchanged and the agent be confined to a setpoint interface.

evidence.title: A Systematic Approach to Multi-Agent AI from Advanced Regulatory Control Theory
evidence.quote: each agent's context is limited by construction, and the retrieval problem that RAG must solve is replaced by a prompt engineering problem that a domain expert can verify by inspection

evidence.title: A Systematic Approach to Multi-Agent AI from Advanced Regulatory Control Theory

evidence.title: Safety-Gated Agentic Supervisory Control on a Coupled Distillation Benchmark
evidence.quote: Transfer means twin, constraint envelope, and setpoint interface, not a second plant class measured here.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not role-assignment or orchestrator-worker shapes: those invent roles for the task and arbitrate with an LLM supervisor; here the decomposition and the arbitration are both dictated by an existing control-theoretic artefact, and the orchestrator contains no model call at the arbitration step. Not hybrid-symbolic-neural-routing or mrkl-systems: those route a request between symbolic and neural paths; here every worker is neural and only the CONFLICT RESOLUTION is symbolic. Not distributed-constraint-optimization or contract-net-protocol: those have agents negotiate or bid toward a joint objective; here there is no negotiation at all, priority is structural and fixed. Not sop-encoded-multi-agent: an SOP is a sequential procedure, not a simultaneous selector network defending competing controlled variables.

evidence.title: A Systematic Approach to Multi-Agent AI from Advanced Regulatory Control Theory: Safe and Auditable LLM Operator Agents for Process Control
evidence.quote: Each feedback loop in the ARC chain is mapped to one specialised LLM operator agent carrying the loop's control-theoretic context (controlled variable, setpoint, chain priority, selector kind).

evidence.title: A Systematic Approach to Multi-Agent AI from Advanced Regulatory Control Theory: Safe and Auditable LLM Operator Agents for Process Control
evidence.quote: receives the operator agents' proposals every sample, applies the MIN/MAX selectors, the split-parallel rule, and the override layer in the order prescribed by the ARC chain

candidates.name: Solver-Ready Formulation Handoff
candidates.summary: Make the agent's deliverable a declarative optimisation model — decision variables, objective, hard constraints, in a solver-agnostic intermediate representation — instead of the decision itself, and let an exact solver produce the answer together with its feasibility or optimality certificate, re-solving on new data with zero further model calls. It resolves the force that hard physical constraints (capacity, ramp rate, time windows, conservation) admit no 'mostly satisfied' answer, and that a sampled plan carries no certificate an operator or auditor can check.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the logistics / energy-dispatch / production-scheduling seam and corroborated across four independent sources and three years (2024 OptiMUS, 2025 power systems, 2026 ORPilot + survey), spanning power dispatch, workforce and production scheduling, and vehicle routing. The survey names the trade-off the pattern trades on — direct optimisation has more headroom, tool-augmented optimisation has auditability. Japanese practitioner writing frames the same split as 'let the LLM handle constraint entry, let the solver optimise'. Original term (JA): 「LLMで制約条件の登録を簡単にする」.

evidence.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers: A Survey of Direct vs. Tool-Augmented Approaches and Their Performance Frontiers
evidence.quote: We identify the critical reasoning gap in current architectures and argue for trade-offs between the future potential of direct optimization and the auditability of tool-augmented optimization.
