evidence.quote: LLMで制約条件の登録を簡単にする

evidence.title: From Natural Language to Solver-Ready Power System Optimization: An LLM-Assisted, Validation-in-the-Loop Framework
evidence.quote: enforces feasibility through systematic validation and iterative repair

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not code-execution / CodeAct: there the run IS the answer and the artefact is imperative code; here the artefact is a declarative model that is separately validated for feasibility, the solver rather than the execution is the authority, and re-solving requires no LLM. Not mrkl-systems: that dispatches a request to whichever expert module fits; here there is one fixed handoff and the LLM is structurally forbidden from emitting the decision. Not hybrid-symbolic-neural-routing: that chooses a symbolic OR a neural path per query; here both run, in a fixed producer/decider order. Not distributed-constraint-optimization: that is many agents jointly assigning shared variables; here one centralised exact solver decides.

evidence.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers: A Survey of Direct vs. Tool-Augmented Approaches and Their Performance Frontiers
evidence.quote: Direct optimization uses iterative prompting and heuristic generation to navigate solution spaces. Tool-augmented optimization translates natural language problems into formal specifications and orchestrates external solvers.

evidence.title: OptiMUS: Scalable Optimization Modeling with (MI)LP Solvers and Large Language Models
evidence.quote: Optimization problems are pervasive in sectors from manufacturing and distribution to healthcare. evidence.title: ORPilot: A Production-Oriented Agentic LLM-for-OR Tool for Optimization Modeling
evidence.quote: a solver-agnostic Intermediate Representation (IR) for deterministic, zero-LLM-call recompilation to Gurobi, CPLEX, PuLP, Pyomo, or OR-Tools solvers

evidence.title: From Natural Language to Solver-Ready Power System Optimization: An LLM-Assisted, Validation-in-the-Loop Framework

candidates.name: Independent-Reference Measurement Check
candidates.summary: Before an agent reasons over live process data, establish each measurement's credibility against references that are causally independent of it — not merely correlated with it — and correct or quarantine the conflicting readings. It resolves the force that biased, delayed, stale or derived values look entirely plausible in a plant historian, and that the obvious cross-check (a strongly correlated neighbouring tag) is worthless when the two share an instrument, a derived formula, a soft-sensing chain, or the same control action.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the process-industry sensor seam (English) and cross-checked against the classical data-validation-and-reconciliation literature (gross error detection via conservation-balance residuals), which supplies the same independence requirement without an LLM. The ADMITBench tier-1 finding ('relies on a suspect flow measurement') is independent corroboration that industrial agents fail here in practice. Japanese manufacturing writing states the enabling problem — plant data arrives from mixed-vendor equipment per process step and must be unified before anyone can reason over it. Original term (JA): 工程ごとに異なるメーカーの装置が混在.

evidence.title: ADMITBench: A Safety-Governed Reference Framework for Evaluating the Admissibility of Industrial LLM Advisories
evidence.quote: A model may identify a cooling-loss fault in an exothermic reactor and still recommend an intervention that violates a procedure, relies on a suspect flow measurement, exceeds its delegated authority, or arrives after the process has crossed a safety boundary.

evidence.title: 製造現場の知見を生かしてAIエージェントを活用するには（1/2）— 東芝 DiGiTAL CONVENTiON, 2026-03-06
evidence.quote: 工程ごとに異なるメーカーの装置が混在しているため、それらの情報を収集して一元的に捉える必要があること

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not physical-hallucination: that is an anti-pattern on the OUTPUT side (the agent emits an infeasible command); this is the INPUT side (the agent's percepts are physically inconsistent before it reasons). Not affordance-grounding-gate: that grounds a candidate ACTION against the current scene; this validates the observations themselves and never touches an action. Not self-consistency or cross-reflection: those sample the model repeatedly; here the corroborating evidence is external sensor data, and the pattern's substance is the independence criterion that decides which external tag is admissible as a reference at all. Not observability-fail-open: that is about the telemetry pipeline going silent, not about live readings that are present but untrustworthy. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: LLM-Guided Measurement Credibility Correction for Trustworthy Industrial Process Inference
evidence.quote: In field deployment, a predictor may receive biased, delayed, stale, or derived measurements that still look plausible. Prediction can then fail before the forecasting backbone becomes the main limitation, because the input window no longer represents the real process.

evidence.title: LLM-Guided Measurement Credibility Correction for Trustworthy Industrial Process Inference
evidence.quote: A correlated variable can also be an unsafe reference when variables share instruments, derived formulas, soft-sensing chains, or control actions. The key issue is to decide before prediction which external measurements can credibly support the current measurement.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the robotics-embodied scout. Wave-1 raised this from process-industry evidence (plant historians, soft sensors, correlated tags). This 2026 review independently generalises the same input-side force to robotics and VLA systems, naming sensor drift, occlusion and state-estimation error as sources of a failure that is silent precisely because the reading remains plausible, and observing that no surveyed research stream closes the gap. Extends the pattern's applicability from process control to embodied perception with a peer-surveyed source. The arXiv cs.RO sweep also surfaced two supporting 2026 results not fetched in full: 'Lost in Fog' (2605.21446), which establishes reasoning consistency as an indicator of VLA trajectory reliability under sensor perturbation, and a camera-only driving degradation benchmark (2608.29005) that distinguishes quality loss from outright deletion across 16 corruption families — both consistent with the pattern's claim that a degraded-but-present channel is the dangerous case.

evidence.title: Silent Failures in Physical AI: A Literature Review of Runtime Action Authorization for Autonomous Systems
evidence.quote: The resulting failure can be silent, arising from sensor drift, occlusion, state-estimation error, distribution shift, hallucinated affordances, or invalid physical assumptions before downstream hardware controllers detect a violation.

candidates.name: Counterexample-Guided Repair Loop
candidates.summary: Close the generation loop with an exhaustive verifier — a model checker or SMV-class tool run against a formal specification — and feed the concrete counterexample trace back as the repair signal, so that acceptance is a proof of specification conformance rather than a passed sample of tests. It resolves the force that in control code and other correctness-critical artefacts, a test suite that passes tells you nothing about the states it did not visit, while a counterexample tells the generator exactly which state sequence violates the spec.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the OT/ICS seam. Two independent groups (UC Irvine/Siemens and Zhejiang University) built the same loop for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text within a year of each other, and further 2026 work (SemaPLC, MPC-Coder) repeats the shape, so this is recurring rather than one lab's harness. LLM4PLC reports success rate 47% -> 72% and code-quality score 2.25/10 -> 7.75/10 when the verifier feedback is added. Flagged medium confidence because a reviewer may read it as a variant of critic; the load-bearing difference is exhaustiveness of the verifier and the counterexample as the repair signal.

evidence.title: Agents4PLC: Automating Closed-loop PLC Code Generation and Verification in Industrial Control Systems using LLM-based Agents
evidence.quote: this paper introduces Agents4PLC, a novel framework that not only automates PLC code generation but also includes code-level verification through an LLM-based multi-agent system

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not critic (Tool-Augmented Self-Correction / CRITIC): there external tools produce feedback, but the feedback is tool output over sampled inputs and acceptance is never a proof; here the verifier is complete over the state space and the repair signal is a witness trace. Not self-refine or reflexion: those consume self-generated critique. Not eval-as-contract: tests are the contract there, and test passage is sampling, not exhaustion. Not formal-proof-compliance-gate: that requires a proof to accompany a proposed ACTION at dispatch time and rejects deterministically — it is a runtime gate with no repair loop and no counterexample consumption; this is an authoring-time generate/verify/repair cycle over an artefact.

evidence.title: LLM4PLC: Harnessing Large Language Models for Verifiable Programming of PLCs in Industrial Control Systems
evidence.quote: We propose LLM4PLC, a user-guided iterative pipeline leveraging user feedback and external verification tools including grammar checkers, compilers and SMV verifiers to guide the LLM's generation.

evidence.title: Agents4PLC: Automating Closed-loop PLC Code Generation and Verification in Industrial Control Systems using LLM-based Agents
evidence.quote: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have made strides in automated code generation, they often fall short in providing correctness guarantees and specialized support for PLC programming.

candidates.name: Handback Lead-Time Budget
candidates.summary: When a continuously-running agent must return control of a moving physical process to a human, issue the takeover request at (time the process reaches its boundary minus predicted reacquisition time minus a buffer) and ship the state reconstruction the operator needs, rather than escalating at the moment the agent gives up. It resolves the force that a reliable agent keeps its supervisor out of the loop, so at the instant of escalation the human has the least situation awareness precisely when the most is required; escalating 'now' hands over a problem the human cannot yet see.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the vehicle/maritime/process-operations seam. The primary science is the conditionally-automated-driving takeover literature, which quantifies the budget; ADMITBench supplies the industrial-process version of the same failure ('arrives after the process has crossed a safety boundary'). German industrial-governance writing states the residual role that makes lead time matter: while liability is unresolved, human release remains the fallback level for consequential operations. Original term (DE): 'die menschliche Freigabe ... die Rückfallebene'. Marked medium because only one WebFetch-verified peer-style source directly measures the budget; the Endsley 'automation conundrum' literature (Human Factors, 2017) is the obvious second anchor but sagepub returned HTTP 403 and I will not cite what I could not open.

evidence.title: ADMITBench: A Safety-Governed Reference Framework for Evaluating the Admissibility of Industrial LLM Advisories
evidence.quote: Diagnosis addresses what may be happening. Operational decision support must also specify what is proposed, whether the available evidence supports it, who is permitted to act, and whether the action remains acceptable over the relevant process horizon.

evidence.title: Die Governance-Lücke im KI-Zeitalter — Saumitra Das, <kes> Informationssicherheit, 25.06.2026
evidence.quote: solange die Haftung ungeklärt ist, bleibt die menschliche Freigabe bei folgenreichen Operationen die Rückfallebene

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Not conversation-handoff: that transfers a conversation to a live human and the world is static while they read; here the process keeps moving during the transfer, which is what creates the time budget. Not mandatory-red-flag-escalation: that fires unconditionally and immediately on a trigger — this pattern is about firing EARLY, on a predicted boundary, with lead time as the design variable. Not human-in-the-loop or approval-queue: those block the agent pending approval; here nothing is blocked, the plant or vehicle continues. Not supervisor-cognitive-overload (an anti-pattern about attention split across parallel agents) and not agentic-skill-atrophy (long-run capability loss, not per-event reacquisition time). [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Adaptive Time Budgets for Safe and Comfortable Vehicle Control Transition in Conditionally Automated Driving
evidence.quote: This study introduces an adaptive time budget framework that dynamically allocates transition time by incorporating a predicted takeover time and a preferred takeover buffer (piecewise function).

evidence.title: Adaptive Time Budgets for Safe and Comfortable Vehicle Control Transition in Conditionally Automated Driving
evidence.quote: Results show that (i) takeover buffers of about 5-6 seconds consistently lead to optimal safety and comfort; and (ii) drivers prefer relatively stable takeover buffers across varying traffic densities and n-back tasks.

candidates.name: Elusion-Sampled Discard Validation
candidates.summary: When an agent's job is to narrow a corpus rather than to answer — responsiveness and privilege review, compliance screening, alert triage, candidate long-listing — validate the pile it threw away: draw a random sample from the discarded set, have humans adjudicate it, and estimate with a stated confidence bound how much relevant material eluded the filter. Accept or reject the run on that bound, not on spot-checking the material the agent kept.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the legal-practice / legal-ops seam (e-discovery, responsiveness and privilege review). The structural force is field-specific and then generalises: in discovery the producing party must DEFEND the adequacy of its narrowing to an adversary and to a court, so 'we looked at what we kept and it was good' is not an admissible argument — the only defensible artefact is a measured bound on what escaped. Lewis/Yang/Frieder (CIKM 2021, peer-reviewed) state plainly that heuristic stopping rules 'lack valid statistical guarantees, which has discouraged their use in some legal contexts'; Grossman & Cormack (Richmond J.L. & Tech., 2011) is the field's founding empirical paper and frames the review task as coding for responsiveness AND privilege over a whole collection. Same shape appears wherever an agent's discard is consequential and unobservable: benefits eligibility pre-screening, KYC alert suppression, resume long-listing, safety-report triage.

evidence.title: Certifying One-Phase Technology-Assisted Reviews (CIKM 2021)
evidence.quote: We further show theoretically and empirically that overshooting a recall target, which has been treated as innocuous or desirable in past evaluations of stopping rules, is a major source of excess cost in one-phase TAR workflows.

evidence.title: Technology-Assisted Review in E-Discovery Can Be More Effective and More Efficient Than Exhaustive Manual Review, XVII Rich. J.L. & Tech. 11 (2011)
evidence.quote: [T]here appears to be a myth that manual review by humans of large amounts of information is as accurate and complete as possible – perhaps even perfect – and constitutes the gold standard by which all searches should be measured.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. Nearest existing entries are verify-before-cite-gate (530), sampled-prompt-trace-eval (156), eval-harness (148) and blind-grader-with-isolated-context (505); nearest wave-1 claims are powered-eval-set and text-independent-completion-oracle. All of them inspect what the agent PRODUCED. This pattern inspects what the agent SILENTLY OMITTED, which is invisible to every output-side check: a corpus-narrowing agent that discards a responsive or privileged document emits nothing at all, so precision-style review of the retained set cannot detect the failure. It also cannot be handled by a held-out labelled eval set (powered-eval-set, eval-harness): the corpus is itself the deliverable and is different every matter, so the negative class has to be sampled at run time, per engagement, and the acceptance criterion is a recall interval on THIS corpus rather than a score on a fixed benchmark. sampled-prompt-trace-eval samples production traces the agent generated; here the sampling frame is the population the agent excluded.

evidence.title: Certifying One-Phase Technology-Assisted Reviews
evidence.quote: Technology-assisted review (TAR) workflows based on iterative active learning are widely used in document review applications. Most stopping rules for one-phase TAR workflows lack valid statistical guarantees, which has discouraged their use in some legal contexts. Drawing on the theory of quantile estimation, we provide the first broadly applicable and statistically valid sample-based stopping rules for one-phase TAR.

evidence.title: Technology-Assisted Review in E-Discovery Can Be More Effective and More Efficient Than Exhaustive Manual Review
evidence.quote: E-discovery processes that use automated tools to prioritize and select documents for review are typically regarded as potential cost-savers – but inferior alternatives – to exhaustive manual review, in which a cadre of reviewers assesses every document for responsiveness to a production request, and for privilege.

candidates.name: Escrowed-Attribute Impact Audit
candidates.summary: To make an agent that decides about people auditable for disparate impact, keep the protected attributes — but hold them in an escrow store that the decision path provably cannot read and that an independent auditor can, joining decisions to attributes only inside the audit boundary. Resolves the direct collision between 'the decision must not see the attribute' (disparate treatment, data minimisation, works-council and GDPR special-category limits) and 'someone must measure outcomes by attribute' (disparate impact, four-fifths testing, NYC-LL144-style annual independent bias audits).

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the HR / recruiting seam (resume screening, adverse-impact and four-fifths testing, NYC Local Law 144-style annual independent bias audits). Kilbertus et al. (ICML 2018) states the force pair in one sentence — attributes must not be considered to avoid disparate treatment, and must be examined to avoid disparate impact — and gives a concrete mechanism (secure multi-party computation over encrypted attributes) that is exactly an escrow. Andrus et al. (arXiv cs.CY, 38 practitioner interviews) supplies the recurring-across-industry evidence: practitioners repeatedly cannot audit because the attribute is not available to them, and in some domains they are legally required to collect it. The agentic twist that makes this a design pattern rather than a compliance note: an agent pipeline has many context-assembling stages (retrieval, tool returns, memory) that leak attributes into the decision path by accident, so 'the decision path cannot read it' has to be an enforced boundary rather than a policy.

evidence.title: "What We Can't Measure, We Can't Understand" (arXiv:2011.02282)
evidence.quote: Participants painted a complex picture of what demographic data availability and use look like on the ground, ranging from not having access to personal data of any kind to being legally required to collect and use demographic data for discrimination assessments.

evidence.title: Blind Justice: Fairness with Encrypted Sensitive Attributes (ICML 2018)
evidence.quote: By encrypting sensitive attributes, we show how an outcome-based fair model may be learned, checked, or have its outputs verified and held to account, without users revealing their sensitive attributes.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. pii-redaction (387) makes the opposite move — it detects and removes sensitive data from inputs and outputs, which is exactly what destroys the ability to audit; this pattern requires the attribute to be RETAINED and deliberately routed away from one consumer and towards another. sovereign-inference-stack (398) partitions by jurisdiction/residency, not by which consumer may read which field. provenance-ledger (153) logs decisions with no protected-attribute partition and no independent reader. Among wave-1 claims: predetermined-change-envelope pins the certified configuration but says nothing about where measurement data lives; principal-reason-code-binding produces a per-subject reason and is silent on population-level impact ratios; contestation-channel is a per-subject dispute route; oversight-as-legitimation is an anti-pattern about a reviewer who cannot detect errors. None of them address the architecture that makes impact measurable at all.

evidence.title: "What We Can't Measure, We Can't Understand": Challenges to Demographic Data Procurement in the Pursuit of Fairness
evidence.quote: As calls for fair and unbiased algorithmic systems increase, so too does the number of individuals working on algorithmic fairness in industry. However, these practitioners often do not have access to the demographic data they feel they need to detect bias in practice. Even with the growing variety of toolkits and strategies for working towards algorithmic fairness, they almost invariably require access to demographic attributes or proxies.

evidence.title: Blind Justice: Fairness with Encrypted Sensitive Attributes
evidence.quote: To avoid disparate treatment, sensitive attributes should not be considered. On the other hand, in order to avoid disparate impact, sensitive attributes must be examined, e.g., in order to learn a fair model, or to check if a given model is fair. We introduce methods from secure multi-party computation which allow us to avoid both.

candidates.name: Detector Score as Accusation
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: route a probabilistic per-person classifier's score — AI-authorship detection, academic-integrity flags, fraud or benefit-abuse screens — straight into an institutional adversarial process as the evidentiary basis for an allegation against a named individual. The base rate is low, the adjudicator has no artefact against which the claim can be checked, errors concentrate on an identifiable group, and the emission of the flag is itself the injury, because it lands on the person's record whether or not it is later upheld.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the education / academic-integrity seam. Liang et al. (published in Patterns, Cell Press, 2023) is the decisive source: it both measures the group-correlated false-positive concentration and states the operational conclusion — the authors explicitly 'caution against their use in evaluative or educational settings'. Weber-Wulff et al. (peer-reviewed, International Journal for Educational Integrity) independently corroborates across 14 tools including the two commercial systems universities actually deploy. HONEST CAVEAT, recorded so the curator can calibrate: an arXiv API query I ran also returned Al Ali, Helcl & Libovicky (arXiv:2602.05769, Feb 2026), which revisits the claim in Czech and reports no systematic bias against non-native speakers and that contemporary detectors no longer rely on perplexity — I did not open that abs page individually, and it is a genuine counterweight to the SPECIFIC non-native mechanism. It does not touch the structural core of the anti-pattern (a low-base-rate, ground-truth-free classification of a person that initiates a disciplinary process), which is why the candidate is framed on that shape rather than on the bias finding alone.

evidence.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers (arXiv:2304.02819; published in Patterns)
evidence.quote: Our results call for a broader conversation about the ethical implications of deploying ChatGPT content detectors and caution against their use in evaluative or educational settings, particularly when they may inadvertently penalize or exclude non-native English speakers from the global discourse.

evidence.title: Testing of Detection Tools for AI-Generated Text (arXiv:2306.15666)
evidence.quote: the available detection tools are neither accurate nor reliable and have a main bias towards classifying the output as human-written rather than detecting AI-generated text

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. false-confidence-syndrome (66) is about a model expressing uniform confidence in its OWN answers; here the output is a classification OF A THIRD PARTY and the harm is institutional rather than epistemic. hallucinated-citations (14) and verify-before-cite-gate (530) concern the agent's own assertions being checkable against a registry — the defining property here is that no registry exists: nobody can prove who wrote a piece of prose. Among wave-1 claims: oversight-as-legitimation is about a reviewer who cannot in practice detect the agent's errors, whereas this is the stronger case where review is impossible in principle because the ground truth is unobtainable; explanation-induced-overreliance concerns showing rationales to users; contestation-channel is the after-the-fact dispute route, which does not undo the harm of the flag existing. rubber-stamped-approval-gate is about pass-through rates on confirmations, not about a classification that starts a disciplinary process.

evidence.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
evidence.quote: Our findings reveal that these detectors consistently misclassify non-native English writing samples as AI-generated, whereas native writing samples are accurately identified. Furthermore, we demonstrate that simple prompting strategies can not only mitigate this bias but also effectively bypass GPT detectors, suggesting that GPT detectors may unintentionally penalize writers with constrained linguistic expressions.

evidence.title: Testing of Detection Tools for AI-Generated Text
evidence.quote: The research covers 12 publicly available tools and two commercial systems (Turnitin and PlagiarismCheck) that are widely used in the academic setting. The researchers conclude that the available detection tools are neither accurate nor reliable and have a main bias towards classifying the output as human-written rather than detecting AI-generated text.

candidates.name: Uncounted Field-Test Seeding
candidates.summary: When an agent generates the instrument that scores people — test items, rubric criteria, screening questions, structured-interview prompts — administer each generated instrument live, embedded among already-calibrated ones, but do not let it contribute to anyone's score until enough real responses have established its measurement properties (difficulty, discrimination, subgroup functioning, independence from neighbouring items). Promote an instrument to scored status on that evidence and retire it when the statistics drift.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the education / assessment seam (agent-authored assessment items and their validation). The two papers establish the recurring problem from opposite directions: Li et al. show that LLM-generated items are psychometrically sound ON AVERAGE but carry per-facet validity failures that only appear once real respondents answer them, and Huang et al. show that automatic item generation introduces construct-irrelevant local dependence that no amount of pre-hoc content review catches — both are defects invisible until the item meets a population. The force the pattern resolves is that generation is now cheap and calibration is not: the volume of generated instruments has outrun the response data needed to certify them, so the design question is how to obtain calibration data without letting an uncalibrated instrument affect a real person's score. The classical answer in high-stakes testing is embedded, unscored field-test items; the pattern lifts that into a general rule for any agent that authors a scoring instrument (LLM-generated eval rubrics, interview scorecards, screening questionnaires).

evidence.title: Automatic Item Generation for Personality Situational Judgment Tests with Large Language Models (arXiv:2412.12144)
evidence.quote: Personality assessment through situational judgment tests (SJTs) offers unique advantages over traditional Likert-type self-report scales, yet their development remains labor-intensive, time-consuming, and heavily dependent on subject matter experts.

evidence.quote: Psychometric validation indicates that LLM-derived metrics align more closely with indicators of construct-irrelevant local dependence and yield more coherent item parameter groupings than traditional text-based measures.

Here the generated artefact is deliberately shown to real people — that is the only way to obtain its response distribution — while being excluded from the consequential score, and there is no incumbent to compare against. silent-pilot-to-production-promotion (174) is the anti-pattern of an unmarked promotion; this names the mechanism that makes promotion earnable. eval-as-contract (147) and eval-harness (148) gate a RELEASE against a fixed suite; this gates a SINGLE GENERATED ARTEFACT's authority to score, one item at a time, continuously. Among wave-1 claims, chance-corrected-judge-validation validates a judge against human labels on a held-out meta-eval set — this validates each instrument against the live population's responses on properties (item difficulty, discrimination, differential item functioning) that no held-out human-labelled set can supply, because they are properties of the population-instrument interaction rather than of agreement with a human.

evidence.title: Automatic Item Generation for Personality Situational Judgment Tests with Large Language Models
evidence.quote: Study 3 evaluated the psychometric properties of LLM-generated SJTs covering five facets of the Big Five personality traits. evidence.title: A Dual-Dimensional LLM Framework for Automated Item Incidental Content Similarity Analysis in Large-Scale Assessments

candidates.name: Contestation Channel
candidates.summary: Ship every consequential agent decision with a working route to dispute it: a stable decision identifier handed to the affected person, the decision-time inputs, model version and applied rule preserved for exactly as long as the appeal window runs, a typed grounds-of-challenge intake, and routing to a human who actually holds authority to reverse. Resolves the force between shipping decisions at machine speed and owing the decision subject a real remedy rather than only a notification.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the government/public-sector seam. Contestability is a named design property with a decade of FAccT/CHI/CSCW literature behind it (Alfrink's CHI 2023 design study; Schmude et al. FAccT 2026 interview study; Balayn et al. CSCW'24 workshop on contestability along AI value chains) and it is now a regulatory requirement rather than a nicety — EU AI Act Art. 86 gives an affected person a right to an explanation of a high-risk decision, and the FAccT 2026 legal-accountability work explicitly frames its goal as making automated determinations 'traceable and contestable'. The catalog has plenty of operator-side oversight but no shape for the decision subject's side.

evidence.title: From Stem to Stern: Contestability Along AI Value Chains

evidence.title: A neuro-symbolic framework for accountability in public-sector AI

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. human-in-the-loop, approval-queue, two-human-touchpoints and cost-aware-action-delegation are all pre-action gates that operate on the operator's side of the decision; conversation-handoff escalates a live session to a human operator mid-conversation; decision-log and provenance-ledger persist reasoning for the operator's own post-hoc review; agent-decision-token mints a justification record but says nothing about who may invoke it or what it obliges the system to do. None of them give the person the decision was made about an addressable channel to challenge an already-issued decision, nor bind the system to keep alive the exact artifacts an adjudicator would need. agent-liability-insurance settles residual risk financially instead of opening a dispute route.

evidence.title: Two Means to an End Goal: Connecting Explainability and Contestability in the Regulation of Public Sector AI
evidence.quote: Explainability and its emerging counterpart contestability have become important normative and design principles for trustworthy AI as they enable users and subjects to understand and challenge AI decisions.

candidates.name: Statutory-Basis Verification
candidates.summary: Encode the governing statute or regulation as a formal rule set, require the agent to name the specific provision its decision rests on, and mechanically check that the justification it will hand the decision subject is entailed by that provision — rejecting explanations that are fluent and plausible but not legally authorised, even when the outcome itself happens to be correct.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the government service-delivery seam (benefits/tax/immigration). The CalFresh case study builds an ontology from California's Manual of Policies and Procedures, extracts statutory logic into a verifiable formal representation, and runs a solver over it to test whether a generated explanation aligns with governing law; case evaluations 'detect legally inconsistent explanations' and 'highlight violated eligibility rules'. Corroborated as a general public-sector gap by Rystrøm et al., who find no existing agent benchmark meets the legal and procedural criteria public institutions actually operate under.

evidence.quote: Case evaluations demonstrate the framework's ability to detect legally inconsistent explanations, highlight violated eligibility rules, and support procedural accountability by making the basis of automated determinations traceable and contestable.

evidence.title: Agent Benchmarks Fail Public Sector Requirements
evidence.quote: Deploying Large Language Model-based agents (LLM agents) in the public sector requires assuring that they meet the stringent legal, procedural, and structural requirements of public-sector institutions.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. formal-proof-compliance-gate proves the proposed *action* satisfies regulatory invariants before dispatch; this verifies the *stated reason* against the law that authorises the decision, and the two come apart — an eligibility denial can be substantively right while the reason given for it is not a ground the statute recognises, which is exactly what makes it reversible on appeal. agent-decision-token records 'the rule that fired' as an artifact but never checks that the fired rule is the one the statute prescribes. hallucinated-citations and citation-attribution bind claims to retrieved documents; here the target is a formal encoding of statutory conditions, not a source passage. policy-as-code-gate externalises operator policy authorship, not legislative authority. evidence.title: A neuro-symbolic framework for accountability in public-sector AI

candidates.name: Pre-Inference Jurisdiction Routing
candidates.summary: Run a small deterministic classifier over the raw request before any model call, derive its legal-sensitivity and residency class, and bind the request to a model endpoint in the jurisdiction lawfully allowed to see it — so a residency or cross-border breach is structurally unreachable rather than detected after the tokens have already left. Resolves the force between wanting frontier capability for ordinary traffic and being legally unable to let regulated content cross a border at all.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the 2026 regulatory-frontier seam (residency and cross-border transfer rules landing in the EU, plus divergent national regimes). The paper names the failure precisely: 'Personally identifiable information (PII) in user queries can reach model endpoints before the system determines whether that data should leave its jurisdictional boundary.' It also rules out the obvious architectural near-miss — Mixture-of-Experts routing does not help because 'this routing occurs between expert layers within the model after data has already arrived at the endpoint'. Reported overhead is 7ms at 99.2% classifier accuracy, so the gate is cheap enough to sit on every request.

evidence.title: ComplianceGate: Classifier-Gated Multi-Tier LLM Routing for Inference in Regulated Industries
evidence.quote: Personally identifiable information (PII) in user queries can reach model endpoints before the system determines whether that data should leave its jurisdictional boundary.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. sovereign-inference-stack (alias 'Data-Residency Agent Architecture') resolves the same regulatory force by moving the *entire* stack inside one boundary — it is architectural and all-or-nothing, and gives up hosted frontier capability for every request. This pattern keeps a hybrid, multi-jurisdiction fleet legal by making the routing key the request's legal sensitivity, evaluated before inference. open-weight-cascade routes by difficulty and escalates *across* the boundary, which is precisely the move a residency rule forbids. complexity-based-routing and multi-model-routing use difficulty or cost as the key and have no notion of a lawful destination. pii-redaction strips identifiers from a request that is still going wherever it was already going. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: ComplianceGate: Classifier-Gated Multi-Tier LLM Routing for Inference in Regulated Industries
evidence.quote: A trained encoder classifier sits before any decoder inference, evaluating each query for complexity and data sensitivity, then routing it to an appropriately sized dense model in the appropriate geographic location. PII-containing queries route to local endpoints before any LLM computation begins, making data residency violations structurally impossible.

candidates.name: Oversight as Legitimation
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: satisfy a statutory human-oversight requirement by designating a reviewer who cannot in practice detect the agent's errors — no counterfactual, no time, no authority, no incentive to dissent — so the sign-off supplies the legal cover that makes an unfit system deployable and relocates blame onto the reviewer, while not a single outcome changes.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the administrative-law seam. Green's survey is peer-reviewed (Computer Law & Security Review 45, 2022) and covers 41 real oversight policies, so this is a recurring institutional shape, not one deployment's gripe. Its force sharpens under the EU AI Act's Article 14 human-oversight duty, which lands as a hard obligation on high-risk systems in 2026: the duty is discharged by assigning a person, and the paper's finding is that assignment alone 'provide[s] a false sense of security in adopting algorithms and enable[s] vendors and agencies to shirk accountability for algorithmic harms'. Green's proposed remedy — institutional rather than individual oversight — is what a catalog entry would point implementers toward.

evidence.title: The Flaws of Policies Requiring Human Oversight of Government Algorithms
evidence.quote: Thus, rather than protect against the potential harms of algorithmic decision-making in government, human oversight policies provide a false sense of security in adopting algorithms and enable vendors and agencies to shirk accountability for algorithmic harms. In light of these flaws, I propose a shift from human oversight to institutional oversight as the central mechanism for regulating government algorithms.

evidence.title: Agent Benchmarks Fail Public Sector Requirements
evidence.quote: no single benchmark meets all of the criteria

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. accountability-laundering-via-algorithm is the mirror failure — a decision routed through an agent so that *no* person owns it; here a person is deliberately named as owner and the naming is the whole problem. agent-output-alert-fatigue is volume-driven desensitisation of reviewers over time; supervisor-cognitive-overload is attention saturation across parallel sub-agents; advisory-to-mandate-escalation is an advisory output being institutionally promoted to a binding order and dissent reframed as insubordination. None of them name the legitimating mechanism: the oversight mandate is what lets the system through the gate, and its ineffectiveness is invisible precisely because the mandate was met. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: The Flaws of Policies Requiring Human Oversight of Government Algorithms
evidence.quote: In this article, I survey 41 policies that prescribe human oversight of government algorithms and find that they suffer from two significant flaws. First, evidence suggests that people are unable to perform the desired oversight functions. Second, as a result of the first flaw, human oversight policies legitimize government uses of faulty and controversial algorithms without addressing the fundamental issues with these tools.

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the vertical-legal-hr-edu scout. New vertical (legal practice) for an already-claimed candidate. Magesh, Surani, Dahl, Suzgun, Manning & Ho (arXiv:2405.20362) is the strongest empirical case yet for oversight-as-legitimation: the designated overseer is an admitted attorney who bears personal Rule-11-style responsibility, the vendors marketed the tools as hallucination-free, and the preregistered study found the two market-leading products 'hallucinate between 17% and 33% of the time'. The overseer is therefore nominally in control while being given a system whose error rate is both high and invisible without re-checking every citation by hand — precisely the shape the anti-pattern names. Dahl et al. (Journal of Legal Analysis, peer-reviewed) supplies the mechanism that defeats the overseer's sampling heuristic: the model's self-assessment does not track when it is wrong, so an overseer who spot-checks the answers that look shaky is checking the wrong ones. Its concluding line in the fetched abstract is quoted above.

evidence.title: Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools
evidence.quote: Recently, certain legal research providers have touted methods such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as "eliminating" (Casetext, 2023) or "avoid[ing]" hallucinations (Thomson Reuters, 2023), or guaranteeing "hallucination-free" legal citations (LexisNexis, 2023). Because of the closed nature of these systems, systematically assessing these claims is challenging.

evidence.title: Large Legal Fictions: Profiling Legal Hallucinations in Large Language Models (Journal of Legal Analysis 16(1), 2024)
evidence.quote: LLMs cannot always predict, or do not always know, when they are producing legal hallucinations.

candidates.name: Air-Gap Omission Drift

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the defense / classified-deployment seam. The paper's population is exactly the regulated set — organizations that cannot send tokens to frontier APIs, naming hospitals with patient records, law firms with privileged discovery, and national agencies handling classified material. It supplies a nine-layer (L0–L8) attribution taxonomy separating deterministic software loss from behavioural non-retrieval, and reports that injected deterministic faults at the lowest layers dominate weighted loss — which is the actionable claim: the omission is mostly plumbing, not the model, so debugging it as a model problem is wasted effort.

evidence.title: Where Facts Go Missing: A Layerwise Taxonomy and Per-Layer Attribution of Information Omission in Air-Gapped LLM Agent Pipelines
evidence.quote: deterministic software loss from behavioral non-retrieval

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. silent-source-rot is an *external* source changing structure so a wrapper returns valid-but-empty results; tool-output-trusted-verbatim is failing to validate what a tool returns; errors-swept-under-the-rug is deliberately scrubbing failures out of the agent's own context; context-compaction and context-window-packing drop material knowingly, under a declared budget. Here the loss is produced by the very layers that were added to make the deployment lawful — the boundary you cannot remove — it is deterministic rather than model-behavioural for the majority of the loss, and neither the agent nor the operator can see it, because the pipeline reports success at every hop. evidence.title: Where Facts Go Missing: A Layerwise Taxonomy and Per-Layer Attribution of Information Omission in Air-Gapped LLM Agent Pipelines
evidence.quote: Air-gapped and on-premises language-model agents can silently omit decision-critical facts at any boundary between source ingestion and final answer generation.

candidates.name: Administrative Burden Transfer

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the government service-delivery seam (SNAP / benefits intake). FAccT 2025 interview study with applicants to a programme serving 41 million people, so the population is large and the shape recurs across intake systems rather than one product. candidates.name: Control-Quality Metering

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the defense / human-on-the-loop-doctrine seam. Sahoo supplies the named mechanism (Control Quality Score) and the graduated-response shape; Green supplies the empirical reason it is needed — oversight assignments are not self-validating, because people demonstrably cannot perform the function they are assigned. The pairing is what makes this a pattern rather than a metric: the measurement exists to close a loop that today is left open by assumption. Flagged medium because the descend-on-signal half of the shape overlaps velocity-magnitude-governor; the defensible novelty is that the instrumented subject is the human, not the agent.

evidence.title: The Controllability Trap: A Governance Framework for Military AI Agents

evidence.title: The Controllability Trap: A Governance Framework for Military AI Agents
evidence.quote: We identify six agentic governance failures tied to these capabilities and show how they erode meaningful human control in military settings. We propose the Agentic Military AI Governance Framework (AMAGF), a measurable architecture structured around three pillars: Preventive Governance (reducing failure likelihood), Detective Governance (real-time detection of control degradation), and Corrective Governance (restoring or safely degrading operations). Its core mechanism, the Control Quality Score (CQS), is a composite real-time metric quantifying human control and enabling graduated responses as control weakens.

evidence.title: The Flaws of Policies Requiring Human Oversight of Government Algorithms
evidence.quote: First, evidence suggests that people are unable to perform the desired oversight functions.

candidates.name: Prior-Art Novelty Gate
candidates.summary: Before an agent-proposed hypothesis, experiment or research idea is allowed to consume scarce resources (instrument time, reagents, a compute run, a human reviewer), resolve it against an external prior-work index — literature APIs, patent or trial registries, the lab's own notebook — and reject, re-scope or re-rank anything already answered. Resolves the force that generative research agents produce plausible-sounding proposals far faster than anyone can check them, and cannot reliably judge their own novelty.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the scientific-research-agent vertical (self-driving labs, automated discovery pipelines). The shape appears as an explicit architectural stage in shipped research agents: The AI Scientist wires a literature API in as a novelty filter between ideation and execution. Si et al. supply the force — LLM self-evaluation of novelty fails, so the check has to be externalised — and the AI Scientist cost figure ($15/paper) supplies the volume pressure that makes an automatic gate necessary rather than a human review step.

candidates.name: Negative-Result Ledger
candidates.summary: Convert every methodologically valid failure — a synthesis that did not yield, a configuration that diverged, a route that dead-ended — into a bounded, typed record in a shared bank, and require the next planning step to explicitly adopt or reject the relevant records before proposing an action. Resolves the force that failures are the majority of an experimental agent's output yet are the part that is never written down, so the same dead ends are re-entered and the surrounding models never learn the shape of the failure region.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the self-driving-lab vertical. Seifrid et al. (Accounts of Chemical Research, peer-reviewed) establish the recurring problem in wet-lab automation — failed runs are the data nobody keeps, and their absence is what breaks the downstream models. Wang (2026) gives the mechanism a concrete agent-architecture shape (curator agent, typed record bank, explicit adopt/reject before the next proposal) and reports it beating vanilla AutoResearch baselines at lower token cost. Two independent domains (autonomous chemistry, automated ML research) reaching the same shape is what lifts this above a single framework's feature.

evidence.title: Autonomous Chemical Experiments: Challenges and Perspectives on Establishing a Self-Driving Lab
evidence.quote: They can increase reproducibility as they eliminate human error and maintain better records of 'failed' experiments.

evidence.title: Negative Knowledge as Failure-aware Shared Memory for AutoResearch
evidence.quote: AI-assisted research systems generate many failed attempts, but those failures rarely become a durable, shared knowledge asset.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. hypothesis-tracking stores the agent's live provisional answers with confidence and next-test; this stores settled negative outcomes as reusable constraints on the search space, and the consumer is the planner rather than the agent's own belief state. open-question-tension-store stores what is still unanswered, not what has been answered in the negative. re-proposing-rejected-decisions is the anti-pattern form of the gap but scoped to design decisions visible in a codebase's history; this is about empirical experimental outcomes that were never recorded anywhere at all. provenance-ledger and lineage-tracking log what happened for audit and reversal; they are not consulted as constraints by the next plan and carry no adopt/reject adjudication step.

evidence.quote: the current endemic publication bias is detrimental to ML approaches as 'negative' results are as important as 'positive' ones for training models.

evidence.title: Negative Knowledge as Failure-aware Shared Memory for AutoResearch
evidence.quote: We propose a negative knowledge memory layer: a curator agent converts each failed attempt into a bounded, typed record in a shared bank, and a downstream research agent explicitly adopts or rejects those records before proposing its next experiment.

candidates.name: De-Novo Artefact Hazard Screen
candidates.summary: When an agent designs an artefact whose danger is a property of the artefact itself — a molecule, a nucleic acid sequence, a formulation, a protocol — gate every downstream actuation on a hazard screen run over the artefact's own structure, combining a canonicalised-identifier lookup against controlled-substance registries with a property-based hazard model, and abort on a hit rather than asking the model to reconsider. Resolves the force that a generative search deliberately produces artefacts that are not on any list, so registry lookup alone is necessary but structurally insufficient.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the self-driving-lab / autonomous-chemistry vertical. Urbina et al. is the canonical computational proof that inverting a generative discovery model yields hazardous artefacts at scale, including compounds absent from any control list — which is precisely why a list lookup is not a sufficient gate and a structural hazard model is required. ChemSafetyBench (peer-reviewed benchmark) shows models still emit unsafe chemistry responses after safety training, so the screen has to sit outside the model. ChemCrow is the shipped instance: a chemistry agent that autonomously plans and executes syntheses, i.e. an agent that actuates on its own designs.

evidence.title: Dual use of artificial-intelligence-powered drug discovery (Nature Machine Intelligence 4, 189-191)
evidence.quote: By inverting the use of our machine learning models, we had transformed our innocuous generative model from a helpful tool of medicine to a generator of likely deadly molecules.

evidence.title: ChemCrow: Augmenting large-language models with chemistry tools
evidence.quote: Our agent autonomously planned and executed the syntheses of an insect repellent, three organocatalysts, and guided the discovery of a novel chromophore.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. mandatory-red-flag-escalation triggers on a deterministic set of high-risk features of the incoming REQUEST and hands off to a human; here the trigger is a computed property of the agent's OWN generated output, the artefact may be entirely novel, and the correct response is to abort before physical actuation rather than to escalate a conversation. input-output-guardrails filters text against content policy; a hazard model over a molecular graph or a sequence is not a text classifier and cannot be expressed as one. simulate-before-actuate predicts the effect of an ACTION on the environment and requires the predicted deltas to match; this screens the intrinsic hazard of the OBJECT regardless of the action taken with it. canonical-entity-grounding resolves business identifiers against master data for correctness; here canonicalisation exists only to defeat synonym and alternate-nomenclature evasion feeding the hazard check. scope-of-practice-gate blocks licence-gated professional activity, which is about who may act, not about what was designed.

evidence.title: Dual use of artificial-intelligence-powered drug discovery
evidence.quote: In less than 6 hours after starting on our in-house server, our model generated forty thousand molecules that scored within our desired threshold.

evidence.title: ChemSafetyBench: Benchmarking LLM Safety on Chemistry Domain
evidence.quote: Despite their impressive abilities, these models can pose significant risks when generating responses related to hazardous or harmful topics, even after safety training.

candidates.name: Canon Consistency Gate
candidates.summary: Maintain the established facts and outstanding commitments of a long-running agent-driven world as an explicit structured specification, and check each candidate output against it for contradiction before the output is emitted, rejecting and regenerating on conflict. Resolves the force that in NPC dialogue, live-ops storylines and other multi-session fiction the constraint set is not authored up front but accumulates from the agent's own prior turns and the player's actions, while users actively push the agent toward contradicting it.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the games / interactive-media vertical. Ma et al. (accepted at ICML 2026) name the problem Narrative Commitment Preservation and build the mechanism the pattern describes — a structured narrative specification of trajectory, commitments and initial facts that can be automatically checked throughout the interaction — then show every current model fails it badly under adversarial player pressure. Abdulhai et al. independently report the same contradiction-of-earlier-statements failure in non-game long-horizon role-play (therapy, education, social simulation), which is what makes this a recurring shape rather than a game-engine quirk.

evidence.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
evidence.quote: Each environment includes a structured narrative specification (trajectory, commitments, and initial facts) that we can automatically check throughout the interaction between the player agent and the narrator agent.

evidence.title: Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. constitutional-charter is a fixed, author-written rule set the agent re-reads and cannot modify; here the constraint set is generated during play, grows every turn, and the test is contradiction against accumulated facts rather than compliance with stated rules. commitment-tracking audits whether a stated intent was followed through (open/followed/expired); this blocks emission of content that conflicts with an established world fact, which is a consistency test rather than a follow-through test. agent-persona-profile is a static identity configuration object; it does not accumulate world state or gate output. degenerate-output-detection catches near-duplicates of the agent's own recent output; the failure here is the opposite — fluent, novel, high-quality text that happens to contradict turn 14. hypothesis-tracking holds provisional beliefs that are supposed to change; canon is precisely the set that must not.

evidence.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
evidence.quote: Experiments across state-of-the-art LLMs reveal a substantial long-horizon consistency gap: high linguistic quality does not guarantee commitment preservation; even strong models frequently generate logically conflicting content under adversarial interventions, with the best-performing model (GPT-5.2) achieving only 42% survival rate after 20 turns, fact conflict rates ranging from 40% to 68% across models

evidence.title: Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
evidence.quote: While these simulations enable scalable training and evaluation of AI agents, off-the-shelf LLMs often drift from their assigned personas, contradict earlier statements, or abandon role-appropriate behavior.

candidates.name: License Envelope Propagation
candidates.summary: Attach machine-readable licence terms to every asset an agent ingests, propagate the most restrictive combination of those terms to each artefact the agent composes, and gate publication on whether the resulting envelope permits the intended use. Resolves the force that licence terms do not survive aggregation — the composed artefact looks clean while the rights that governed its inputs have silently been lost, and nobody discovers this until the output ships.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the media-production / marketing-content vertical, where an agent composes a deliverable out of stock footage, fonts, sampled audio, model-generated frames and third-party brand assets. Longpre et al. is the direct empirical measurement of the mechanism: when assets flow through aggregation and re-hosting, licence metadata is omitted 70%+ of the time and wrong 50%+ of the time — so composition, not authoring, is where rights are lost. Caveat for the authoring step: that measurement is on text training datasets rather than on media assets, and the pattern generalises the mechanism rather than citing a media-pipeline study. Henderson et al. supplies the downstream consequence — the composed output itself can fall outside fair use, so the envelope must be evaluated at publication time, not only at ingestion.

evidence.title: The Data Provenance Initiative: A Large Scale Audit of Dataset Licensing & Attribution in AI
evidence.quote: We develop tools and standards to trace the lineage of these datasets, from their source, creators, series of license conditions, properties, and subsequent use.

evidence.title: Foundation Models and Fair Use
evidence.quote: we emphasize that fair use is not guaranteed, and additional work may be necessary to keep model development and deployment squarely in the realm of fair use.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. lineage-tracking records which prompt version, model version and data sources produced an output, for debugging and audit; it carries no legal terms and performs no combination, so it can tell you where a frame came from but not whether you may broadcast it. provenance-ledger logs decisions and state changes for explanation and reversal. deontic-token-delegation reifies obligations and permissions about ACTING and passes them between agents along a delegation chain; this attaches rights to CONTENT and combines them by a most-restrictive lattice, and the holder of the obligation is the publisher rather than a downstream agent. two-human-touchpoints places human review at selection and publication but does not model the rights themselves.

evidence.title: The Data Provenance Initiative: A Large Scale Audit of Dataset Licensing & Attribution in AI (published as 'A large-scale audit of dataset licensing and attribution in AI', Nature Machine Intelligence, 2024)
evidence.quote: We also observe frequent miscategorization of licenses on widely used dataset hosting sites, with license omission of 70%+ and error rates of 50%+. This points to a crisis in misattribution and informed use of the most popular datasets driving many recent breakthroughs.

evidence.title: Foundation Models and Fair Use
evidence.quote: If the model produces output that is similar to copyrighted data, particularly in scenarios that affect the market of that data, fair use may no longer apply to the output of the model.

candidates.name: Affine Budget Delegation
candidates.summary: Model an agent's spend allowance as an owned, non-copyable resource that is split and moved on delegation: handing a sub-agent a budget transfers ownership of that slice, the parent cannot spend what it gave away, and the sum of all children's budgets is bounded by the parent's. Resolves the tension between letting sub-agents decide their own spend autonomously and keeping one hard ceiling over a concurrent fan-out, where a budget passed by value is silently duplicated so N branches each draw the full cap.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the war-story seam (runaway agent spend post-mortems, 2026). The recurring operator story is 'a multi-agent fan-out blew through a cap we thought we had set'. The grounding paper is itself a cross-product incident catalog: 63 confirmed production incidents across 21 orchestration frameworks 2023-2026, of which the M-delegation-fanout cluster (11 rows / 6 frameworks) is exactly this shape — the budget is a copyable number, so each concurrent delegate reserves against the same balance. The catalog's existing cost controls all sit at the wrong granularity for it.

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents, with an Affine-Typed Rust Mitigation as a Case Study (HTML, taxonomy section)
evidence.quote: the M-delegation-fanout race documented in 11 catalog incidents is rejected by the borrow checker at compile time, while the same pattern under asyncio overshoots 30/30

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents (abstract)
evidence.quote: LLM-agent budget overruns are a documented production failure class: a single retry loop can spend thousands of dollars before an operator notices, and the in-process integrity properties that would prevent it (no aliasing, no double-spend, no use-after-delegation of a cost-bearing value) are enforced, if at all, by ad-hoc wrappers rather than by the type system.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. step-budget caps loop iterations per request, not a fungible consumable, and is silent about delegation. cost-gating blocks one action above a threshold; it does not stop N children each passing that same threshold concurrently. token-economy-blindness is the anti-pattern of having no per-run cap at all — here the cap exists but is aliased across the fan-out. session-scoped-payment-authorization bounds a commerce payment session's total spend, not the propagation of an internal compute budget down a delegation tree. rate-limiting is a per-window request throttle, not an ownership discipline. deontic-token-delegation transfers permissions/obligations with provenance, but a permission is not depleted by exercising it — the failure named here is double-spend of a consumable quantity, not ambiguity about who is allowed to act. unbounded-subagent-spawn caps how many children exist, not how much each may spend. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents, with an Affine-Typed Rust Mitigation as a Case Study
evidence.quote: the delegation-fanout race documented in 11 incidents is rejected by the borrow checker at compile time, while the same pattern under asyncio overshoots 30/30 and three disciplined alternatives overshoot 0/30

evidence.title: Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents (empirical catalog section)
evidence.quote: a catalog of 63 confirmed production incidents from 21 orchestration frameworks (2023-2026), each backed by a quoted GitHub issue and, where reported, a dollar loss, organized into an eight-cluster failure taxonomy (inter-rater Cohen's kappa = 0.837, N = 113)

candidates.name: Residual-Complexity Concentration
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: let the agent absorb the routine majority of a work queue while sizing the remaining human tier — headcount, handle-time targets, skill mix, training pipeline — on the old mixed difficulty distribution. The humans are then left with a stream that is almost entirely hard, ambiguous, high-context, emotionally loaded cases, so per-case handle time, error rate, escalation depth and attrition all rise even though total volume fell, and the easy cases that used to build and maintain competence are gone.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the war-story seam (2026 agent de-adoption and support-deflection retrospectives). Bainbridge 1983 (Automatica 19(6):775-779, DOI 10.1016/0005-1098(83)90046-8) is the canonical peer-reviewed statement of the mechanism and I read the full PDF, not a summary. The 2026 corroboration is the CX side: tier-1 deflection concentrates on routine intents, so the human tier is left with 'fewer but harder interactions' while headcount was cut against the old average. The catalog currently has no entry for the difficulty-distribution shift of the residual human queue.

evidence.title: Customer Support Ticket Volume: 17-25/Agent Daily | Stealth Agents (2026-06-07)
evidence.quote: agents field fewer but harder interactions

evidence.title: Why three-quarters of enterprises have rolled back AI agents — CX Dive, Kristen Doerer, 2026-05-27
evidence.quote: customer data exposure as the leading cause

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. agentic-skill-atrophy is about an individual losing implicit knowledge because the agent makes routine decisions for them; this is about the composition of the remaining queue and the staffing/economic model built on the pre-automation average. supervisor-cognitive-overload is a human steering many parallel sub-agents; here the human is not supervising the agent at all — they are doing original work the agent could not do. hidden-validation-work-amplification is effort shifting from doing to validating agent output; the residual work here was never agent output. understanding-capacity-gap is a team outrunning its own capacity to verify generated artefacts. conflict-competency-gap is about an agent's inability to handle conflict. agent-withdrawal-criteria is a governance remedy for de-adoption, not this failure mode. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Ironies of Automation
evidence.quote: By taking away the easy parts of his task, automation can make the difficult parts of the human operator's task more difficult.

evidence.title: Ironies of Automation (Automatica 19(6), 775-779), Section 1 Introduction
evidence.quote: The second irony is that the designer who tries to eliminate the operator still leaves the operator to do the tasks which the designer cannot think how to automate. It is this approach which causes the problems to be discussed here, as it means that the operator can be left with an arbitrary collection of tasks, and little thought may have been given to providing support for them.

candidates.name: Rubber-Stamped Approval Gate
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: treat the existence of a per-action human confirmation prompt as an actual control, without ever measuring its pass-through rate. Under a stream of frequent, low-context, truncated or indirection-obscured prompts the operator approves almost everything — including actions outside the request they originally made — so the gate emits an audit trail of approvals while filtering nothing.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the war-story seam (August 2026 coding-agent incident cluster). Yan 2026 (arXiv 2608.27443, 27 Aug 2026 — after the catalog's 2026-07-16 scan) is the direct measurement: 113 participants, 18 simulated actions including 7 designed overreaches, and the great majority of executed overreach actions went through *after* a human approved them; users overwhelmingly chose 'ask' over a standing policy and then approved anyway. Goddard et al. (JAMIA 2012) supply the mechanism — automation bias — with a meta-analysis of clinical decision support showing a 26% relative increase in incorrect decisions when the advice was wrong. The 2026 operator reports add the interface half: approval surfaces that truncate long commands off-screen, and prompts that display a symlink's apparent target rather than the real write target, so 'what was approved' and 'what executed' diverge.

evidence.title: Six AI Coding Agent Incidents in One Month: A Containment Checklist for Tech Leads (August 2026)
evidence.quote: collapsing two different trust levels into one approval step: read vs. write, workspace-local vs. external-facing, routine vs. destructive

evidence.title: Do User-Authored Permission Policies Improve Protection Against AI Agent Overreach? (abstract)
evidence.quote: We examine a mechanism in which a language model maps actions to plain-language consequence categories with user-authored "allow", "ask", or "never" rules.

evidence.title: Ten AI Agents Destroyed Production. Zero Postmortems. — Harper Foley, 2026-03-08
evidence.quote: No vendor postmortems. Despite incidents hitting Hacker News front pages, Fortune, Tom's Hardware, and multiple tech outlets, no AI coding tool vendor has published a detailed post-incident review for any of these events.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. human-in-the-loop is the positive pattern this is the degenerate implementation of: it prescribes approval points but neither names the pass-through failure nor requires the approval rate to be instrumented. agent-output-alert-fatigue is the opposite direction — an agent's high-volume, low-precision *findings* desensitise reviewers until they MUTE the agent; here the human keeps answering the prompts and keeps saying yes to *action requests*. supervisor-cognitive-overload is attention saturation from having to steer many parallel sub-agents, not wholesale approval of a single sequential prompt stream. blanket-authorization-accountability-rupture is one broad standing grant with no per-action prompts at all; here there are many prompts, all answered yes. refund-threshold-drift is the cap itself creeping upward; here the cap holds but the gate over it does not bind. two-human-touchpoints, risk-tiered-action-autonomy and sync-execution-plan-confirmation are prescriptions, not the failure.

evidence.title: Do User-Authored Permission Policies Improve Protection Against AI Agent Overreach?
evidence.quote: many actions outside users' original requests went through after users approved them

evidence.title: Automation bias: a systematic review of frequency, effect mediators, and mitigators
evidence.quote: as a heuristic replacement of vigilant information seeking and processing

raised_by.note: Cross-seam corroboration from the org-process scout. Both are direct evidence for the wave1 claim that an approval artifact's existence is not a control. Farrag supplies the vendor-documented case (one provider ships an agent that approves pull requests below a configured risk threshold and can dismiss reviews) and the mechanism — the pass-through is now a product property, not a human habit. Ye et al. supply the measured pass-through rate under realistic conditions: 100+ participants, ~5h task, 94% miss rate, and 56% still accept after an explicit monitor warning. That second number is the strongest available evidence that adding a warning surface does not convert a rubber-stamp into a control.

evidence.title: Where Accountability Lives: Mapping Human Responsibility to Workflow Artifacts in Agentic Software Development
evidence.quote: A decade of code-review research already recorded that the approval artifact carries less than the terms assume. What changes is that this weakness moved from a property of how people work to a property of what a product does: a vendor now documents a product that stands at the approval event and emits the same artifact with no party capable of forming a judgement present.

evidence.title: Coding with "Enemy": Can Human Developers Detect AI Agent Sabotage?
evidence.quote: We find that 94% of developers fail to detect sabotage, and our analysis of participant feedback attributes this vulnerability to minimal code review, plausible cover story, and overtrust in agents. We further test the effectiveness of a safety monitor in one condition: while the monitor reduces sabotage success, 56% of participants still accept the malicious code, ignoring its warnings.

candidates.name: Operator as Moral Crumple Zone
candidates.summary: Anti-pattern: respond to an agent-caused incident by inserting a human sign-off at the end of the agent pipeline and declaring the accountability problem solved. The named reviewer inherits liability for outputs they have neither the time, the context, nor the practical authority to refuse, so the organisation acquires a blame sink rather than a control — and the underlying system keeps its capabilities, its throughput and its failure modes.

raised_by.note: Surfaced via the war-story seam: Amazon's March 2026 storefront outages. Amazon's own account placed the cause on an engineer acting on advice an agent had inferred from a stale internal wiki, and the post-incident remedy was to require senior-engineer review of AI-assisted changes authored by junior staff — i.e. a human review layer added after the fact, at the point where blame lands rather than where control lives. One operator write-up names the loop explicitly. The peer-reviewed grounding is Hu & Rong 2026, who take Elish's 'moral crumple zone' (Elish, Engaging Science, Technology and Society 5:40-60, 2019 — cited via Hu & Rong, which I opened; I did not fetch Elish directly) and show why an agent-principal dyad without consequence-agency coupling systematically puts the pain on the human.

evidence.title: Amazon puts humans further back in the loop as its retail website crashes from 'inaccurate advice' that an AI agent took from an old wiki — Fortune, Eva Roytburg, 2026-03-12
evidence.quote: an engineer following inaccurate advice that an agent inferred from an outdated internal wiki

evidence.title: Governing AI Agents: What the Amazon Outage Reveals about Enterprise Risk — Wharton Accountable AI Lab, Jon Iwry, 2026-04-14
evidence.quote: The company introduced additional senior-engineer reviews for AI-assisted changes and renewed its emphasis on human oversight

evidence.title: Amazon's AI Outages Escalated. So Did the Denial. — paddo.dev, 2026-03-12
evidence.quote: Ship the capability. Mandate adoption. Discover the failure mode in production. Add the guardrail. Blame the human.

raised_by.note: Scientific grounding. accountability-laundering-via-algorithm is the opposite direction — a decision is routed through the agent so that NO person owns the outcome; here a specific, usually junior, human is made to own it. blanket-authorization-accountability-rupture describes a broad standing grant after which no party retains accountability; here accountability is concentrated on the least-empowered party. rubber-stamped-approval-gate names why such a gate does not filter (measured approval pass-through, automation bias); this names what the gate is FOR organisationally and the liability it relocates — the two compose, mechanism and governance consequence. agent-liability-insurance transfers residual risk to an insurer (a remedy, not the failure). silent-pilot-to-production-promotion is about scope creep under a 'pilot' label. hidden-validation-work-amplification is about net productivity, not liability allocation. [CURATOR NOTE: single unique scientific source — needs a second reference or an explicit single-source caveat before authoring.]

evidence.title: Some[Body] Must Receive That Pain for Agent Accountability
evidence.quote: The thin-identity agent-principal dyad has a body but no consequence–agency coupling: the human bears pain for behaviors beyond their control -- Elish's moral crumple zone.

evidence.title: Some[Body] Must Receive That Pain for Agent Accountability (prescription)
evidence.quote: Until such architectures exist, high-stakes AI deployment should remain tethered to accountable human principals with meaningful control, proportional liability, and authority to constrain or terminate the agent.
